Rclone - syncs your files to cloud storage 

<h2>Description</h2><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>About rclone
<dt>&bull;
<dd>What can rclone do for you?
<dt>&bull;
<dd>What features does rclone have?
<dt>&bull;
<dd>What providers does rclone support?
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Download (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/downloads/)">https://rclone.org/downloads/)</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Install (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/install/)">https://rclone.org/install/)</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Donate. (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/donate/)">https://rclone.org/donate/)</a></dl><h3>About rclone</h3>Rclone is a command line program to manage files on cloud storage. It is a feature rich alternative to cloud vendors' web storage interfaces. Over 40 cloud storage products support rclone including S3 object stores, business &amp; consumer file storage services, as well as standard transfer protocols. 

 Rclone has powerful cloud equivalents to the unix commands rsync, cp, mv, mount, ls, ncdu, tree, rm, and cat. Rclone's familiar syntax includes shell pipeline support, and --dry-run protection. It is used at the command line, in scripts or via its API. 

 Users call rclone "The Swiss army knife of cloud storage", and "Technology indistinguishable from magic". 

 Rclone really looks after your data. It preserves timestamps and verifies checksums at all times. Transfers over limited bandwidth; intermittent connections, or subject to quota can be restarted, from the last good file transferred. You can check (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/)</a> the integrity of your files. Where possible, rclone employs server side transfers to minimise local bandwidth use and transfers from one provider to another without using local disk. 

 Virtual backends wrap local and cloud file systems to apply encryption (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/crypt/">https://rclone.org/crypt/</a>), caching (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/cache/">https://rclone.org/cache/</a>), chunking (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/chunker/)">https://rclone.org/chunker/)</a> and joining (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/union/">https://rclone.org/union/</a>). 

 Rclone mounts (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mount/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mount/)</a> any local, cloud or virtual filesystem as a disk on Windows, macOS, linux and FreeBSD, and also serves these over SFTP (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_sftp/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_sftp/</a>), HTTP (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_http/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_http/</a>), WebDAV (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_webdav/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_webdav/</a>), FTP (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_ftp/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_ftp/)</a> and DLNA (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_dlna/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_dlna/</a>). 

 Rclone is mature, open source software originally inspired by rsync and written in Go (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://golang.org">https://golang.org</a>). The friendly support community are familiar with varied use cases. Official Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Brew and Chocolatey repos. include rclone. For the latest version downloading from rclone.org (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/downloads/)">https://rclone.org/downloads/)</a> is recommended. 

 Rclone is widely used on Linux, Windows and Mac. Third party developers create innovative backup, restore, GUI and business process solutions using the rclone command line or API. 

 Rclone does the heavy lifting of communicating with cloud storage.
<h3>What can rclone do for you?</h3>Rclone helps you:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Backup (and encrypt) files to cloud storage
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Restore (and decrypt) files from cloud storage
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Mirror cloud data to other cloud services or locally
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Migrate data to cloud, or between cloud storage vendors
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Mount multiple, encrypted, cached or diverse cloud storage as a disk
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Analyse and account for data held on cloud storage using lsf (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_lsf/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_lsf/</a>), ljson (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_lsjson/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_lsjson/</a>), size (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_size/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_size/</a>), ncdu (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_ncdu/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_ncdu/)</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Union (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/union/)">https://rclone.org/union/)</a> file systems together to present multiple local and/or cloud file systems as one</dl><h3>Features</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Transfers
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>MD5, SHA1 hashes are checked at all times for file integrity
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Timestamps are preserved on files
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Operations can be restarted at any time
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Can be to and from network, eg two different cloud providers
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Can use multi-threaded downloads to local disk</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>Copy (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/)</a> new or changed files to cloud storage
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Sync (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/)</a> (one way) to make a directory identical
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Move (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_move/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_move/)</a> files to cloud storage deleting the local after verification
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Check (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/)</a> hashes and for missing/extra files
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Mount (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mount/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mount/)</a> your cloud storage as a network disk
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Serve (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve/)</a> local or remote files over HTTP (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_http/)/WebDav">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_http/)/WebDav</a> (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_webdav/)/FTP">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_webdav/)/FTP</a> (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_ftp/)/SFTP">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_ftp/)/SFTP</a> (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_sftp/)/dlna">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_sftp/)/dlna</a> (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_dlna/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve_dlna/)</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Experimental Web based GUI (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/gui/)">https://rclone.org/gui/)</a></dl><h3>Supported providers</h3>(There are many others, built on standard protocols such as WebDAV or S3, that work out of the box.)

As the object storage systems have quite complicated authentication these are kept in a config file. (See the --config entry for how to find the config file and choose its location.) 

 The easiest way to make the config is to run rclone with the config option:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config</pre></dl>

<dt>&bull;
<dd>The local filesystem (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/local/)">https://rclone.org/local/)</a></dl><h3>Usage</h3>Rclone syncs a directory tree from one storage system to another. 

 Its syntax is like this
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Syntax: [options] subcommand &lt;parameters&gt; &lt;parameters...&gt;</pre></dl>
 

 Source and destination paths are specified by the name you gave the storage system in the config file then the sub path, eg "drive:myfolder" to look at "myfolder" in Google drive. 

 You can define as many storage paths as you like in the config file. 

 Please use the -i / --interactive flag while learning rclone to avoid accidental data loss.
<h3>Subcommands</h3>rclone uses a system of subcommands. For example
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:path # lists a remote
rclone copy /local/path remote:path # copies /local/path to the remote
rclone sync -i /local/path remote:path # syncs /local/path to the remote</pre></dl><h2>rclone config</h2>Enter an interactive configuration session.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Enter an interactive configuration session where you can setup new remotes and manage existing ones. You may also set or remove a password to protect your configuration.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for config</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.

<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config reconnect (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_reconnect/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_reconnect/)</a> - Re-authenticates user with remote.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config show (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_show/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_show/)</a> - Print (decrypted) config file, or the config for a single remote.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config update (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_update/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_update/)</a> - Update options in an existing remote.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config userinfo (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_userinfo/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_userinfo/)</a> - Prints info about logged in user of remote.</dl><h2>rclone copy</h2>Copy files from source to dest, skipping already copied.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Copy the source to the destination. Doesn't transfer unchanged files, testing by size and modification time or MD5SUM. Doesn't delete files from the destination. 

 Note that it is always the contents of the directory that is synced, not the directory so when source:path is a directory, it's the contents of source:path that are copied, not the directory name and contents. 

 If dest:path doesn't exist, it is created and the source:path contents go there. 

 For example
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy source:sourcepath dest:destpath</pre></dl>
 

 Let's say there are two files in sourcepath
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>sourcepath/one.txt
sourcepath/two.txt</pre></dl>
 

 This copies them to
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>destpath/one.txt
destpath/two.txt</pre></dl>
 

 Not to
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>destpath/sourcepath/one.txt
destpath/sourcepath/two.txt</pre></dl>
 

 If you are familiar with rsync, rclone always works as if you had written a trailing / - meaning "copy the contents of this directory". This applies to all commands and whether you are talking about the source or destination. 

 See the -no-traverse (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#no-traverse)">https://rclone.org/docs/#no-traverse)</a> option for controlling whether rclone lists the destination directory or not. Supplying this option when copying a small number of files into a large destination can speed transfers up greatly. 

 For example, if you have many files in /path/to/src but only a few of them change every day, you can copy all the files which have changed recently very efficiently like this:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy --max-age 24h --no-traverse /path/to/src remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Note: Use the -P/--progress flag to view real-time transfer statistics. 

 Note: Use the --dry-run or the --interactive/-i flag to test without copying anything.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy source:path dest:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --create-empty-src-dirs Create empty source dirs on destination after copy
 -h, --help help for copy</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone sync</h2>Make source and dest identical, modifying destination only.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Sync the source to the destination, changing the destination only. Doesn't transfer unchanged files, testing by size and modification time or MD5SUM. Destination is updated to match source, including deleting files if necessary. 

 Important: Since this can cause data loss, test first with the --dry-run or the --interactive/-i flag.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i SOURCE remote:DESTINATION</pre></dl>
 

 Note that files in the destination won't be deleted if there were any errors at any point. 

 It is always the contents of the directory that is synced, not the directory so when source:path is a directory, it's the contents of source:path that are copied, not the directory name and contents. See extended explanation in the copy command above if unsure. 

 If dest:path doesn't exist, it is created and the source:path contents go there. 

 Note: Use the -P/--progress flag to view real-time transfer statistics
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync source:path dest:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --create-empty-src-dirs Create empty source dirs on destination after sync
 -h, --help help for sync</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone move</h2>Move files from source to dest.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Moves the contents of the source directory to the destination directory. Rclone will error if the source and destination overlap and the remote does not support a server side directory move operation. 

 If no filters are in use and if possible this will server side move source:path into dest:path. After this source:path will no longer exist. 

 Otherwise for each file in source:path selected by the filters (if any) this will move it into dest:path. If possible a server side move will be used, otherwise it will copy it (server side if possible) into dest:path then delete the original (if no errors on copy) in source:path. 

 If you want to delete empty source directories after move, use the -delete-empty-src-dirs flag. 

 See the -no-traverse (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#no-traverse)">https://rclone.org/docs/#no-traverse)</a> option for controlling whether rclone lists the destination directory or not. Supplying this option when moving a small number of files into a large destination can speed transfers up greatly. 

 Important: Since this can cause data loss, test first with the --dry-run or the --interactive/-i flag. 

 Note: Use the -P/--progress flag to view real-time transfer statistics.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone move source:path dest:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --create-empty-src-dirs Create empty source dirs on destination after move
 --delete-empty-src-dirs Delete empty source dirs after move
 -h, --help help for move</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone delete</h2>Remove the contents of path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Remove the files in path. Unlike purge it obeys include/exclude filters so can be used to selectively delete files. 

 rclone delete only deletes objects but leaves the directory structure alone. If you want to delete a directory and all of its contents use rclone purge 

 If you supply the -rmdirs flag, it will remove all empty directories along with it. 

 Eg delete all files bigger than 100MBytes 

 Check what would be deleted first (use either)
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone --min-size 100M lsl remote:path
rclone --dry-run --min-size 100M delete remote:path</pre></dl>
 

 Then delete
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone --min-size 100M delete remote:path</pre></dl>
 

 That reads "delete everything with a minimum size of 100 MB", hence delete all files bigger than 100MBytes. 

 Important: Since this can cause data loss, test first with the --dry-run or the --interactive/-i flag.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone delete remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for delete
 --rmdirs rmdirs removes empty directories but leaves root intact</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone purge</h2>Remove the path and all of its contents.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Remove the path and all of its contents. Note that this does not obey include/exclude filters - everything will be removed. Use delete if you want to selectively delete files. 

 Important: Since this can cause data loss, test first with the --dry-run or the --interactive/-i flag.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone purge remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for purge</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone mkdir</h2>Make the path if it doesn't already exist.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Make the path if it doesn't already exist.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for mkdir</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone rmdir</h2>Remove the path if empty.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Remove the path. Note that you can't remove a path with objects in it, use purge for that.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rmdir remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for rmdir</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone check</h2>Checks the files in the source and destination match.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Checks the files in the source and destination match. It compares sizes and hashes (MD5 or SHA1) and logs a report of files which don't match. It doesn't alter the source or destination. 

 If you supply the -size-only flag, it will only compare the sizes not the hashes as well. Use this for a quick check. 

 If you supply the -download flag, it will download the data from both remotes and check them against each other on the fly. This can be useful for remotes that don't support hashes or if you really want to check all the data. 

 If you supply the --one-way flag, it will only check that files in the source match the files in the destination, not the other way around. This means that extra files in the destination that are not in the source will not be detected. 

 The --differ, --missing-on-dst, --missing-on-src, --match and --error flags write paths, one per line, to the file name (or stdout if it is -) supplied. What they write is described in the help below. For example --differ will write all paths which are present on both the source and destination but different. 

 The --combined flag will write a file (or stdout) which contains all file paths with a symbol and then a space and then the path to tell you what happened to it. These are reminiscent of diff files.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>= path means path was found in source and destination and was identical
<dt>&bull;
<dd>`- path` means path was missing on the source, so only in the destination
<dt>&bull;
<dd>`+ path` means path was missing on the destination, so only in the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>`* path` means path was present in source and destination but different.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>! path means there was an error reading or hashing the source or dest.
<dd><pre>rclone check source:path dest:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --combined string Make a combined report of changes to this file
 --differ string Report all non-matching files to this file
 --download Check by downloading rather than with hash.
 --error string Report all files with errors (hashing or reading) to this file
 -h, --help help for check
 --match string Report all matching files to this file
 --missing-on-dst string Report all files missing from the destination to this file
 --missing-on-src string Report all files missing from the source to this file
 --one-way Check one way only, source files must exist on remote</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone ls</h2>List the objects in the path with size and path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Lists the objects in the source path to standard output in a human readable format with size and path. Recurses by default. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone ls swift:bucket
 60295 bevajer5jef
 90613 canole
 94467 diwogej7
 37600 fubuwic</pre></dl>
 

 Any of the filtering options can be applied to this command. 

 There are several related list commands
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>ls to list size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsl to list modification time, size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsd to list directories only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsf to list objects and directories in easy to parse format
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsjson to list objects and directories in JSON format</dl>
 

 ls,lsl,lsd are designed to be human readable. lsf is designed to be human and machine readable. lsjson is designed to be machine readable. 

 Note that ls and lsl recurse by default - use "-max-depth 1" to stop the recursion. 

 The other list commands lsd,lsf,lsjson do not recurse by default - use "-R" to make them recurse. 

 Listing a non existent directory will produce an error except for remotes which can't have empty directories (eg s3, swift, gcs, etc - the bucket based remotes).
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for ls</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone lsd</h2>List all directories/containers/buckets in the path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Lists the directories in the source path to standard output. Does not recurse by default. Use the -R flag to recurse. 

 This command lists the total size of the directory (if known, -1 if not), the modification time (if known, the current time if not), the number of objects in the directory (if known, -1 if not) and the name of the directory, Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsd swift:
 494000 2018-04-26 08:43:20 10000 10000files
 65 2018-04-26 08:43:20 1 1File</pre></dl>
 

 Or
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsd drive:test
 -1 2016-10-17 17:41:53 -1 1000files
 -1 2017-01-03 14:40:54 -1 2500files
 -1 2017-07-08 14:39:28 -1 4000files</pre></dl>
 

 If you just want the directory names use "rclone lsf -dirs-only". 

 Any of the filtering options can be applied to this command. 

 There are several related list commands
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>ls to list size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsl to list modification time, size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsd to list directories only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsf to list objects and directories in easy to parse format
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsjson to list objects and directories in JSON format</dl>
 

 ls,lsl,lsd are designed to be human readable. lsf is designed to be human and machine readable. lsjson is designed to be machine readable. 

 Note that ls and lsl recurse by default - use "-max-depth 1" to stop the recursion. 

 The other list commands lsd,lsf,lsjson do not recurse by default - use "-R" to make them recurse. 

 Listing a non existent directory will produce an error except for remotes which can't have empty directories (eg s3, swift, gcs, etc - the bucket based remotes).
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for lsd
 -R, --recursive Recurse into the listing.</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone lsl</h2>List the objects in path with modification time, size and path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Lists the objects in the source path to standard output in a human readable format with modification time, size and path. Recurses by default. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsl swift:bucket
 60295 2016-06-25 18:55:41.062626927 bevajer5jef
 90613 2016-06-25 18:55:43.302607074 canole
 94467 2016-06-25 18:55:43.046609333 diwogej7
 37600 2016-06-25 18:55:40.814629136 fubuwic</pre></dl>
 

 Any of the filtering options can be applied to this command. 

 There are several related list commands
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>ls to list size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsl to list modification time, size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsd to list directories only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsf to list objects and directories in easy to parse format
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsjson to list objects and directories in JSON format</dl>
 

 ls,lsl,lsd are designed to be human readable. lsf is designed to be human and machine readable. lsjson is designed to be machine readable. 

 Note that ls and lsl recurse by default - use "-max-depth 1" to stop the recursion. 

 The other list commands lsd,lsf,lsjson do not recurse by default - use "-R" to make them recurse. 

 Listing a non existent directory will produce an error except for remotes which can't have empty directories (eg s3, swift, gcs, etc - the bucket based remotes).
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsl remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for lsl</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone md5sum</h2>Produces an md5sum file for all the objects in the path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Produces an md5sum file for all the objects in the path. This is in the same format as the standard md5sum tool produces.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone md5sum remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for md5sum</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone sha1sum</h2>Produces an sha1sum file for all the objects in the path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Produces an sha1sum file for all the objects in the path. This is in the same format as the standard sha1sum tool produces.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sha1sum remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for sha1sum</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone size</h2>Prints the total size and number of objects in remote:path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Prints the total size and number of objects in remote:path.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone size remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for size
 --json format output as JSON</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone version</h2>Show the version number.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Show the version number, the go version and the architecture. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone version
rclone v1.41
- os/arch: linux/amd64
- go version: go1.10</pre></dl>
 

 If you supply the -check flag, then it will do an online check to compare your version with the latest release and the latest beta.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone version --check
yours: 1.42.0.6
latest: 1.42 (released 2018-06-16)
beta: 1.42.0.5 (released 2018-06-17)</pre></dl>
 

 Or
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone version --check
yours: 1.41
latest: 1.42 (released 2018-06-16)
 upgrade: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://downloads.rclone.org/v1.42">https://downloads.rclone.org/v1.42</a>
beta: 1.42.0.5 (released 2018-06-17)
 upgrade: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://beta.rclone.org/v1.42-005-g56e1e820">https://beta.rclone.org/v1.42-005-g56e1e820</a></pre><dd><pre>rclone version [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --check Check for new version.
 -h, --help help for version</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone cleanup</h2>Clean up the remote if possible.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Clean up the remote if possible. Empty the trash or delete old file versions. Not supported by all remotes.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cleanup remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for cleanup</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone dedupe</h2>Interactively find duplicate filenames and delete/rename them.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>By default dedupe interactively finds files with duplicate names and offers to delete all but one or rename them to be different. 

 This is only useful with backends like Google Drive which can have duplicate file names. It can be run on wrapping backends (eg crypt) if they wrap a backend which supports duplicate file names. 

 In the first pass it will merge directories with the same name. It will do this iteratively until all the identically named directories have been merged. 

 In the second pass, for every group of duplicate file names, it will delete all but one identical files it finds without confirmation. This means that for most duplicated files the dedupe command will not be interactive. 

 dedupe considers files to be identical if they have the same hash. If the backend does not support hashes (eg crypt wrapping Google Drive) then they will never be found to be identical. If you use the --size-only flag then files will be considered identical if they have the same size (any hash will be ignored). This can be useful on crypt backends which do not support hashes. 

 Important: Since this can cause data loss, test first with the --dry-run or the --interactive/-i flag. 

 Here is an example run. 

 Before - with duplicates
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsl drive:dupes
 6048320 2016-03-05 16:23:16.798000000 one.txt
 6048320 2016-03-05 16:23:11.775000000 one.txt
 564374 2016-03-05 16:23:06.731000000 one.txt
 6048320 2016-03-05 16:18:26.092000000 one.txt
 6048320 2016-03-05 16:22:46.185000000 two.txt
 1744073 2016-03-05 16:22:38.104000000 two.txt
 564374 2016-03-05 16:22:52.118000000 two.txt</pre></dl>
 

 Now the dedupe session
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone dedupe drive:dupes
2016/03/05 16:24:37 Google drive root 'dupes': Looking for duplicates using interactive mode.
one.txt: Found 4 files with duplicate names
one.txt: Deleting 2/3 identical duplicates (MD5 &quot;1eedaa9fe86fd4b8632e2ac549403b36&quot;)
one.txt: 2 duplicates remain
 1: 6048320 bytes, 2016-03-05 16:23:16.798000000, MD5 1eedaa9fe86fd4b8632e2ac549403b36
 2: 564374 bytes, 2016-03-05 16:23:06.731000000, MD5 7594e7dc9fc28f727c42ee3e0749de81
s) Skip and do nothing
k) Keep just one (choose which in next step)
r) Rename all to be different (by changing file.jpg to file-1.jpg)
s/k/r&gt; k
Enter the number of the file to keep&gt; 1
one.txt: Deleted 1 extra copies
two.txt: Found 3 files with duplicates names
two.txt: 3 duplicates remain
 1: 564374 bytes, 2016-03-05 16:22:52.118000000, MD5 7594e7dc9fc28f727c42ee3e0749de81
 2: 6048320 bytes, 2016-03-05 16:22:46.185000000, MD5 1eedaa9fe86fd4b8632e2ac549403b36
 3: 1744073 bytes, 2016-03-05 16:22:38.104000000, MD5 851957f7fb6f0bc4ce76be966d336802
s) Skip and do nothing
k) Keep just one (choose which in next step)
r) Rename all to be different (by changing file.jpg to file-1.jpg)
s/k/r&gt; r
two-1.txt: renamed from: two.txt
two-2.txt: renamed from: two.txt
two-3.txt: renamed from: two.txt</pre></dl>
 

 The result being
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsl drive:dupes
 6048320 2016-03-05 16:23:16.798000000 one.txt
 564374 2016-03-05 16:22:52.118000000 two-1.txt
 6048320 2016-03-05 16:22:46.185000000 two-2.txt
 1744073 2016-03-05 16:22:38.104000000 two-3.txt</pre></dl>
 

 Dedupe can be run non interactively using the --dedupe-mode flag or by using an extra parameter with the same value
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode interactive - interactive as above.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode skip - removes identical files then skips anything left.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode first - removes identical files then keeps the first one.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode newest - removes identical files then keeps the newest one.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode oldest - removes identical files then keeps the oldest one.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode largest - removes identical files then keeps the largest one.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode smallest - removes identical files then keeps the smallest one.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--dedupe-mode rename - removes identical files then renames the rest to be different.</dl>
 

 For example to rename all the identically named photos in your Google Photos directory, do
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone dedupe --dedupe-mode rename &quot;drive:Google Photos&quot;</pre></dl>
 

 Or
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone dedupe rename &quot;drive:Google Photos&quot;</pre><dd><pre>rclone dedupe [mode] remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --dedupe-mode string Dedupe mode interactive|skip|first|newest|oldest|largest|smallest|rename. (default &quot;interactive&quot;)
 -h, --help help for dedupe</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone about</h2>Get quota information from the remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Get quota information from the remote, like bytes used/free/quota and bytes used in the trash. Not supported by all remotes. 

 This will print to stdout something like this:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Total: 17G
Used: 7.444G
Free: 1.315G
Trashed: 100.000M
Other: 8.241G</pre></dl>
 

 Where the fields are:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Total: total size available.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Used: total size used
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Free: total amount this user could upload.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Trashed: total amount in the trash
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Other: total amount in other storage (eg Gmail, Google Photos)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Objects: total number of objects in the storage</dl>
 

 Note that not all the backends provide all the fields - they will be missing if they are not known for that backend. Where it is known that the value is unlimited the value will also be omitted. 

 Use the -full flag to see the numbers written out in full, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Total: 18253611008
Used: 7993453766
Free: 1411001220
Trashed: 104857602
Other: 8849156022</pre></dl>
 

 Use the -json flag for a computer readable output, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;total&quot;: 18253611008,
 &quot;used&quot;: 7993453766,
 &quot;trashed&quot;: 104857602,
 &quot;other&quot;: 8849156022,
 &quot;free&quot;: 1411001220
}</pre><dd><pre>rclone about remote: [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --full Full numbers instead of SI units
 -h, --help help for about
 --json Format output as JSON</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone authorize</h2>Remote authorization.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Remote authorization. Used to authorize a remote or headless rclone from a machine with a browser - use as instructed by rclone config. 

 Use the -auth-no-open-browser to prevent rclone to open auth link in default browser automatically.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone authorize [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --auth-no-open-browser Do not automatically open auth link in default browser
 -h, --help help for authorize</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone backend</h2>Run a backend specific command.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>This runs a backend specific command. The commands themselves (except for "help" and "features") are defined by the backends and you should see the backend docs for definitions. 

 You can discover what commands a backend implements by using
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend help remote:
rclone backend help &lt;backendname&gt;</pre></dl>
 

 You can also discover information about the backend using (see operations/fsinfo (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/rc/#operations/fsinfo)">https://rclone.org/rc/#operations/fsinfo)</a> in the remote control docs for more info).
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend features remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Pass options to the backend command with -o. This should be key=value or key, eg:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend stats remote:path stats -o format=json -o long</pre></dl>
 

 Pass arguments to the backend by placing them on the end of the line
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend cleanup remote:path file1 file2 file3</pre></dl>
 

 Note to run these commands on a running backend then see backend/command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/rc/#backend/command)">https://rclone.org/rc/#backend/command)</a> in the rc docs.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend &lt;command&gt; remote:path [opts] &lt;args&gt; [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for backend
 --json Always output in JSON format.
 -o, --option stringArray Option in the form name=value or name.</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone cat</h2>Concatenates any files and sends them to stdout.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>rclone cat sends any files to standard output. 

 You can use it like this to output a single file
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cat remote:path/to/file</pre></dl>
 

 Or like this to output any file in dir or its subdirectories.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cat remote:path/to/dir</pre></dl>
 

 Or like this to output any .txt files in dir or its subdirectories.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone --include &quot;*.txt&quot; cat remote:path/to/dir</pre></dl>
 

 Use the -head flag to print characters only at the start, -tail for the end and -offset and -count to print a section in the middle. Note that if offset is negative it will count from the end, so -offset -1 -count 1 is equivalent to -tail 1.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cat remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --count int Only print N characters. (default -1)
 --discard Discard the output instead of printing.
 --head int Only print the first N characters.
 -h, --help help for cat
 --offset int Start printing at offset N (or from end if -ve).
 --tail int Only print the last N characters.</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone config create</h2>Create a new remote with name, type and options.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Create a new remote of name with type and options. The options should be passed in pairs of key value. 

 For example to make a swift remote of name myremote using auto config you would do:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config create myremote swift env_auth true</pre></dl>
 

 Note that if the config process would normally ask a question the default is taken. Each time that happens rclone will print a message saying how to affect the value taken. 

 If any of the parameters passed is a password field, then rclone will automatically obscure them if they aren't already obscured before putting them in the config file. 

 NB If the password parameter is 22 characters or longer and consists only of base64 characters then rclone can get confused about whether the password is already obscured or not and put unobscured passwords into the config file. If you want to be 100% certain that the passwords get obscured then use the "-obscure" flag, or if you are 100% certain you are already passing obscured passwords then use "-no-obscure". You can also set osbscured passwords using the "rclone config password" command. 

 So for example if you wanted to configure a Google Drive remote but using remote authorization you would do this:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config create mydrive drive config_is_local false</pre><dd><pre>rclone config create `name` `type` [`key` `value`]* [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for create
 --no-obscure Force any passwords not to be obscured.
 --obscure Force any passwords to be obscured.</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config delete</h2>Delete an existing remote name.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Delete an existing remote name.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config delete `name` [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for delete</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config disconnect</h2>Disconnects user from remote
<h3>Synopsis</h3>This disconnects the remote: passed in to the cloud storage system. 

 This normally means revoking the oauth token. 

 To reconnect use "rclone config reconnect".
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config disconnect remote: [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for disconnect</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config dump</h2>Dump the config file as JSON.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Dump the config file as JSON.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config dump [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for dump</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config edit</h2>Enter an interactive configuration session.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Enter an interactive configuration session where you can setup new remotes and manage existing ones. You may also set or remove a password to protect your configuration.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config edit [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for edit</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config file</h2>Show path of configuration file in use.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Show path of configuration file in use.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config file [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for file</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config password</h2>Update password in an existing remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Update an existing remote's password. The password should be passed in pairs of key value. 

 For example to set password of a remote of name myremote you would do:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config password myremote fieldname mypassword</pre></dl>
 

 This command is obsolete now that "config update" and "config create" both support obscuring passwords directly.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config password `name` [`key` `value`]+ [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for password</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config providers</h2>List in JSON format all the providers and options.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>List in JSON format all the providers and options.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config providers [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for providers</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config reconnect</h2>Re-authenticates user with remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>This reconnects remote: passed in to the cloud storage system. 

 To disconnect the remote use "rclone config disconnect". 

 This normally means going through the interactive oauth flow again.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config reconnect remote: [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for reconnect</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config show</h2>Print (decrypted) config file, or the config for a single remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Print (decrypted) config file, or the config for a single remote.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config show [&lt;remote&gt;] [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for show</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config update</h2>Update options in an existing remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Update an existing remote's options. The options should be passed in in pairs of key value. 

 For example to update the env_auth field of a remote of name myremote you would do:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config update myremote swift env_auth true</pre></dl>
 

 If any of the parameters passed is a password field, then rclone will automatically obscure them if they aren't already obscured before putting them in the config file. 

 NB If the password parameter is 22 characters or longer and consists only of base64 characters then rclone can get confused about whether the password is already obscured or not and put unobscured passwords into the config file. If you want to be 100% certain that the passwords get obscured then use the "-obscure" flag, or if you are 100% certain you are already passing obscured passwords then use "-no-obscure". You can also set osbscured passwords using the "rclone config password" command. 

 If the remote uses OAuth the token will be updated, if you don't require this add an extra parameter thus:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config update myremote swift env_auth true config_refresh_token false</pre><dd><pre>rclone config update `name` [`key` `value`]+ [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for update
 --no-obscure Force any passwords not to be obscured.
 --obscure Force any passwords to be obscured.</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone config userinfo</h2>Prints info about logged in user of remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>This prints the details of the person logged in to the cloud storage system.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config userinfo remote: [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for userinfo
 --json Format output as JSON</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone config (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/)</a> - Enter an interactive configuration session.</dl><h2>rclone copyto</h2>Copy files from source to dest, skipping already copied.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>If source:path is a file or directory then it copies it to a file or directory named dest:path. 

 This can be used to upload single files to other than their current name. If the source is a directory then it acts exactly like the copy command. 

 So
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copyto src dst</pre></dl>
 

 where src and dst are rclone paths, either remote:path or /path/to/local or C:. 

 This will:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>if src is file
 copy it to dst, overwriting an existing file if it exists
if src is directory
 copy it to dst, overwriting existing files if they exist
 see copy command for full details</pre></dl>
 

 This doesn't transfer unchanged files, testing by size and modification time or MD5SUM. It doesn't delete files from the destination. 

 Note: Use the -P/--progress flag to view real-time transfer statistics
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copyto source:path dest:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for copyto</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone copyurl</h2>Copy url content to dest.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Download a URL's content and copy it to the destination without saving it in temporary storage. 

 Setting -auto-filename will cause the file name to be retrieved from the from URL (after any redirections) and used in the destination path. 

 Setting -no-clobber will prevent overwriting file on the destination if there is one with the same name. 

 Setting -stdout or making the output file name "-" will cause the output to be written to standard output.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copyurl <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://example.com">https://example.com</a> dest:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -a, --auto-filename Get the file name from the URL and use it for destination file path
 -h, --help help for copyurl
 --no-clobber Prevent overwriting file with same name
 --stdout Write the output to stdout rather than a file</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone cryptcheck</h2>Cryptcheck checks the integrity of a crypted remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>rclone cryptcheck checks a remote against a crypted remote. This is the equivalent of running rclone check, but able to check the checksums of the crypted remote. 

 For it to work the underlying remote of the cryptedremote must support some kind of checksum. 

 It works by reading the nonce from each file on the cryptedremote: and using that to encrypt each file on the remote:. It then checks the checksum of the underlying file on the cryptedremote: against the checksum of the file it has just encrypted. 

 Use it like this
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cryptcheck /path/to/files encryptedremote:path</pre></dl>
 

 You can use it like this also, but that will involve downloading all the files in remote:path.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cryptcheck remote:path encryptedremote:path</pre></dl>
 

 After it has run it will log the status of the encryptedremote:. 

 If you supply the --one-way flag, it will only check that files in the source match the files in the destination, not the other way around. This means that extra files in the destination that are not in the source will not be detected. 

 The --differ, --missing-on-dst, --missing-on-src, --match and --error flags write paths, one per line, to the file name (or stdout if it is -) supplied. What they write is described in the help below. For example --differ will write all paths which are present on both the source and destination but different. 

 The --combined flag will write a file (or stdout) which contains all file paths with a symbol and then a space and then the path to tell you what happened to it. These are reminiscent of diff files.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>= path means path was found in source and destination and was identical
<dt>&bull;
<dd>`- path` means path was missing on the source, so only in the destination
<dt>&bull;
<dd>`+ path` means path was missing on the destination, so only in the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>`* path` means path was present in source and destination but different.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>! path means there was an error reading or hashing the source or dest.
<dd><pre>rclone cryptcheck remote:path cryptedremote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --combined string Make a combined report of changes to this file
 --differ string Report all non-matching files to this file
 --error string Report all files with errors (hashing or reading) to this file
 -h, --help help for cryptcheck
 --match string Report all matching files to this file
 --missing-on-dst string Report all files missing from the destination to this file
 --missing-on-src string Report all files missing from the source to this file
 --one-way Check one way only, source files must exist on remote</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone cryptdecode</h2>Cryptdecode returns unencrypted file names.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>rclone cryptdecode returns unencrypted file names when provided with a list of encrypted file names. List limit is 10 items. 

 If you supply the -reverse flag, it will return encrypted file names. 

 use it like this
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cryptdecode encryptedremote: encryptedfilename1 encryptedfilename2
rclone cryptdecode --reverse encryptedremote: filename1 filename2</pre><dd><pre>rclone cryptdecode encryptedremote: encryptedfilename [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for cryptdecode
 --reverse Reverse cryptdecode, encrypts filenames</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone deletefile</h2>Remove a single file from remote.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Remove a single file from remote. Unlike delete it cannot be used to remove a directory and it doesn't obey include/exclude filters - if the specified file exists, it will always be removed.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone deletefile remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for deletefile</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone genautocomplete</h2>Output completion script for a given shell.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Generates a shell completion script for rclone. Run with -help to list the supported shells.
<h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for genautocomplete</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone genautocomplete bash (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete_bash/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete_bash/)</a> - Output bash completion script for rclone.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone genautocomplete fish (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete_fish/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete_fish/)</a> - Output fish completion script for rclone.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone genautocomplete zsh (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete_zsh/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete_zsh/)</a> - Output zsh completion script for rclone.</dl><h2>rclone genautocomplete bash</h2>Output bash completion script for rclone.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Generates a bash shell autocompletion script for rclone. 

 This writes to /etc/bash_completion.d/rclone by default so will probably need to be run with sudo or as root, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>sudo rclone genautocomplete bash</pre></dl>
 

 Logout and login again to use the autocompletion scripts, or source them directly
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>. /etc/bash_completion</pre></dl>
 

 If you supply a command line argument the script will be written there.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone genautocomplete bash [output_file] [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for bash</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone genautocomplete (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete/)</a> - Output completion script for a given shell.</dl><h2>rclone genautocomplete fish</h2>Output fish completion script for rclone.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Generates a fish autocompletion script for rclone. 

 This writes to /etc/fish/completions/rclone.fish by default so will probably need to be run with sudo or as root, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>sudo rclone genautocomplete fish</pre></dl>
 

 Logout and login again to use the autocompletion scripts, or source them directly
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>. /etc/fish/completions/rclone.fish</pre></dl>
 

 If you supply a command line argument the script will be written there.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone genautocomplete fish [output_file] [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for fish</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone genautocomplete (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete/)</a> - Output completion script for a given shell.</dl><h2>rclone genautocomplete zsh</h2>Output zsh completion script for rclone.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Generates a zsh autocompletion script for rclone. 

 This writes to /usr/share/zsh/vendor-completions/_rclone by default so will probably need to be run with sudo or as root, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>sudo rclone genautocomplete zsh</pre></dl>
 

 Logout and login again to use the autocompletion scripts, or source them directly
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>autoload -U compinit &amp;&amp; compinit</pre></dl>
 

 If you supply a command line argument the script will be written there.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone genautocomplete zsh [output_file] [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for zsh</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone genautocomplete (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_genautocomplete/)</a> - Output completion script for a given shell.</dl><h2>rclone gendocs</h2>Output markdown docs for rclone to the directory supplied.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>This produces markdown docs for the rclone commands to the directory supplied. These are in a format suitable for hugo to render into the rclone.org website.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone gendocs output_directory [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for gendocs</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone hashsum</h2>Produces a hashsum file for all the objects in the path.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>Produces a hash file for all the objects in the path using the hash named. The output is in the same format as the standard md5sum/sha1sum tool. 

 Run without a hash to see the list of supported hashes, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone hashsum
Supported hashes are:
 * MD5
 * SHA-1
 * DropboxHash
 * QuickXorHash</pre></dl>
 

 Then
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone hashsum MD5 remote:path</pre><dd><pre>rclone hashsum &lt;hash&gt; remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --base64 Output base64 encoded hashsum
 -h, --help help for hashsum</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone link</h2>Generate public link to file/folder.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>rclone link will create, retrieve or remove a public link to the given file or folder.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone link remote:path/to/file
rclone link remote:path/to/folder/
rclone link --unlink remote:path/to/folder/
rclone link --expire 1d remote:path/to/file</pre></dl>
 

 If you supply the -expire flag, it will set the expiration time otherwise it will use the default (100 years). Note not all backends support the -expire flag - if the backend doesn't support it then the link returned won't expire. 

 Use the -unlink flag to remove existing public links to the file or folder. Note not all backends support "-unlink" flag - those that don't will just ignore it. 

 If successful, the last line of the output will contain the link. Exact capabilities depend on the remote, but the link will always by default be created with the least constraints - e.g. no expiry, no password protection, accessible without account.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone link remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --expire Duration The amount of time that the link will be valid (default 100y)
 -h, --help help for link
 --unlink Remove existing public link to file/folder</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone listremotes</h2>List all the remotes in the config file.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>rclone listremotes lists all the available remotes from the config file. 

 When uses with the -l flag it lists the types too.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone listremotes [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> -h, --help help for listremotes
 --long Show the type as well as names.</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone lsf</h2>List directories and objects in remote:path formatted for parsing.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>List the contents of the source path (directories and objects) to standard output in a form which is easy to parse by scripts. By default this will just be the names of the objects and directories, one per line. The directories will have a / suffix. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsf swift:bucket
bevajer5jef
canole
diwogej7
ferejej3gux/
fubuwic</pre></dl>
 

 Use the -format option to control what gets listed. By default this is just the path, but you can use these parameters to control the output:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>p - path
s - size
t - modification time
h - hash
i - ID of object
o - Original ID of underlying object
m - MimeType of object if known
e - encrypted name
T - tier of storage if known, eg &quot;Hot&quot; or &quot;Cool&quot;</pre></dl>
 

 So if you wanted the path, size and modification time, you would use -format "pst", or maybe -format "tsp" to put the path last. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsf --format &quot;tsp&quot; swift:bucket
2016-06-25 18:55:41;60295;bevajer5jef
2016-06-25 18:55:43;90613;canole
2016-06-25 18:55:43;94467;diwogej7
2018-04-26 08:50:45;0;ferejej3gux/
2016-06-25 18:55:40;37600;fubuwic</pre></dl>
 

 If you specify "h" in the format you will get the MD5 hash by default, use the "-hash" flag to change which hash you want. Note that this can be returned as an empty string if it isn't available on the object (and for directories), "ERROR" if there was an error reading it from the object and "UNSUPPORTED" if that object does not support that hash type. 

 For example to emulate the md5sum command you can use
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsf -R --hash MD5 --format hp --separator &quot; &quot; --files-only .</pre></dl>
 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsf -R --hash MD5 --format hp --separator &quot; &quot; --files-only swift:bucket 
7908e352297f0f530b84a756f188baa3 bevajer5jef
cd65ac234e6fea5925974a51cdd865cc canole
03b5341b4f234b9d984d03ad076bae91 diwogej7
8fd37c3810dd660778137ac3a66cc06d fubuwic
99713e14a4c4ff553acaf1930fad985b gixacuh7ku</pre></dl>
 

 (Though "rclone md5sum ." is an easier way of typing this.) 

 By default the separator is ";" this can be changed with the -separator flag. Note that separators aren't escaped in the path so putting it last is a good strategy. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsf --separator &quot;,&quot; --format &quot;tshp&quot; swift:bucket
2016-06-25 18:55:41,60295,7908e352297f0f530b84a756f188baa3,bevajer5jef
2016-06-25 18:55:43,90613,cd65ac234e6fea5925974a51cdd865cc,canole
2016-06-25 18:55:43,94467,03b5341b4f234b9d984d03ad076bae91,diwogej7
2018-04-26 08:52:53,0,,ferejej3gux/
2016-06-25 18:55:40,37600,8fd37c3810dd660778137ac3a66cc06d,fubuwic</pre></dl>
 

 You can output in CSV standard format. This will escape things in &quot; if they contain , 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsf --csv --files-only --format ps remote:path
test.log,22355
test.sh,449
&quot;this file contains a comma, in the file name.txt&quot;,6</pre></dl>
 

 Note that the -absolute parameter is useful for making lists of files to pass to an rclone copy with the -files-from-raw flag. 

 For example to find all the files modified within one day and copy those only (without traversing the whole directory structure):
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsf --absolute --files-only --max-age 1d /path/to/local &gt; new_files
rclone copy --files-from-raw new_files /path/to/local remote:path</pre></dl>
 

 Any of the filtering options can be applied to this command. 

 There are several related list commands
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>ls to list size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsl to list modification time, size and path of objects only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsd to list directories only
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsf to list objects and directories in easy to parse format
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsjson to list objects and directories in JSON format</dl>
 

 ls,lsl,lsd are designed to be human readable. lsf is designed to be human and machine readable. lsjson is designed to be machine readable. 

 Note that ls and lsl recurse by default - use "-max-depth 1" to stop the recursion. 

 The other list commands lsd,lsf,lsjson do not recurse by default - use "-R" to make them recurse. 

 Listing a non existent directory will produce an error except for remotes which can't have empty directories (eg s3, swift, gcs, etc - the bucket based remotes).
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsf remote:path [flags]</pre></dl><h3>Options</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre> --absolute Put a leading / in front of path names.
 --csv Output in CSV format.
 -d, --dir-slash Append a slash to directory names. (default true)
 --dirs-only Only list directories.
 --files-only Only list files.
 -F, --format string Output format - see help for details (default &quot;p&quot;)
 --hash h Use this hash when h is used in the format MD5|SHA-1|DropboxHash (default &quot;MD5&quot;)
 -h, --help help for lsf
 -R, --recursive Recurse into the listing.
 -s, --separator string Separator for the items in the format. (default &quot;;&quot;)</pre></dl>
 

 See the global flags page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/flags/)">https://rclone.org/flags/)</a> for global options not listed here.
<h3>See Also</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone/)</a> - Show help for rclone commands, flags and backends.</dl><h2>rclone lsjson</h2>List directories and objects in the path in JSON format.
<h3>Synopsis</h3>List directories and objects in the path in JSON format. 

 The output is an array of Items, where each Item looks like this 

 { "Hashes" : { "SHA-1" : "f572d396fae9206628714fb2ce00f72e94f2258f", "MD5" : "b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184", "DropboxHash" : "ecb65bb98f9d905b70458986c39fcbad7715e5f2fcc3b1f07767d7c83e2438cc" }, "ID": "y2djkhiujf83u33", "OrigID": "UYOJVTUW00Q1RzTDA", "IsBucket" : false, "IsDir" : false, "MimeType" : "application/octet-stream", "ModTime" : "2017-05-31T16:15:57.034468261+01:00", "Name" : "file.txt", "Encrypted" : "v0qpsdq8anpci8n929v3uu9338", "EncryptedPath" : "kja9098349023498/v0qpsdq8anpci8n929v3uu9338", "Path" : "full/path/goes/here/file.txt", "Size" : 6, "Tier" : "hot", } 

 If -hash is not specified the Hashes property won't be emitted. The types of hash can be specified with the -hash-type parameter (which may be repeated). If -hash-type is set then it implies -hash. 

 If -no-modtime is specified then ModTime will be blank. This can speed things up on remotes where reading the ModTime takes an extra request (eg s3, swift). 

 If -no-mimetype is specified then MimeType will be blank. This can speed things up on remotes where reading the MimeType takes an extra request (eg s3, swift). 

 If -encrypted is not specified the Encrypted won't be emitted. 

 If -dirs-only is not specified files in addition to directories are returned 

 If -files-only is not specified directories in addition to the files will be returned. 

 The Path field will only show folders below the remote path being listed. If "remote:path" contains the file "subfolder/file.txt", the Path for "file.txt" will be "subfolder/file.txt", not "remote:path/subfolder/file.txt". When used without -recursive the Path will always be the same as Name. 

 If the directory is a bucket in a bucket based backend, then "IsBucket" will be set to true. This key won't be present unless it is "true". 

 The time is in RFC3339 format with up to nanosecond precision.
