 This assumes you are running rclone locally on your machine. It is possible to separate the rclone and the GUI - see below for details. 

 If you wish to check for updates then you can add --rc-web-gui-update to the command line. 

 If you find your GUI broken, you may force it to update by add --rc-web-gui-force-update. 

 By default, rclone will open your browser. Add --rc-web-gui-no-open-browser to disable this feature.
<h3>Using the GUI</h3>Once the GUI opens, you will be looking at the dashboard which has an overall overview. 

 On the left hand side you will see a series of view buttons you can click on:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Dashboard - main overview
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Configs - examine and create new configurations
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Explorer - view, download and upload files to the cloud storage systems
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Backend - view or alter the backend config
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Log out</dl>
 

 (More docs and walkthrough video to come!)
<h3>How it works</h3>When you run the rclone rcd --rc-web-gui this is what happens
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Rclone starts but only runs the remote control API ("rc").
<dt>&bull;
<dd>The API is bound to localhost with an auto generated username and password.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>If the API bundle is missing then rclone will download it.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone will start serving the files from the API bundle over the same port as the API
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone will open the browser with a login_token so it can log straight in.</dl><h3>Advanced use</h3>The rclone rcd may use any of the flags documented on the rc page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/rc/#supported-parameters">https://rclone.org/rc/#supported-parameters</a>). 

 The flag --rc-web-gui is shorthand for
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Download the web GUI if necessary
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Check we are using some authentication
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-user gui
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-pass &lt;random password&gt;
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-serve</dl>
 

 These flags can be overridden as desired. 

 See also the rclone rcd documentation (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rcd/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rcd/</a>).
<h3>Example: Running a public GUI</h3>For example the GUI could be served on a public port over SSL using an htpasswd file using the following flags:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-web-gui
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-addr :443
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-htpasswd /path/to/htpasswd
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-cert /path/to/ssl.crt
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-key /path/to/ssl.key</dl><h3>Example: Running a GUI behind a proxy</h3>If you want to run the GUI behind a proxy at /rclone you could use these flags:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-web-gui
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-baseurl rclone
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-htpasswd /path/to/htpasswd</dl>
 

 Or instead of htpasswd if you just want a single user and password:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-user me
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--rc-pass mypassword</dl><h3>Project</h3>The GUI is being developed in the: rclone/rclone-webui-react repository (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/rclone/rclone-webui-react">https://github.com/rclone/rclone-webui-react</a>). 

 Bug reports and contributions are very welcome :-) 

 If you have questions then please ask them on the rclone forum (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://forum.rclone.org/">https://forum.rclone.org/</a>).
<h2>Remote controlling rclone with its API</h2>If rclone is run with the --rc flag then it starts an http server which can be used to remote control rclone using its API. 

 If you just want to run a remote control then see the rcd command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rcd/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rcd/</a>).
<h3>Supported parameters</h3><h3>-rc</h3>Flag to start the http server listen on remote requests
<h3>-rc-addr=IP</h3>IPaddress:Port or :Port to bind server to. (default "localhost:5572")
<h3>-rc-cert=KEY</h3>SSL PEM key (concatenation of certificate and CA certificate)
<h3>-rc-client-ca=PATH</h3>Client certificate authority to verify clients with
<h3>-rc-htpasswd=PATH</h3>htpasswd file - if not provided no authentication is done
<h3>-rc-key=PATH</h3>SSL PEM Private key
<h3>-rc-max-header-bytes=VALUE</h3>Maximum size of request header (default 4096)
<h3>-rc-user=VALUE</h3>User name for authentication.
<h3>-rc-pass=VALUE</h3>Password for authentication.
<h3>-rc-realm=VALUE</h3>Realm for authentication (default "rclone")
<h3>-rc-server-read-timeout=DURATION</h3>Timeout for server reading data (default 1h0m0s)
<h3>-rc-server-write-timeout=DURATION</h3>Timeout for server writing data (default 1h0m0s)
<h3>-rc-serve</h3>Enable the serving of remote objects via the HTTP interface. This means objects will be accessible at <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:5572/">http://127.0.0.1:5572/</a> by default, so you can browse to <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:5572/">http://127.0.0.1:5572/</a> or <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:5572/*">http://127.0.0.1:5572/*</a> to see a listing of the remotes. Objects may be requested from remotes using this syntax <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:5572/[remote:path]/path/to/object">http://127.0.0.1:5572/[remote:path]/path/to/object</a> 

 Default Off.
<h3>-rc-files /path/to/directory</h3>Path to local files to serve on the HTTP server. 

 If this is set then rclone will serve the files in that directory. It will also open the root in the web browser if specified. This is for implementing browser based GUIs for rclone functions. 

 If --rc-user or --rc-pass is set then the URL that is opened will have the authorization in the URL in the <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://user:pass@localhost/">http://user:pass@localhost/</a> style. 

 Default Off.
<h3>-rc-enable-metrics</h3>Enable OpenMetrics/Prometheus compatible endpoint at /metrics. 

 Default Off.
<h3>-rc-web-gui</h3>Set this flag to serve the default web gui on the same port as rclone. 

 Default Off.
<h3>-rc-allow-origin</h3>Set the allowed Access-Control-Allow-Origin for rc requests. 

 Can be used with -rc-web-gui if the rclone is running on different IP than the web-gui. 

 Default is IP address on which rc is running.
<h3>-rc-web-fetch-url</h3>Set the URL to fetch the rclone-web-gui files from. 

 Default <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://api.github.com/repos/rclone/rclone-webui-react/releases/latest.">https://api.github.com/repos/rclone/rclone-webui-react/releases/latest.</a>
<h3>-rc-web-gui-update</h3>Set this flag to check and update rclone-webui-react from the rc-web-fetch-url. 

 Default Off.
<h3>-rc-web-gui-force-update</h3>Set this flag to force update rclone-webui-react from the rc-web-fetch-url. 

 Default Off.
<h3>-rc-web-gui-no-open-browser</h3>Set this flag to disable opening browser automatically when using web-gui. 

 Default Off.
<h3>-rc-job-expire-duration=DURATION</h3>Expire finished async jobs older than DURATION (default 60s).
<h3>-rc-job-expire-interval=DURATION</h3>Interval duration to check for expired async jobs (default 10s).
<h3>-rc-no-auth</h3>By default rclone will require authorisation to have been set up on the rc interface in order to use any methods which access any rclone remotes. Eg operations/list is denied as it involved creating a remote as is sync/copy. 

 If this is set then no authorisation will be required on the server to use these methods. The alternative is to use --rc-user and --rc-pass and use these credentials in the request. 

 Default Off.
<h3>Accessing the remote control via the rclone rc command</h3>Rclone itself implements the remote control protocol in its rclone rc command. 

 You can use it like this
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone rc rc/noop param1=one param2=two
{
 &quot;param1&quot;: &quot;one&quot;,
 &quot;param2&quot;: &quot;two&quot;
}</pre></dl>
 

 Run rclone rc on its own to see the help for the installed remote control commands.
<h3>JSON input</h3>rclone rc also supports a --json flag which can be used to send more complicated input parameters.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone rc --json '{ &quot;p1&quot;: [1,&quot;2&quot;,null,4], &quot;p2&quot;: { &quot;a&quot;:1, &quot;b&quot;:2 } }' rc/noop
{
 &quot;p1&quot;: [
 1,
 &quot;2&quot;,
 null,
 4
 ],
 &quot;p2&quot;: {
 &quot;a&quot;: 1,
 &quot;b&quot;: 2
 }
}</pre></dl>
 

 If the parameter being passed is an object then it can be passed as a JSON string rather than using the --json flag which simplifies the command line.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc operations/list fs=/tmp remote=test opt='{&quot;showHash&quot;: true}'</pre></dl>
 

 Rather than
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc operations/list --json '{&quot;fs&quot;: &quot;/tmp&quot;, &quot;remote&quot;: &quot;test&quot;, &quot;opt&quot;: {&quot;showHash&quot;: true}}'</pre></dl><h3>Special parameters</h3>The rc interface supports some special parameters which apply to all commands. These start with _ to show they are different.
<h3>Running asynchronous jobs with _async = true</h3>Each rc call is classified as a job and it is assigned its own id. By default jobs are executed immediately as they are created or synchronously. 

 If _async has a true value when supplied to an rc call then it will return immediately with a job id and the task will be run in the background. The job/status call can be used to get information of the background job. The job can be queried for up to 1 minute after it has finished. 

 It is recommended that potentially long running jobs, eg sync/sync, sync/copy, sync/move, operations/purge are run with the _async flag to avoid any potential problems with the HTTP request and response timing out. 

 Starting a job with the _async flag:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone rc --json '{ &quot;p1&quot;: [1,&quot;2&quot;,null,4], &quot;p2&quot;: { &quot;a&quot;:1, &quot;b&quot;:2 }, &quot;_async&quot;: true }' rc/noop
{
 &quot;jobid&quot;: 2
}</pre></dl>
 

 Query the status to see if the job has finished. For more information on the meaning of these return parameters see the job/status call.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone rc --json '{ &quot;jobid&quot;:2 }' job/status
{
 &quot;duration&quot;: 0.000124163,
 &quot;endTime&quot;: &quot;2018-10-27T11:38:07.911245881+01:00&quot;,
 &quot;error&quot;: &quot;&quot;,
 &quot;finished&quot;: true,
 &quot;id&quot;: 2,
 &quot;output&quot;: {
 &quot;_async&quot;: true,
 &quot;p1&quot;: [
 1,
 &quot;2&quot;,
 null,
 4
 ],
 &quot;p2&quot;: {
 &quot;a&quot;: 1,
 &quot;b&quot;: 2
 }
 },
 &quot;startTime&quot;: &quot;2018-10-27T11:38:07.911121728+01:00&quot;,
 &quot;success&quot;: true
}</pre></dl>
 

 job/list can be used to show the running or recently completed jobs
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone rc job/list
{
 &quot;jobids&quot;: [
 2
 ]
}</pre></dl><h3>Assigning operations to groups with _group = value</h3>Each rc call has its own stats group for tracking its metrics. By default grouping is done by the composite group name from prefix job/ and id of the job like so job/1. 

 If _group has a value then stats for that request will be grouped under that value. This allows caller to group stats under their own name. 

 Stats for specific group can be accessed by passing group to core/stats:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone rc --json '{ &quot;group&quot;: &quot;job/1&quot; }' core/stats
{
 &quot;speed&quot;: 12345
 ...
}</pre></dl><h3>Supported commands</h3><h3>backend/command: Runs a backend command.</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>command - a string with the command name
<dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>arg - a list of arguments for the backend command
<dt>&bull;
<dd>opt - a map of string to string of options</dl>
 

 Returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>result - result from the backend command</dl>
 

 For example
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc backend/command command=noop fs=. -o echo=yes -o blue -a path1 -a path2</pre></dl>
 

 Returns
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;result&quot;: {
 &quot;arg&quot;: [
 &quot;path1&quot;,
 &quot;path2&quot;
 ],
 &quot;name&quot;: &quot;noop&quot;,
 &quot;opt&quot;: {
 &quot;blue&quot;: &quot;&quot;,
 &quot;echo&quot;: &quot;yes&quot;
 }
 }
}</pre></dl>
 

 Note that this is the direct equivalent of using this "backend" command:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend noop . -o echo=yes -o blue path1 path2</pre></dl>
 

 Note that arguments must be preceded by the "-a" flag 

 See the backend (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_backend/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_backend/)</a> command for more information. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>cache/expire: Purge a remote from cache</h3>Purge a remote from the cache backend. Supports either a directory or a file. Params: - remote = path to remote (required) - withData = true/false to delete cached data (chunks) as well (optional) 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc cache/expire remote=path/to/sub/folder/
rclone rc cache/expire remote=/ withData=true</pre></dl><h3>cache/fetch: Fetch file chunks</h3>Ensure the specified file chunks are cached on disk. 

 The chunks= parameter specifies the file chunks to check. It takes a comma separated list of array slice indices. The slice indices are similar to Python slices: start[:end] 

 start is the 0 based chunk number from the beginning of the file to fetch inclusive. end is 0 based chunk number from the beginning of the file to fetch exclusive. Both values can be negative, in which case they count from the back of the file. The value "-5:" represents the last 5 chunks of a file. 

 Some valid examples are: ":5,-5:" -&gt; the first and last five chunks "0,-2" -&gt; the first and the second last chunk "0:10" -&gt; the first ten chunks 

 Any parameter with a key that starts with "file" can be used to specify files to fetch, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc cache/fetch chunks=0 file=hello file2=home/goodbye</pre></dl>
 

 File names will automatically be encrypted when the a crypt remote is used on top of the cache.
<h3>cache/stats: Get cache stats</h3>Show statistics for the cache remote.
<h3>config/create: create the config for a remote.</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>name - name of remote
<dt>&bull;
<dd>parameters - a map of { "key": "value" } pairs
<dt>&bull;
<dd>type - type of the new remote
<dt>&bull;
<dd>obscure - optional bool - forces obscuring of passwords
<dt>&bull;
<dd>noObscure - optional bool - forces passwords not to be obscured</dl>
 

 See the config create command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_create/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_create/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>config/delete: Delete a remote in the config file.</h3>Parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>name - name of remote to delete</dl>
 

 See the config delete command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_delete/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_delete/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>config/dump: Dumps the config file.</h3>Returns a JSON object: - key: value 

 Where keys are remote names and values are the config parameters. 

 See the config dump command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_dump/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_dump/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>config/get: Get a remote in the config file.</h3>Parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>name - name of remote to get</dl>
 

 See the config dump command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_dump/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_dump/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>config/listremotes: Lists the remotes in the config file.</h3>Returns - remotes - array of remote names 

 See the listremotes command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_listremotes/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_listremotes/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>config/password: password the config for a remote.</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>name - name of remote
<dt>&bull;
<dd>parameters - a map of { "key": "value" } pairs</dl>
 

 See the config password command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_password/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_password/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>config/providers: Shows how providers are configured in the config file.</h3>Returns a JSON object: - providers - array of objects 

 See the config providers command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_providers/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_providers/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>config/update: update the config for a remote.</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>name - name of remote
<dt>&bull;
<dd>parameters - a map of { "key": "value" } pairs
<dt>&bull;
<dd>obscure - optional bool - forces obscuring of passwords
<dt>&bull;
<dd>noObscure - optional bool - forces passwords not to be obscured</dl>
 

 See the config update command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_update/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config_update/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>core/bwlimit: Set the bandwidth limit.</h3>This sets the bandwidth limit to that passed in. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc core/bwlimit rate=off
{
 &quot;bytesPerSecond&quot;: -1,
 &quot;rate&quot;: &quot;off&quot;
}
rclone rc core/bwlimit rate=1M
{
 &quot;bytesPerSecond&quot;: 1048576,
 &quot;rate&quot;: &quot;1M&quot;
}</pre></dl>
 

 If the rate parameter is not supplied then the bandwidth is queried
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc core/bwlimit
{
 &quot;bytesPerSecond&quot;: 1048576,
 &quot;rate&quot;: &quot;1M&quot;
}</pre></dl>
 

 The format of the parameter is exactly the same as passed to -bwlimit except only one bandwidth may be specified. 

 In either case "rate" is returned as a human readable string, and "bytesPerSecond" is returned as a number.
<h3>core/command: Run a rclone terminal command over rc.</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>command - a string with the command name
<dt>&bull;
<dd>arg - a list of arguments for the backend command
<dt>&bull;
<dd>opt - a map of string to string of options</dl>
 

 Returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>result - result from the backend command
<dt>&bull;
<dd>error - set if rclone exits with an error code
<dt>&bull;
<dd>returnType - one of ("COMBINED_OUTPUT", "STREAM", "STREAM_ONLY_STDOUT". "STREAM_ONLY_STDERR")</dl>
 

 For example
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc core/command command=ls -a mydrive:/ -o max-depth=1
rclone rc core/command -a ls -a mydrive:/ -o max-depth=1</pre></dl>
 

 Returns
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;error&quot;: false,
 &quot;result&quot;: &quot;&lt;Raw command line output&gt;&quot;
}
OR 
{
 &quot;error&quot;: true,
 &quot;result&quot;: &quot;&lt;Raw command line output&gt;&quot;
}</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>core/gc: Runs a garbage collection.</h3>This tells the go runtime to do a garbage collection run. It isn't necessary to call this normally, but it can be useful for debugging memory problems.
<h3>core/group-list: Returns list of stats.</h3>This returns list of stats groups currently in memory. 

 Returns the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;groups&quot;: an array of group names:
 [
 &quot;group1&quot;,
 &quot;group2&quot;,
 ...
 ]
}</pre></dl><h3>core/memstats: Returns the memory statistics</h3>This returns the memory statistics of the running program. What the values mean are explained in the go docs: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://golang.org/pkg/runtime/#MemStats">https://golang.org/pkg/runtime/#MemStats</a> 

 The most interesting values for most people are:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>HeapAlloc: This is the amount of memory rclone is actually using
<dt>&bull;
<dd>HeapSys: This is the amount of memory rclone has obtained from the OS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Sys: this is the total amount of memory requested from the OS
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>It is virtual memory so may include unused memory</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>core/obscure: Obscures a string passed in.</h3>Pass a clear string and rclone will obscure it for the config file: - clear - string 

 Returns - obscured - string
<h3>core/pid: Return PID of current process</h3>This returns PID of current process. Useful for stopping rclone process.
<h3>core/quit: Terminates the app.</h3>(optional) Pass an exit code to be used for terminating the app: - exitCode - int
<h3>core/stats: Returns stats about current transfers.</h3>This returns all available stats:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc core/stats</pre></dl>
 

 If group is not provided then summed up stats for all groups will be returned. 

 Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>group - name of the stats group (string)</dl>
 

 Returns the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;speed&quot;: average speed in bytes/sec since start of the process,
 &quot;bytes&quot;: total transferred bytes since the start of the process,
 &quot;errors&quot;: number of errors,
 &quot;fatalError&quot;: whether there has been at least one FatalError,
 &quot;retryError&quot;: whether there has been at least one non-NoRetryError,
 &quot;checks&quot;: number of checked files,
 &quot;transfers&quot;: number of transferred files,
 &quot;deletes&quot; : number of deleted files,
 &quot;renames&quot; : number of renamed files,
 &quot;transferTime&quot; : total time spent on running jobs,
 &quot;elapsedTime&quot;: time in seconds since the start of the process,
 &quot;lastError&quot;: last occurred error,
 &quot;transferring&quot;: an array of currently active file transfers:
 [
 {
 &quot;bytes&quot;: total transferred bytes for this file,
 &quot;eta&quot;: estimated time in seconds until file transfer completion
 &quot;name&quot;: name of the file,
 &quot;percentage&quot;: progress of the file transfer in percent,
 &quot;speed&quot;: average speed over the whole transfer in bytes/sec,
 &quot;speedAvg&quot;: current speed in bytes/sec as an exponentially weighted moving average,
 &quot;size&quot;: size of the file in bytes
 }
 ],
 &quot;checking&quot;: an array of names of currently active file checks
 []
}</pre></dl>
 

 Values for "transferring", "checking" and "lastError" are only assigned if data is available. The value for "eta" is null if an eta cannot be determined.
<h3>core/stats-delete: Delete stats group.</h3>This deletes entire stats group 

 Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>group - name of the stats group (string)</dl><h3>core/stats-reset: Reset stats.</h3>This clears counters, errors and finished transfers for all stats or specific stats group if group is provided. 

 Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>group - name of the stats group (string)</dl><h3>core/transferred: Returns stats about completed transfers.</h3>This returns stats about completed transfers:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc core/transferred</pre></dl>
 

 If group is not provided then completed transfers for all groups will be returned. 

 Note only the last 100 completed transfers are returned. 

 Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>group - name of the stats group (string)</dl>
 

 Returns the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;transferred&quot;: an array of completed transfers (including failed ones):
 [
 {
 &quot;name&quot;: name of the file,
 &quot;size&quot;: size of the file in bytes,
 &quot;bytes&quot;: total transferred bytes for this file,
 &quot;checked&quot;: if the transfer is only checked (skipped, deleted),
 &quot;timestamp&quot;: integer representing millisecond unix epoch,
 &quot;error&quot;: string description of the error (empty if successful),
 &quot;jobid&quot;: id of the job that this transfer belongs to
 }
 ]
}</pre></dl><h3>core/version: Shows the current version of rclone and the go runtime.</h3>This shows the current version of go and the go runtime
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>version - rclone version, eg "v1.53.0"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>decomposed - version number as [major, minor, patch]
<dt>&bull;
<dd>isGit - boolean - true if this was compiled from the git version
<dt>&bull;
<dd>isBeta - boolean - true if this is a beta version
<dt>&bull;
<dd>os - OS in use as according to Go
<dt>&bull;
<dd>arch - cpu architecture in use according to Go
<dt>&bull;
<dd>goVersion - version of Go runtime in use</dl><h3>debug/set-block-profile-rate: Set runtime.SetBlockProfileRate for blocking profiling.</h3>SetBlockProfileRate controls the fraction of goroutine blocking events that are reported in the blocking profile. The profiler aims to sample an average of one blocking event per rate nanoseconds spent blocked. 

 To include every blocking event in the profile, pass rate = 1. To turn off profiling entirely, pass rate &lt;= 0. 

 After calling this you can use this to see the blocking profile:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>go tool pprof <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/block">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/block</a></pre></dl>
 

 Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rate - int</dl><h3>debug/set-mutex-profile-fraction: Set runtime.SetMutexProfileFraction for mutex profiling.</h3>SetMutexProfileFraction controls the fraction of mutex contention events that are reported in the mutex profile. On average 1/rate events are reported. The previous rate is returned. 

 To turn off profiling entirely, pass rate 0. To just read the current rate, pass rate &lt; 0. (For n&gt;1 the details of sampling may change.) 

 Once this is set you can look use this to profile the mutex contention:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>go tool pprof <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/mutex">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/mutex</a></pre></dl>
 

 Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rate - int</dl>
 

 Results
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>previousRate - int</dl><h3>job/list: Lists the IDs of the running jobs</h3>Parameters - None 

 Results
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>jobids - array of integer job ids</dl><h3>job/status: Reads the status of the job ID</h3>Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>jobid - id of the job (integer)</dl>
 

 Results
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>finished - boolean
<dt>&bull;
<dd>duration - time in seconds that the job ran for
<dt>&bull;
<dd>endTime - time the job finished (eg "2018-10-26T18:50:20.528746884+01:00")
<dt>&bull;
<dd>error - error from the job or empty string for no error
<dt>&bull;
<dd>finished - boolean whether the job has finished or not
<dt>&bull;
<dd>id - as passed in above
<dt>&bull;
<dd>startTime - time the job started (eg "2018-10-26T18:50:20.528336039+01:00")
<dt>&bull;
<dd>success - boolean - true for success false otherwise
<dt>&bull;
<dd>output - output of the job as would have been returned if called synchronously
<dt>&bull;
<dd>progress - output of the progress related to the underlying job</dl><h3>job/stop: Stop the running job</h3>Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>jobid - id of the job (integer)</dl><h3>mount/listmounts: Show current mount points</h3>This shows currently mounted points, which can be used for performing an unmount 

 This takes no parameters and returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>mountPoints: list of current mount points</dl>
 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc mount/listmounts</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>mount/mount: Create a new mount point</h3>rclone allows Linux, FreeBSD, macOS and Windows to mount any of Rclone's cloud storage systems as a file system with FUSE. 

 If no mountType is provided, the priority is given as follows: 1. mount 2.cmount 3.mount2 

 This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote path to be mounted (required)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>mountPoint: valid path on the local machine (required)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>mountType: One of the values (mount, cmount, mount2) specifies the mount implementation to use
<dt>&bull;
<dd>mountOpt: a JSON object with Mount options in.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>vfsOpt: a JSON object with VFS options in.</dl>
 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc mount/mount fs=mydrive: mountPoint=/home/&lt;user&gt;/mountPoint
rclone rc mount/mount fs=mydrive: mountPoint=/home/&lt;user&gt;/mountPoint mountType=mount
rclone rc mount/mount fs=TestDrive: mountPoint=/mnt/tmp vfsOpt='{&quot;CacheMode&quot;: 2}' mountOpt='{&quot;AllowOther&quot;: true}'</pre></dl>
 

 The vfsOpt are as described in options/get and can be seen in the the "vfs" section when running and the mountOpt can be seen in the "mount" section.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc options/get</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>mount/types: Show all possible mount types</h3>This shows all possible mount types and returns them as a list. 

 This takes no parameters and returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>mountTypes: list of mount types</dl>
 

 The mount types are strings like "mount", "mount2", "cmount" and can be passed to mount/mount as the mountType parameter. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc mount/types</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>mount/unmount: Unmount selected active mount</h3>rclone allows Linux, FreeBSD, macOS and Windows to mount any of Rclone's cloud storage systems as a file system with FUSE. 

 This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>mountPoint: valid path on the local machine where the mount was created (required)</dl>
 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc mount/unmount mountPoint=/home/&lt;user&gt;/mountPoint</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>mount/unmountall: Show current mount points</h3>This shows currently mounted points, which can be used for performing an unmount 

 This takes no parameters and returns error if unmount does not succeed. 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc mount/unmountall</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/about: Return the space used on the remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"</dl>
 

 The result is as returned from rclone about -json 

 See the about command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_size/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_size/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/cleanup: Remove trashed files in the remote or path</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"</dl>
 

 See the cleanup command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_cleanup/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_cleanup/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/copyfile: Copy a file from source remote to destination remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>srcFs - a remote name string eg "drive:" for the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>srcRemote - a path within that remote eg "file.txt" for the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>dstFs - a remote name string eg "drive2:" for the destination
<dt>&bull;
<dd>dstRemote - a path within that remote eg "file2.txt" for the destination</dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/copyurl: Copy the URL to the object</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>url - string, URL to read from
<dt>&bull;
<dd>autoFilename - boolean, set to true to retrieve destination file name from url See the copyurl command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copyurl/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copyurl/)</a> command for more information on the above.</dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/delete: Remove files in the path</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"</dl>
 

 See the delete command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_delete/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_delete/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/deletefile: Remove the single file pointed to</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"</dl>
 

 See the deletefile command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_deletefile/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_deletefile/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/fsinfo: Return information about the remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"</dl>
 

 This returns info about the remote passed in;
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 // optional features and whether they are available or not
 &quot;Features&quot;: {
 &quot;About&quot;: true,
 &quot;BucketBased&quot;: false,
 &quot;CanHaveEmptyDirectories&quot;: true,
 &quot;CaseInsensitive&quot;: false,
 &quot;ChangeNotify&quot;: false,
 &quot;CleanUp&quot;: false,
 &quot;Copy&quot;: false,
 &quot;DirCacheFlush&quot;: false,
 &quot;DirMove&quot;: true,
 &quot;DuplicateFiles&quot;: false,
 &quot;GetTier&quot;: false,
 &quot;ListR&quot;: false,
 &quot;MergeDirs&quot;: false,
 &quot;Move&quot;: true,
 &quot;OpenWriterAt&quot;: true,
 &quot;PublicLink&quot;: false,
 &quot;Purge&quot;: true,
 &quot;PutStream&quot;: true,
 &quot;PutUnchecked&quot;: false,
 &quot;ReadMimeType&quot;: false,
 &quot;ServerSideAcrossConfigs&quot;: false,
 &quot;SetTier&quot;: false,
 &quot;SetWrapper&quot;: false,
 &quot;UnWrap&quot;: false,
 &quot;WrapFs&quot;: false,
 &quot;WriteMimeType&quot;: false
 },
 // Names of hashes available
 &quot;Hashes&quot;: [
 &quot;MD5&quot;,
 &quot;SHA-1&quot;,
 &quot;DropboxHash&quot;,
 &quot;QuickXorHash&quot;
 ],
 &quot;Name&quot;: &quot;local&quot;, // Name as created
 &quot;Precision&quot;: 1, // Precision of timestamps in ns
 &quot;Root&quot;: &quot;/&quot;, // Path as created
 &quot;String&quot;: &quot;Local file system at /&quot; // how the remote will appear in logs
}</pre></dl>
 

 This command does not have a command line equivalent so use this instead:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc --loopback operations/fsinfo fs=remote:</pre></dl><h3>operations/list: List the given remote and path in JSON format</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>opt - a dictionary of options to control the listing (optional)
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>recurse - If set recurse directories
<dt>&bull;
<dd>noModTime - If set return modification time
<dt>&bull;
<dd>showEncrypted - If set show decrypted names
<dt>&bull;
<dd>showOrigIDs - If set show the IDs for each item if known
<dt>&bull;
<dd>showHash - If set return a dictionary of hashes</dl></dl>
</dl>
 

 The result is
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>list
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>This is an array of objects as described in the lsjson command</dl></dl>
</dl>
 

 See the lsjson command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_lsjson/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_lsjson/)</a> for more information on the above and examples. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/mkdir: Make a destination directory or container</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"</dl>
 

 See the mkdir command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mkdir/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mkdir/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/movefile: Move a file from source remote to destination remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>srcFs - a remote name string eg "drive:" for the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>srcRemote - a path within that remote eg "file.txt" for the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>dstFs - a remote name string eg "drive2:" for the destination
<dt>&bull;
<dd>dstRemote - a path within that remote eg "file2.txt" for the destination</dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/publiclink: Create or retrieve a public link to the given file or folder.</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>unlink - boolean - if set removes the link rather than adding it (optional)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>expire - string - the expiry time of the link eg "1d" (optional)</dl>
 

 Returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>url - URL of the resource</dl>
 

 See the link command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_link/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_link/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/purge: Remove a directory or container and all of its contents</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"</dl>
 

 See the purge command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_purge/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_purge/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/rmdir: Remove an empty directory or container</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"</dl>
 

 See the rmdir command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rmdir/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rmdir/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/rmdirs: Remove all the empty directories in the path</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>leaveRoot - boolean, set to true not to delete the root</dl>
 

 See the rmdirs command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rmdirs/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rmdirs/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/size: Count the number of bytes and files in remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:path/to/dir"</dl>
 

 Returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>count - number of files
<dt>&bull;
<dd>bytes - number of bytes in those files</dl>
 

 See the size command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_size/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_size/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>operations/uploadfile: Upload file using multiform/form-data</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>fs - a remote name string eg "drive:"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>remote - a path within that remote eg "dir"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>each part in body represents a file to be uploaded See the uploadfile command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_uploadfile/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_uploadfile/)</a> command for more information on the above.</dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>options/blocks: List all the option blocks</h3>Returns - options - a list of the options block names
<h3>options/get: Get all the options</h3>Returns an object where keys are option block names and values are an object with the current option values in. 

 This shows the internal names of the option within rclone which should map to the external options very easily with a few exceptions.
<h3>options/set: Set an option</h3>Parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>option block name containing an object with
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>key: value</dl></dl>
</dl>
 

 Repeated as often as required. 

 Only supply the options you wish to change. If an option is unknown it will be silently ignored. Not all options will have an effect when changed like this. 

 For example: 

 This sets DEBUG level logs (-vv)
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc options/set --json '{&quot;main&quot;: {&quot;LogLevel&quot;: 8}}'</pre></dl>
 

 And this sets INFO level logs (-v)
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc options/set --json '{&quot;main&quot;: {&quot;LogLevel&quot;: 7}}'</pre></dl>
 

 And this sets NOTICE level logs (normal without -v)
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc options/set --json '{&quot;main&quot;: {&quot;LogLevel&quot;: 6}}'</pre></dl><h3>pluginsctl/addPlugin: Add a plugin using url</h3>used for adding a plugin to the webgui 

 This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>url: http url of the github repo where the plugin is hosted (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://github.com/rclone/rclone-webui-react)">http://github.com/rclone/rclone-webui-react)</a></dl>
 

 Eg 

 rclone rc pluginsctl/addPlugin 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>pluginsctl/getPluginsForType: Get plugins with type criteria</h3>This shows all possible plugins by a mime type 

 This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>type: supported mime type by a loaded plugin eg (video/mp4, audio/mp3)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>pluginType: filter plugins based on their type eg (DASHBOARD, FILE_HANDLER, TERMINAL)</dl>
 

 and returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>loadedPlugins: list of current production plugins
<dt>&bull;
<dd>testPlugins: list of temporarily loaded development plugins, usually running on a different server.</dl>
 

 Eg 

 rclone rc pluginsctl/getPluginsForType type=video/mp4 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>pluginsctl/listPlugins: Get the list of currently loaded plugins</h3>This allows you to get the currently enabled plugins and their details. 

 This takes no parameters and returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>loadedPlugins: list of current production plugins
<dt>&bull;
<dd>testPlugins: list of temporarily loaded development plugins, usually running on a different server.</dl>
 

 Eg 

 rclone rc pluginsctl/listPlugins 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>pluginsctl/listTestPlugins: Show currently loaded test plugins</h3>allows listing of test plugins with the rclone.test set to true in package.json of the plugin 

 This takes no parameters and returns
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>loadedTestPlugins: list of currently available test plugins</dl>
 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc pluginsctl/listTestPlugins</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>pluginsctl/removePlugin: Remove a loaded plugin</h3>This allows you to remove a plugin using it's name 

 This takes parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>name: name of the plugin in the format author/plugin_name</dl>
 

 Eg 

 rclone rc pluginsctl/removePlugin name=rclone/video-plugin 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>pluginsctl/removeTestPlugin: Remove a test plugin</h3>This allows you to remove a plugin using it's name 

 This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>name: name of the plugin in the format author/plugin_name</dl>
 

 Eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc pluginsctl/removeTestPlugin name=rclone/rclone-webui-react</pre></dl>
 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>rc/error: This returns an error</h3>This returns an error with the input as part of its error string. Useful for testing error handling.
<h3>rc/list: List all the registered remote control commands</h3>This lists all the registered remote control commands as a JSON map in the commands response.
<h3>rc/noop: Echo the input to the output parameters</h3>This echoes the input parameters to the output parameters for testing purposes. It can be used to check that rclone is still alive and to check that parameter passing is working properly.
<h3>rc/noopauth: Echo the input to the output parameters requiring auth</h3>This echoes the input parameters to the output parameters for testing purposes. It can be used to check that rclone is still alive and to check that parameter passing is working properly. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>sync/copy: copy a directory from source remote to destination remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>srcFs - a remote name string eg "drive:src" for the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>dstFs - a remote name string eg "drive:dst" for the destination</dl>
 

 See the copy command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>sync/move: move a directory from source remote to destination remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>srcFs - a remote name string eg "drive:src" for the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>dstFs - a remote name string eg "drive:dst" for the destination
<dt>&bull;
<dd>deleteEmptySrcDirs - delete empty src directories if set</dl>
 

 See the move command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_move/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_move/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>sync/sync: sync a directory from source remote to destination remote</h3>This takes the following parameters
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>srcFs - a remote name string eg "drive:src" for the source
<dt>&bull;
<dd>dstFs - a remote name string eg "drive:dst" for the destination</dl>
 

 See the sync command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/)</a> command for more information on the above. 

 Authentication is required for this call.
<h3>vfs/forget: Forget files or directories in the directory cache.</h3>This forgets the paths in the directory cache causing them to be re-read from the remote when needed. 

 If no paths are passed in then it will forget all the paths in the directory cache.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc vfs/forget</pre></dl>
 

 Otherwise pass files or dirs in as file=path or dir=path. Any parameter key starting with file will forget that file and any starting with dir will forget that dir, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc vfs/forget file=hello file2=goodbye dir=home/junk</pre></dl>
 

 This command takes an "fs" parameter. If this parameter is not supplied and if there is only one VFS in use then that VFS will be used. If there is more than one VFS in use then the "fs" parameter must be supplied.
<h3>vfs/list: List active VFSes.</h3>This lists the active VFSes. 

 It returns a list under the key "vfses" where the values are the VFS names that could be passed to the other VFS commands in the "fs" parameter.
<h3>vfs/poll-interval: Get the status or update the value of the poll-interval option.</h3>Without any parameter given this returns the current status of the poll-interval setting. 

 When the interval=duration parameter is set, the poll-interval value is updated and the polling function is notified. Setting interval=0 disables poll-interval.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc vfs/poll-interval interval=5m</pre></dl>
 

 The timeout=duration parameter can be used to specify a time to wait for the current poll function to apply the new value. If timeout is less or equal 0, which is the default, wait indefinitely. 

 The new poll-interval value will only be active when the timeout is not reached. 

 If poll-interval is updated or disabled temporarily, some changes might not get picked up by the polling function, depending on the used remote. 

 This command takes an "fs" parameter. If this parameter is not supplied and if there is only one VFS in use then that VFS will be used. If there is more than one VFS in use then the "fs" parameter must be supplied.
<h3>vfs/refresh: Refresh the directory cache.</h3>This reads the directories for the specified paths and freshens the directory cache. 

 If no paths are passed in then it will refresh the root directory.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc vfs/refresh</pre></dl>
 

 Otherwise pass directories in as dir=path. Any parameter key starting with dir will refresh that directory, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rc vfs/refresh dir=home/junk dir2=data/misc</pre></dl>
 

 If the parameter recursive=true is given the whole directory tree will get refreshed. This refresh will use -fast-list if enabled. 

 This command takes an "fs" parameter. If this parameter is not supplied and if there is only one VFS in use then that VFS will be used. If there is more than one VFS in use then the "fs" parameter must be supplied.
<h3>Accessing the remote control via HTTP</h3>Rclone implements a simple HTTP based protocol. 

 Each endpoint takes an JSON object and returns a JSON object or an error. The JSON objects are essentially a map of string names to values. 

 All calls must made using POST. 

 The input objects can be supplied using URL parameters, POST parameters or by supplying "Content-Type: application/json" and a JSON blob in the body. There are examples of these below using curl. 

 The response will be a JSON blob in the body of the response. This is formatted to be reasonably human readable.
<h3>Error returns</h3>If an error occurs then there will be an HTTP error status (eg 500) and the body of the response will contain a JSON encoded error object, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;error&quot;: &quot;Expecting string value for key \&quot;remote\&quot; (was float64)&quot;,
 &quot;input&quot;: {
 &quot;fs&quot;: &quot;/tmp&quot;,
 &quot;remote&quot;: 3
 },
 &quot;status&quot;: 400
 &quot;path&quot;: &quot;operations/rmdir&quot;,
}</pre></dl>
 

 The keys in the error response are - error - error string - input - the input parameters to the call - status - the HTTP status code - path - the path of the call
<h3>Cors</h3>The sever implements basic CORS support and allows all origins for that. The response to a preflight OPTIONS request will echo the requested "Access-Control-Request-Headers" back.
<h3>Using POST with URL parameters only</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre>curl -X POST '<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/rc/noop?potato=1">http://localhost:5572/rc/noop?potato=1</a>&amp;sausage=2'</pre></dl>
 

 Response
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;potato&quot;: &quot;1&quot;,
 &quot;sausage&quot;: &quot;2&quot;
}</pre></dl>
 

 Here is what an error response looks like:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>curl -X POST '<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/rc/error?potato=1">http://localhost:5572/rc/error?potato=1</a>&amp;sausage=2'</pre><dd><pre>{
 &quot;error&quot;: &quot;arbitrary error on input map[potato:1 sausage:2]&quot;,
 &quot;input&quot;: {
 &quot;potato&quot;: &quot;1&quot;,
 &quot;sausage&quot;: &quot;2&quot;
 }
}</pre></dl>
 

 Note that curl doesn't return errors to the shell unless you use the -f option
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ curl -f -X POST '<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/rc/error?potato=1">http://localhost:5572/rc/error?potato=1</a>&amp;sausage=2'
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 400 Bad Request
$ echo $?
22</pre></dl><h3>Using POST with a form</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre>curl --data &quot;potato=1&quot; --data &quot;sausage=2&quot; <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/rc/noop">http://localhost:5572/rc/noop</a></pre></dl>
 

 Response
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;potato&quot;: &quot;1&quot;,
 &quot;sausage&quot;: &quot;2&quot;
}</pre></dl>
 

 Note that you can combine these with URL parameters too with the POST parameters taking precedence.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>curl --data &quot;potato=1&quot; --data &quot;sausage=2&quot; &quot;<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/rc/noop?rutabaga=3">http://localhost:5572/rc/noop?rutabaga=3</a>&amp;sausage=4&quot;</pre></dl>
 

 Response
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;potato&quot;: &quot;1&quot;,
 &quot;rutabaga&quot;: &quot;3&quot;,
 &quot;sausage&quot;: &quot;4&quot;
}</pre></dl><h3>Using POST with a JSON blob</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre>curl -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; -X POST -d '{&quot;potato&quot;:2,&quot;sausage&quot;:1}' <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/rc/noop">http://localhost:5572/rc/noop</a></pre></dl>
 

 response
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>{
 &quot;password&quot;: &quot;xyz&quot;,
 &quot;username&quot;: &quot;xyz&quot;
}</pre></dl>
 

 This can be combined with URL parameters too if required. The JSON blob takes precedence.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>curl -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; -X POST -d '{&quot;potato&quot;:2,&quot;sausage&quot;:1}' '<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/rc/noop?rutabaga=3">http://localhost:5572/rc/noop?rutabaga=3</a>&amp;potato=4'</pre><dd><pre>{
 &quot;potato&quot;: 2,
 &quot;rutabaga&quot;: &quot;3&quot;,
 &quot;sausage&quot;: 1
}</pre></dl><h3>Debugging rclone with pprof</h3>If you use the --rc flag this will also enable the use of the go profiling tools on the same port. 

 To use these, first install go (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://golang.org/doc/install">https://golang.org/doc/install</a>).
<h3>Debugging memory use</h3>To profile rclone's memory use you can run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>go tool pprof -web <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/heap">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/heap</a></pre></dl>
 

 This should open a page in your browser showing what is using what memory. 

 You can also use the -text flag to produce a textual summary
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ go tool pprof -text <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/heap">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/heap</a>
Showing nodes accounting for 1537.03kB, 100% of 1537.03kB total
 flat flat% sum% cum cum%
 1024.03kB 66.62% 66.62% 1024.03kB 66.62% github.com/rclone/rclone/vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack.addDecoderNode
 513kB 33.38% 100% 513kB 33.38% net/http.newBufioWriterSize
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% github.com/rclone/rclone/cmd/all.init
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% github.com/rclone/rclone/cmd/serve.init
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% github.com/rclone/rclone/cmd/serve/restic.init
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% github.com/rclone/rclone/vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2.init
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% github.com/rclone/rclone/vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack.init
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% github.com/rclone/rclone/vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack.init.0
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% main.init
 0 0% 100% 513kB 33.38% net/http.(*conn).readRequest
 0 0% 100% 513kB 33.38% net/http.(*conn).serve
 0 0% 100% 1024.03kB 66.62% runtime.main</pre></dl><h3>Debugging go routine leaks</h3>Memory leaks are most often caused by go routine leaks keeping memory alive which should have been garbage collected. 

 See all active go routines using
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>curl <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1</a></pre></dl>
 

 Or go to <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1</a> in your browser.
<h3>Other profiles to look at</h3>You can see a summary of profiles available at <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/</a> 

 Here is how to use some of them:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Memory: go tool pprof <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/heap">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/heap</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Go routines: curl <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>30-second CPU profile: go tool pprof <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/profile">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/profile</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>5-second execution trace: wget <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/trace?seconds=5">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/trace?seconds=5</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Goroutine blocking profile
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Enable first with: rclone rc debug/set-block-profile-rate rate=1 (docs)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>go tool pprof <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/block">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/block</a></dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>Contended mutexes:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Enable first with: rclone rc debug/set-mutex-profile-fraction rate=1 (docs)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>go tool pprof <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/mutex">http://localhost:5572/debug/pprof/mutex</a></dl></dl>
</dl>
 

 See the net/http/pprof docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://golang.org/pkg/net/http/pprof/)">https://golang.org/pkg/net/http/pprof/)</a> for more info on how to use the profiling and for a general overview see the Go team's blog post on profiling go programs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://blog.golang.org/profiling-go-programs">https://blog.golang.org/profiling-go-programs</a>). 

 The profiling hook is zero overhead unless it is used (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://stackoverflow.com/q/26545159/164234">https://stackoverflow.com/q/26545159/164234</a>).
<h2>Overview of cloud storage systems</h2>Each cloud storage system is slightly different. Rclone attempts to provide a unified interface to them, but some underlying differences show through.

</td></tr> </table><h3>Hash</h3>The cloud storage system supports various hash types of the objects. The hashes are used when transferring data as an integrity check and can be specifically used with the --checksum flag in syncs and in the check command. 

 To use the verify checksums when transferring between cloud storage systems they must support a common hash type. 

 - Note that Dropbox supports its own custom hash (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.dropbox.com/developers/reference/content-hash">https://www.dropbox.com/developers/reference/content-hash</a>). This is an SHA256 sum of all the 4MB block SHA256s. 

 = SFTP supports checksums if the same login has shell access and md5sum or sha1sum as well as echo are in the remote's PATH. 

 -- WebDAV supports hashes when used with Owncloud and Nextcloud only. 

 --- WebDAV supports modtimes when used with Owncloud and Nextcloud only. 

 == Microsoft OneDrive Personal supports SHA1 hashes, whereas OneDrive for business and SharePoint server support Microsoft's own QuickXorHash (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/developer/code-snippets/quickxorhash">https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/developer/code-snippets/quickxorhash</a>). 

 === Mail.ru uses its own modified SHA1 hash
<h3>ModTime</h3>The cloud storage system supports setting modification times on objects. If it does then this enables a using the modification times as part of the sync. If not then only the size will be checked by default, though the MD5SUM can be checked with the --checksum flag. 

 All cloud storage systems support some kind of date on the object and these will be set when transferring from the cloud storage system.
<h3>Case Insensitive</h3>If a cloud storage systems is case sensitive then it is possible to have two files which differ only in case, eg file.txt and FILE.txt. If a cloud storage system is case insensitive then that isn't possible. 

 This can cause problems when syncing between a case insensitive system and a case sensitive system. The symptom of this is that no matter how many times you run the sync it never completes fully. 

 The local filesystem and SFTP may or may not be case sensitive depending on OS.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Windows - usually case insensitive, though case is preserved
<dt>&bull;
<dd>OSX - usually case insensitive, though it is possible to format case sensitive
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Linux - usually case sensitive, but there are case insensitive file systems (eg FAT formatted USB keys)</dl>
 

 Most of the time this doesn't cause any problems as people tend to avoid files whose name differs only by case even on case sensitive systems.
<h3>Duplicate files</h3>If a cloud storage system allows duplicate files then it can have two objects with the same name. 

 This confuses rclone greatly when syncing - use the rclone dedupe command to rename or remove duplicates. 

 * Opendrive does not support creation of duplicate files using their web client interface or other stock clients, but the underlying storage platform has been determined to allow duplicate files, and it is possible to create them with rclone. It may be that this is a mistake or an unsupported feature.
<h3>Restricted filenames</h3>Some cloud storage systems might have restrictions on the characters that are usable in file or directory names. When rclone detects such a name during a file upload, it will transparently replace the restricted characters with similar looking Unicode characters. 

 This process is designed to avoid ambiguous file names as much as possible and allow to move files between many cloud storage systems transparently. 

 The name shown by rclone to the user or during log output will only contain a minimal set of replaced characters to ensure correct formatting and not necessarily the actual name used on the cloud storage. 

 This transformation is reversed when downloading a file or parsing rclone arguments. For example, when uploading a file named my file?.txt to Onedrive will be displayed as my file?.txt on the console, but stored as my file1F.txt (the ? gets replaced by the similar looking 1F character) to Onedrive. The reverse transformation allows to read a fileunusual/name.txt from Google Drive, by passing the name unusual0Fname.txt (the / needs to be replaced by the similar looking 0F character) on the command line.
<h3>Default restricted characters</h3>The table below shows the characters that are replaced by default. 

 When a replacement character is found in a filename, this character will be escaped with the 1B character to avoid ambiguous file names. (e.g. a file named 00.txt would shown as 1B00.txt) 

 Each cloud storage backend can use a different set of characters, which will be specified in the documentation for each backend.

</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> .. </td><td ALIGN=center> 0E0E 
</td></tr> </table><h3>Invalid UTF-8 bytes</h3>Some backends only support a sequence of well formed UTF-8 bytes as file or directory names. 

 In this case all invalid UTF-8 bytes will be replaced with a quoted representation of the byte value to allow uploading a file to such a backend. For example, the invalid byte 0xFE will be encoded as 1BFE. 

 A common source of invalid UTF-8 bytes are local filesystems, that store names in a different encoding than UTF-8 or UTF-16, like latin1. See the local filenames (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/local/#filenames)">https://rclone.org/local/#filenames)</a> section for details.
<h3>Encoding option</h3>Most backends have an encoding options, specified as a flag --backend-encoding where backend is the name of the backend, or as a config parameter encoding (you'll need to select the Advanced config in rclone config to see it). 

 This will have default value which encodes and decodes characters in such a way as to preserve the maximum number of characters (see above). 

 However this can be incorrect in some scenarios, for example if you have a Windows file system with characters such as 0A and 1F that you want to remain as those characters on the remote rather than being translated to * and ?. 

 The --backend-encoding flags allow you to change that. You can disable the encoding completely with --backend-encoding None or set encoding = None in the config file. 

 Encoding takes a comma separated list of encodings. You can see the list of all available characters by passing an invalid value to this flag, eg --local-encoding &quot;help&quot; and rclone help flags encoding will show you the defaults for the backends. 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Encoding </td><td> Characters 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=2><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Asterisk </td><td> * 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> BackQuote </td><td> ` 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> BackSlash </td><td> \ 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Colon </td><td> : 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> CrLf </td><td> CR 0x0D, LF 0x0A 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Ctl </td><td> All control characters 0x00-0x1F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Del </td><td> DEL 0x7F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Dollar </td><td> $ 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Dot </td><td> . 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> DoubleQuote </td><td> &quot; 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Hash </td><td> #

</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> LeftCrLfHtVt </td><td> CR 0x0D, LF 0x0A,HT 0x09, VT 0x0B on the left of a string 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> LeftPeriod </td><td> . on the left of a string

</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> LeftTilde </td><td> ~ on the left of a string 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> LtGt </td><td> &lt;, &gt;

</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Percent </td><td> % 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Pipe </td><td> | 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> Question </td><td> ? 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> RightCrLfHtVt </td><td> CR 0x0D, LF 0x0A, HT 0x09, VT 0x0B on the right of a string 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> RightPeriod </td><td> . on the right of a string

 To take a specific example, the FTP backend's default encoding is
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>--ftp-encoding &quot;Slash,Del,Ctl,RightSpace,Dot&quot;</pre></dl>
 

 However, let's say the FTP server is running on Windows and can't have any of the invalid Windows characters in file names. You are backing up Linux servers to this FTP server which do have those characters in file names. So you would add the Windows set which are
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Slash,LtGt,DoubleQuote,Colon,Question,Asterisk,Pipe,BackSlash,Ctl,RightSpace,RightPeriod,InvalidUtf8,Dot</pre></dl>
 

 to the existing ones, giving:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Slash,LtGt,DoubleQuote,Colon,Question,Asterisk,Pipe,BackSlash,Ctl,RightSpace,RightPeriod,InvalidUtf8,Dot,Del,RightSpace</pre></dl>
 

 This can be specified using the --ftp-encoding flag or using an encoding parameter in the config file. 

 Or let's say you have a Windows server but you want to preserve 0A and 1F, you would then have this as the encoding (the Windows encoding minus Asterisk and Question).
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Slash,LtGt,DoubleQuote,Colon,Pipe,BackSlash,Ctl,RightSpace,RightPeriod,InvalidUtf8,Dot</pre></dl>
 

 This can be specified using the --local-encoding flag or using an encoding parameter in the config file.
<h3>MIME Type</h3>MIME types (also known as media types) classify types of documents using a simple text classification, eg text/html or application/pdf. 

 Some cloud storage systems support reading (R) the MIME type of objects and some support writing (W) the MIME type of objects. 

 The MIME type can be important if you are serving files directly to HTTP from the storage system. 

 If you are copying from a remote which supports reading (R) to a remote which supports writing (W) then rclone will preserve the MIME types. Otherwise they will be guessed from the extension, or the remote itself may assign the MIME type.
