<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "standard"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"standard"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Encrypt the filenames see the docs for the details.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"obfuscate"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Very simple filename obfuscation.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"off"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Don't encrypt the file names. Adds a ".bin" extension only.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-crypt-directory-name-encryption</h3>Option to either encrypt directory names or leave them intact. 

 NB If filename_encryption is "off" then this option will do nothing.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: directory_name_encryption
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_CRYPT_DIRECTORY_NAME_ENCRYPTION
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: true
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"true"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Encrypt directory names.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"false"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Don't encrypt directory names, leave them intact.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-crypt-password</h3>Password or pass phrase for encryption. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: password
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_CRYPT_PASSWORD
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-crypt-password2</h3>Password or pass phrase for salt. Optional but recommended. Should be different to the previous password. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: password2
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_CRYPT_PASSWORD2
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to crypt (Encrypt/Decrypt a remote).
<h3>-crypt-server-side-across-configs</h3>Allow server side operations (eg copy) to work across different crypt configs. 

 Normally this option is not what you want, but if you have two crypts pointing to the same backend you can use it. 

 This can be used, for example, to change file name encryption type without re-uploading all the data. Just make two crypt backends pointing to two different directories with the single changed parameter and use rclone move to move the files between the crypt remotes.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: server_side_across_configs
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_CRYPT_SERVER_SIDE_ACROSS_CONFIGS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-crypt-show-mapping</h3>For all files listed show how the names encrypt. 

 If this flag is set then for each file that the remote is asked to list, it will log (at level INFO) a line stating the decrypted file name and the encrypted file name. 

 This is so you can work out which encrypted names are which decrypted names just in case you need to do something with the encrypted file names, or for debugging purposes.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: show_mapping
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_CRYPT_SHOW_MAPPING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>Backend commands</h3>Here are the commands specific to the crypt backend. 

 Run them with
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend COMMAND remote:</pre></dl>
 

 The help below will explain what arguments each command takes. 

 See the "rclone backend" command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_backend/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_backend/)</a> for more info on how to pass options and arguments. 

 These can be run on a running backend using the rc command backend/command (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/rc/#backend/command">https://rclone.org/rc/#backend/command</a>).
<h3>encode</h3>Encode the given filename(s)
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend encode remote: [options] [&lt;arguments&gt;+]</pre></dl>
 

 This encodes the filenames given as arguments returning a list of strings of the encoded results. 

 Usage Example:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend encode crypt: file1 [file2...]
rclone rc backend/command command=encode fs=crypt: file1 [file2...]</pre></dl><h3>decode</h3>Decode the given filename(s)
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend decode remote: [options] [&lt;arguments&gt;+]</pre></dl>
 

 This decodes the filenames given as arguments returning a list of strings of the decoded results. It will return an error if any of the inputs are invalid. 

 Usage Example:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone backend decode crypt: encryptedfile1 [encryptedfile2...]
rclone rc backend/command command=decode fs=crypt: encryptedfile1 [encryptedfile2...]</pre></dl><h3>Backing up a crypted remote</h3>If you wish to backup a crypted remote, it is recommended that you use rclone sync on the encrypted files, and make sure the passwords are the same in the new encrypted remote. 

 This will have the following advantages
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone sync will check the checksums while copying
<dt>&bull;
<dd>you can use rclone check between the encrypted remotes
<dt>&bull;
<dd>you don't decrypt and encrypt unnecessarily</dl>
 

 For example, let's say you have your original remote at remote: with the encrypted version at eremote: with path remote:crypt. You would then set up the new remote remote2: and then the encrypted version eremote2: with path remote2:crypt using the same passwords as eremote:. 

 To sync the two remotes you would do
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i remote:crypt remote2:crypt</pre></dl>
 

 And to check the integrity you would do
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone check remote:crypt remote2:crypt</pre></dl><h3>File formats</h3><h3>File encryption</h3>Files are encrypted 1:1 source file to destination object. The file has a header and is divided into chunks.
<h3>Header</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>8 bytes magic string RCLONE\x00\x00
<dt>&bull;
<dd>24 bytes Nonce (IV)</dl>
 

 The initial nonce is generated from the operating systems crypto strong random number generator. The nonce is incremented for each chunk read making sure each nonce is unique for each block written. The chance of a nonce being re-used is minuscule. If you wrote an exabyte of data (10&sup1;78 bytes) you would have a probability of approximately 2mu107B&sup3;&sup2; of re-using a nonce.
<h3>Chunk</h3>Each chunk will contain 64kB of data, except for the last one which may have less data. The data chunk is in standard NACL secretbox format. Secretbox uses XSalsa20 and Poly1305 to encrypt and authenticate messages. 

 Each chunk contains:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>16 Bytes of Poly1305 authenticator
<dt>&bull;
<dd>1 - 65536 bytes XSalsa20 encrypted data</dl>
 

 64k chunk size was chosen as the best performing chunk size (the authenticator takes too much time below this and the performance drops off due to cache effects above this). Note that these chunks are buffered in memory so they can't be too big. 

 This uses a 32 byte (256 bit key) key derived from the user password.
<h3>Examples</h3>1 byte file will encrypt to
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>32 bytes header
<dt>&bull;
<dd>17 bytes data chunk</dl>
 

 49 bytes total 

 1MB (1048576 bytes) file will encrypt to
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>32 bytes header
<dt>&bull;
<dd>16 chunks of 65568 bytes</dl>
 

 1049120 bytes total (a 0.05% overhead). This is the overhead for big files.
<h3>Name encryption</h3>File names are encrypted segment by segment - the path is broken up into / separated strings and these are encrypted individually. 

 File segments are padded using PKCS#7 to a multiple of 16 bytes before encryption. 

 They are then encrypted with EME using AES with 256 bit key. EME (ECB-Mix-ECB) is a wide-block encryption mode presented in the 2003 paper "A Parallelizable Enciphering Mode" by Halevi and Rogaway. 

 This makes for deterministic encryption which is what we want - the same filename must encrypt to the same thing otherwise we can't find it on the cloud storage system. 

 This means that
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>filenames with the same name will encrypt the same
<dt>&bull;
<dd>filenames which start the same won't have a common prefix</dl>
 

 This uses a 32 byte key (256 bits) and a 16 byte (128 bits) IV both of which are derived from the user password. 

 After encryption they are written out using a modified version of standard base32 encoding as described in RFC4648. The standard encoding is modified in two ways:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>it becomes lower case (no-one likes upper case filenames!)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>we strip the padding character =</dl>
 

 base32 is used rather than the more efficient base64 so rclone can be used on case insensitive remotes (eg Windows, Amazon Drive).
<h3>Key derivation</h3>Rclone uses scrypt with parameters N=16384, r=8, p=1 with an optional user supplied salt (password2) to derive the 32+32+16 = 80 bytes of key material required. If the user doesn't supply a salt then rclone uses an internal one. 

 scrypt makes it impractical to mount a dictionary attack on rclone encrypted data. For full protection against this you should always use a salt.
<h3>Dropbox</h3>Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Dropbox paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 The initial setup for dropbox involves getting a token from Dropbox which you need to do in your browser. rclone config walks you through it. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>n) New remote
d) Delete remote
q) Quit config
e/n/d/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / Dropbox
 \ &quot;dropbox&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; dropbox
Dropbox App Key - leave blank normally.
app_key&gt;
Dropbox App Secret - leave blank normally.
app_secret&gt;
Remote config
Please visit:
<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.dropbox.com/1/oauth2/authorize?client_id=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX">https://www.dropbox.com/1/oauth2/authorize?client_id=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX</a>&amp;response_type=code
Enter the code: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX_XXXXXXXXXX
--------------------
[remote]
app_key =
app_secret =
token = XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX_XXXX_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 You can then use it like this, 

 List directories in top level of your dropbox
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your dropbox
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to a dropbox directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Dropbox for business</h3>Rclone supports Dropbox for business and Team Folders. 

 When using Dropbox for business remote: and remote:path/to/file will refer to your personal folder. 

 If you wish to see Team Folders you must use a leading / in the path, so rclone lsd remote:/ will refer to the root and show you all Team Folders and your User Folder. 

 You can then use team folders like this remote:/TeamFolder and remote:/TeamFolder/path/to/file. 

 A leading / for a Dropbox personal account will do nothing, but it will take an extra HTTP transaction so it should be avoided.
<h3>Modified time and Hashes</h3>Dropbox supports modified times, but the only way to set a modification time is to re-upload the file. 

 This means that if you uploaded your data with an older version of rclone which didn't support the v2 API and modified times, rclone will decide to upload all your old data to fix the modification times. If you don't want this to happen use --size-only or --checksum flag to stop it. 

 Dropbox supports its own hash type (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.dropbox.com/developers/reference/content-hash)">https://www.dropbox.com/developers/reference/content-hash)</a> which is checked for all transfers.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3><table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> NUL </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x00 </td><td ALIGN=center> 00 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> DEL </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x7F </td><td ALIGN=center> 21 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> \ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x5C </td><td ALIGN=center> 3C 
</td></tr> </table> 

 File names can also not end with the following characters. These only get replaced if they are the last character in the name: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> SP </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x20 </td><td ALIGN=center> 20 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to dropbox (Dropbox).
<h3>-dropbox-client-id</h3>OAuth Client Id Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_id
<dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-dropbox-client-secret</h3>OAuth Client Secret Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_secret
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DROPBOX_CLIENT_SECRET
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to dropbox (Dropbox).
<h3>-dropbox-token</h3>OAuth Access Token as a JSON blob.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DROPBOX_TOKEN
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-dropbox-auth-url</h3>Auth server URL. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: auth_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DROPBOX_AUTH_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-dropbox-token-url</h3>Token server url. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DROPBOX_TOKEN_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-dropbox-chunk-size</h3>Upload chunk size. (&lt; 150M). 

 Any files larger than this will be uploaded in chunks of this size. 

 Note that chunks are buffered in memory (one at a time) so rclone can deal with retries. Setting this larger will increase the speed slightly (at most 10% for 128MB in tests) at the cost of using more memory. It can be set smaller if you are tight on memory.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: chunk_size
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DROPBOX_CHUNK_SIZE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 48M</dl><h3>-dropbox-impersonate</h3>Impersonate this user when using a business account.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: impersonate
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DROPBOX_IMPERSONATE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-dropbox-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DROPBOX_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,BackSlash,Del,RightSpace,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>Note that Dropbox is case insensitive so you can't have a file called "Hello.doc" and one called "hello.doc". 

 There are some file names such as thumbs.db which Dropbox can't store. There is a full list of them in the "Ignored Files" section of this document (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.dropbox.com/en/help/145">https://www.dropbox.com/en/help/145</a>). Rclone will issue an error message File name disallowed - not uploading if it attempts to upload one of those file names, but the sync won't fail. 

 Some errors may occur if you try to sync copyright-protected files because Dropbox has its own copyright detector (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://techcrunch.com/2014/03/30/how-dropbox-knows-when-youre-sharing-copyrighted-stuff-without-actually-looking-at-your-stuff/)">https://techcrunch.com/2014/03/30/how-dropbox-knows-when-youre-sharing-copyrighted-stuff-without-actually-looking-at-your-stuff/)</a> that prevents this sort of file being downloaded. This will return the error ERROR : /path/to/your/file: Failed to copy: failed to open source object: path/restricted_content/. 

 If you have more than 10,000 files in a directory then rclone purge dropbox:dir will return the error Failed to purge: There are too many files involved in this operation. As a work-around do an rclone delete dropbox:dir followed by an rclone rmdir dropbox:dir.
<h3>Get your own Dropbox App ID</h3>When you use rclone with Dropbox in its default configuration you are using rclone's App ID. This is shared between all the rclone users. 

 Here is how to create your own Dropbox App ID for rclone:
<dl COMPACT><dt>1.
<dd>Log into the Dropbox App console (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps/create)">https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps/create)</a> with your Dropbox Account (It need not to be the same account as the Dropbox you want to access)
<dt>2.
<dd>Choose an API =&gt; Usually this should be Dropbox API
<dt>3.
<dd>Choose the type of access you want to use =&gt; Full Dropbox or App Folder
<dt>4.
<dd>Name your App. The app name is global, so you can't use rclone for example
<dt>5.
<dd>Click the button Create App
<dt>6.
<dd>Fill Redirect URIs as <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:53682/">http://localhost:53682/</a>
<dt>7.
<dd>Find the App key and App secret Use these values in rclone config to add a new remote or edit an existing remote.</dl><h3>Ftp</h3>FTP is the File Transfer Protocol. FTP support is provided using the github.com/jlaffaye/ftp (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://godoc.org/github.com/jlaffaye/ftp)">https://godoc.org/github.com/jlaffaye/ftp)</a> package. 

 Paths are specified as remote:path. If the path does not begin with a / it is relative to the home directory of the user. An empty path remote: refers to the user's home directory. 

 Here is an example of making an FTP configuration. First run
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process. An FTP remote only needs a host together with and a username and a password. With anonymous FTP server, you will need to use anonymous as username and your email address as the password.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one

r) Rename remote

s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config

[snip]

[snip]

 This remote is called remote and can now be used like this 

 See all directories in the home directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:path/to/directory</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:path/to/directory</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote directory, deleting any excess files in the directory.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:directory</pre></dl><h3>Modified time</h3>FTP does not support modified times. Any times you see on the server will be time of upload.
<h3>Checksums</h3>FTP does not support any checksums.
<h3>Usage without a config file</h3>An example how to use the ftp remote without a config file:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsf :ftp: --ftp-host=speedtest.tele2.net --ftp-user=anonymous --ftp-pass=`rclone obscure dummy`</pre></dl><h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>In addition to the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> the following characters are also replaced: 

 File names can also not end with the following characters. These only get replaced if they are the last character in the name: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> SP </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x20 </td><td ALIGN=center> 20 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Note that not all FTP servers can have all characters in file names, for example: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> FTP Server </td><td ALIGN=center> Forbidden characters 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=2><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> proftpd </td><td ALIGN=center> * 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> pureftpd </td><td ALIGN=center> \ [ ] 
</td></tr> </table><h3>Implicit TLS</h3>FTP supports implicit FTP over TLS servers (FTPS). This has to be enabled in the config for the remote. The default FTPS port is 990 so the port will likely have to be explicitly set in the config for the remote.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to ftp (FTP Connection).
<h3>-ftp-host</h3>FTP host to connect to
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: host
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_HOST
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"<a HREF="ftp://ftp.example.com">ftp.example.com</a>"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Connect to <a HREF="ftp://ftp.example.com">ftp.example.com</a></dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-ftp-user</h3>FTP username, leave blank for current username, $USER
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: user
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_USER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-ftp-port</h3>FTP port, leave blank to use default (21)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: port
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_PORT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-ftp-pass</h3>FTP password 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: pass
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_PASS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-ftp-tls</h3>Use FTPS over TLS (Implicit) When using implicit FTP over TLS the client will connect using TLS right from the start, which in turn breaks the compatibility with non-TLS-aware servers. This is usually served over port 990 rather than port 21. Cannot be used in combination with explicit FTP.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: tls
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_TLS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-ftp-explicit-tls</h3>Use FTP over TLS (Explicit) When using explicit FTP over TLS the client explicitly request security from the server in order to upgrade a plain text connection to an encrypted one. Cannot be used in combination with implicit FTP.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: explicit_tls
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_EXPLICIT_TLS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to ftp (FTP Connection).
<h3>-ftp-concurrency</h3>Maximum number of FTP simultaneous connections, 0 for unlimited
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: concurrency
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_CONCURRENCY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: int
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 0</dl><h3>-ftp-no-check-certificate</h3>Do not verify the TLS certificate of the server
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: no_check_certificate
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_NO_CHECK_CERTIFICATE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-ftp-disable-epsv</h3>Disable using EPSV even if server advertises support
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: disable_epsv
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_DISABLE_EPSV
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-ftp-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_FTP_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,Del,Ctl,RightSpace,Dot</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>Note that FTP does have its own implementation of : --dump headers, --dump bodies, --dump auth for debugging which isn't the same as the HTTP based backends - it has less fine grained control. 

 Note that --timeout isn't supported (but --contimeout is). 

 Note that --bind isn't supported. 

 FTP could support server side move but doesn't yet. 

 Note that the ftp backend does not support the ftp_proxy environment variable yet.
<h3>Google Cloud Storage</h3>Paths are specified as remote:bucket (or remote: for the lsd command.) You may put subdirectories in too, eg remote:bucket/path/to/dir. 

 The initial setup for google cloud storage involves getting a token from Google Cloud Storage which you need to do in your browser. rclone config walks you through it. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>

 Note that rclone runs a webserver on your local machine to collect the token as returned from Google if you use auto config mode. This only runs from the moment it opens your browser to the moment you get back the verification code. This is on <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/">http://127.0.0.1:53682/</a> and this it may require you to unblock it temporarily if you are running a host firewall, or use manual mode. 

 This remote is called remote and can now be used like this 

 See all the buckets in your project
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new bucket
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:bucket</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a bucket
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:bucket</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote bucket, deleting any excess files in the bucket.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:bucket</pre></dl><h3>Service Account support</h3>You can set up rclone with Google Cloud Storage in an unattended mode, i.e. not tied to a specific end-user Google account. This is useful when you want to synchronise files onto machines that don't have actively logged-in users, for example build machines. 

 To get credentials for Google Cloud Platform IAM Service Accounts (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-accounts">https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-accounts</a>), please head to the Service Account (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://console.cloud.google.com/permissions/serviceaccounts)">https://console.cloud.google.com/permissions/serviceaccounts)</a> section of the Google Developer Console. Service Accounts behave just like normal User permissions in Google Cloud Storage ACLs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control">https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control</a>), so you can limit their access (e.g. make them read only). After creating an account, a JSON file containing the Service Account's credentials will be downloaded onto your machines. These credentials are what rclone will use for authentication. 

 To use a Service Account instead of OAuth2 token flow, enter the path to your Service Account credentials at the service_account_file prompt and rclone won't use the browser based authentication flow. If you'd rather stuff the contents of the credentials file into the rclone config file, you can set service_account_credentials with the actual contents of the file instead, or set the equivalent environment variable.
<h3>Anonymous Access</h3>For downloads of objects that permit public access you can configure rclone to use anonymous access by setting anonymous to true. With unauthorized access you can't write or create files but only read or list those buckets and objects that have public read access.
<h3>Application Default Credentials</h3>If no other source of credentials is provided, rclone will fall back to Application Default Credentials (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://cloud.google.com/video-intelligence/docs/common/auth#authenticating_with_application_default_credentials)">https://cloud.google.com/video-intelligence/docs/common/auth#authenticating_with_application_default_credentials)</a> this is useful both when you already have configured authentication for your developer account, or in production when running on a google compute host. Note that if running in docker, you may need to run additional commands on your google compute machine - see this page (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://cloud.google.com/container-registry/docs/advanced-authentication#gcloud_as_a_docker_credential_helper">https://cloud.google.com/container-registry/docs/advanced-authentication#gcloud_as_a_docker_credential_helper</a>). 

 Note that in the case application default credentials are used, there is no need to explicitly configure a project number.
<h3>-fast-list</h3>This remote supports --fast-list which allows you to use fewer transactions in exchange for more memory. See the rclone docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)">https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)</a> for more details.
<h3>Custom upload headers</h3>You can set custom upload headers with the --header-upload flag. Google Cloud Storage supports the headers as described in the working with metadata documentation (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/gsutil/addlhelp/WorkingWithObjectMetadata)">https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/gsutil/addlhelp/WorkingWithObjectMetadata)</a>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Cache-Control
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Content-Disposition
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Content-Encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Content-Language
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Content-Type
<dt>&bull;
<dd>X-Goog-Meta-</dl>
 

 Eg --header-upload &quot;Content-Type text/potato&quot; 

 Note that the last of these is for setting custom metadata in the form --header-upload &quot;x-goog-meta-key: value&quot;
<h3>Modified time</h3>Google google cloud storage stores md5sums natively and rclone stores modification times as metadata on the object, under the "mtime" key in RFC3339 format accurate to 1ns.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3><table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> NUL </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x00 </td><td ALIGN=center> 00 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> LF </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x0A </td><td ALIGN=center> 0A 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> CR </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x0D </td><td ALIGN=center> 0D 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to google cloud storage (Google Cloud Storage (this is not Google Drive)).
<h3>-gcs-client-id</h3>OAuth Client Id Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_GCS_CLIENT_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-gcs-client-secret</h3>OAuth Client Secret Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_secret
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_GCS_CLIENT_SECRET
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-gcs-project-number</h3>Project number. Optional - needed only for list/create/delete buckets - see your developer console.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: project_number
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_GCS_PROJECT_NUMBER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-gcs-service-account-file</h3>Service Account Credentials JSON file path Leave blank normally. Needed only if you want use SA instead of interactive login. 

 Leading ~ will be expanded in the file name as will environment variables such as ${RCLONE_CONFIG_DIR}.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: service_account_file
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_GCS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-gcs-service-account-credentials</h3>Service Account Credentials JSON blob Leave blank normally. Needed only if you want use SA instead of interactive login.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: service_account_credentials
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_GCS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_CREDENTIALS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-gcs-anonymous</h3>Access public buckets and objects without credentials Set to `true' if you just want to download files and don't configure credentials.

</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to google cloud storage (Google Cloud Storage (this is not Google Drive)).
<h3>-gcs-token</h3>OAuth Access Token as a JSON blob.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token

<dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-gcs-token-url</h3>Token server url. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.

<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_GCS_TOKEN_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-gcs-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_GCS_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,CrLf,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Google Drive</h3>Paths are specified as drive:path 

 Drive paths may be as deep as required, eg drive:directory/subdirectory. 

 The initial setup for drive involves getting a token from Google drive which you need to do in your browser. rclone config walks you through it. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
r) Rename remote
c) Copy remote
s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config
n/r/c/s/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / Google Drive
 \ &quot;drive&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; drive
Google Application Client Id - leave blank normally.
client_id&gt;
Google Application Client Secret - leave blank normally.
client_secret&gt;
Scope that rclone should use when requesting access from drive.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
 1 / Full access all files, excluding Application Data Folder.
 \ &quot;drive&quot;
 2 / Read-only access to file metadata and file contents.
 \ &quot;drive.readonly&quot;
 / Access to files created by rclone only.
 3 | These are visible in the drive website.
 | File authorization is revoked when the user deauthorizes the app.
 \ &quot;drive.file&quot;
 / Allows read and write access to the Application Data folder.
 4 | This is not visible in the drive website.
 \ &quot;drive.appfolder&quot;
 / Allows read-only access to file metadata but
 5 | does not allow any access to read or download file content.
 \ &quot;drive.metadata.readonly&quot;
scope&gt; 1
ID of the root folder - leave blank normally. Fill in to access &quot;Computers&quot; folders. (see docs).
root_folder_id&gt; 
Service Account Credentials JSON file path - needed only if you want use SA instead of interactive login.
service_account_file&gt;
Remote config
Use auto config?
 * Say Y if not sure
 * Say N if you are working on a remote or headless machine or Y didn't work
y) Yes
n) No
y/n&gt; y
If your browser doesn't open automatically go to the following link: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth">http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth</a>
Log in and authorize rclone for access
Waiting for code...
Got code
Configure this as a team drive?
y) Yes
n) No
y/n&gt; n
--------------------
[remote]
client_id = 
client_secret = 
scope = drive
root_folder_id = 
service_account_file =
token = {&quot;access_token&quot;:&quot;XXX&quot;,&quot;token_type&quot;:&quot;Bearer&quot;,&quot;refresh_token&quot;:&quot;XXX&quot;,&quot;expiry&quot;:&quot;2014-03-16T13:57:58.955387075Z&quot;}
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 Note that rclone runs a webserver on your local machine to collect the token as returned from Google if you use auto config mode. This only runs from the moment it opens your browser to the moment you get back the verification code. This is on <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/">http://127.0.0.1:53682/</a> and this it may require you to unblock it temporarily if you are running a host firewall, or use manual mode. 

 You can then use it like this, 

 List directories in top level of your drive
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your drive
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to a drive directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Scopes</h3>Rclone allows you to select which scope you would like for rclone to use. This changes what type of token is granted to rclone. The scopes are defined here (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://developers.google.com/drive/v3/web/about-auth">https://developers.google.com/drive/v3/web/about-auth</a>). 

 The scope are
<h3>drive</h3>This is the default scope and allows full access to all files, except for the Application Data Folder (see below). 

 Choose this one if you aren't sure.
<h3>drive.readonly</h3>This allows read only access to all files. Files may be listed and downloaded but not uploaded, renamed or deleted.
<h3>drive.file</h3>With this scope rclone can read/view/modify only those files and folders it creates. 

 So if you uploaded files to drive via the web interface (or any other means) they will not be visible to rclone. 

 This can be useful if you are using rclone to backup data and you want to be sure confidential data on your drive is not visible to rclone. 

 Files created with this scope are visible in the web interface.
<h3>drive.appfolder</h3>This gives rclone its own private area to store files. Rclone will not be able to see any other files on your drive and you won't be able to see rclone's files from the web interface either.
<h3>drive.metadata.readonly</h3>This allows read only access to file names only. It does not allow rclone to download or upload data, or rename or delete files or directories.
<h3>Root folder ID</h3>You can set the root_folder_id for rclone. This is the directory (identified by its Folder ID) that rclone considers to be the root of your drive. 

 Normally you will leave this blank and rclone will determine the correct root to use itself. 

 However you can set this to restrict rclone to a specific folder hierarchy or to access data within the "Computers" tab on the drive web interface (where files from Google's Backup and Sync desktop program go). 

 In order to do this you will have to find the Folder ID of the directory you wish rclone to display. This will be the last segment of the URL when you open the relevant folder in the drive web interface. 

 So if the folder you want rclone to use has a URL which looks like <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyfxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxKHCh">https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyfxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxKHCh</a> in the browser, then you use 1XyfxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxKHCh as the root_folder_id in the config. 

 NB folders under the "Computers" tab seem to be read only (drive gives a 500 error) when using rclone. 

 There doesn't appear to be an API to discover the folder IDs of the "Computers" tab - please contact us if you know otherwise! 

 Note also that rclone can't access any data under the "Backups" tab on the google drive web interface yet.
<h3>Service Account support</h3>You can set up rclone with Google Drive in an unattended mode, i.e. not tied to a specific end-user Google account. This is useful when you want to synchronise files onto machines that don't have actively logged-in users, for example build machines. 

 To use a Service Account instead of OAuth2 token flow, enter the path to your Service Account credentials at the service_account_file prompt during rclone config and rclone won't use the browser based authentication flow. If you'd rather stuff the contents of the credentials file into the rclone config file, you can set service_account_credentials with the actual contents of the file instead, or set the equivalent environment variable.
<h3>Use case - Google Apps/G-suite account and individual Drive</h3>Let's say that you are the administrator of a Google Apps (old) or G-suite account. The goal is to store data on an individual's Drive account, who IS a member of the domain. We'll call the domain example.com, and the user foo [at] example.com. 

 There's a few steps we need to go through to accomplish this:
<h3>1. Create a service account for example.com</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>To create a service account and obtain its credentials, go to the Google Developer Console (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://console.developers.google.com">https://console.developers.google.com</a>).
<dt>&bull;
<dd>You must have a project - create one if you don't.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Then go to "IAM &amp; admin" -&gt; "Service Accounts".
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Use the "Create Credentials" button. Fill in "Service account name" with something that identifies your client. "Role" can be empty.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Tick "Furnish a new private key" - select "Key type JSON".
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Tick "Enable G Suite Domain-wide Delegation". This option makes "impersonation" possible, as documented here: Delegating domain-wide authority to the service account (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority)">https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority)</a>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>These credentials are what rclone will use for authentication. If you ever need to remove access, press the "Delete service account key" button.</dl><h3>2. Allowing API access to example.com Google Drive</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Go to example.com's admin console
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Go into "Security" (or use the search bar)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Select "Show more" and then "Advanced settings"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Select "Manage API client access" in the "Authentication" section
<dt>&bull;
<dd>In the "Client Name" field enter the service account's "Client ID" - this can be found in the Developer Console under "IAM &amp; Admin" -&gt; "Service Accounts", then "View Client ID" for the newly created service account. It is a ~21 character numerical string.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>In the next field, "One or More API Scopes", enter <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive">https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive</a> to grant access to Google Drive specifically.</dl><h3>3. Configure rclone, assuming a new install</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config
n/s/q&gt; n # New
name&gt;gdrive # Gdrive is an example name
Storage&gt; # Select the number shown for Google Drive
client_id&gt; # Can be left blank
client_secret&gt; # Can be left blank
scope&gt; # Select your scope, 1 for example
root_folder_id&gt; # Can be left blank
service_account_file&gt; /home/foo/myJSONfile.json # This is where the JSON file goes!
y/n&gt; # Auto config, y</pre></dl><h3>4. Verify that it's working</h3><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>rclone -v --drive-impersonate foo [at] example.com lsf gdrive:backup
<dt>&bull;
<dd>The arguments do:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>-v - verbose logging
<dt>&bull;
<dd>--drive-impersonate foo [at] example.com - this is what does the magic, pretending to be user foo.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>lsf - list files in a parsing friendly way
<dt>&bull;
<dd>gdrive:backup - use the remote called gdrive, work in the folder named backup.</dl></dl>
</dl>
 

 Note: in case you configured a specific root folder on gdrive and rclone is unable to access the contents of that folder when using --drive-impersonate, do this instead: - in the gdrive web interface, share your root folder with the user/email of the new Service Account you created/selected at step #1 - use rclone without specifying the --drive-impersonate option, like this: rclone -v foo [at] example.com lsf gdrive:backup
<h3>Team drives</h3>If you want to configure the remote to point to a Google Team Drive then answer y to the question Configure this as a team drive?. 

 This will fetch the list of Team Drives from google and allow you to configure which one you want to use. You can also type in a team drive ID if you prefer. 

 For example:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Configure this as a team drive?
y) Yes
n) No
y/n&gt; y
Fetching team drive list...
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
 1 / Rclone Test
 \ &quot;xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx&quot;
 2 / Rclone Test 2
 \ &quot;yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy&quot;
 3 / Rclone Test 3
 \ &quot;zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz&quot;
Enter a Team Drive ID&gt; 1
--------------------
[remote]
client_id =
client_secret =
token = {&quot;AccessToken&quot;:&quot;xxxx.x.xxxxx_xxxxxxxxxxx_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx&quot;,&quot;RefreshToken&quot;:&quot;1/xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx&quot;,&quot;Expiry&quot;:&quot;2014-03-16T13:57:58.955387075Z&quot;,&quot;Extra&quot;:null}
team_drive = xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl><h3>-fast-list</h3>This remote supports --fast-list which allows you to use fewer transactions in exchange for more memory. See the rclone docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)">https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)</a> for more details. 

 It does this by combining multiple list calls into a single API request. 

 This works by combining many '%s' in parents filters into one expression. To list the contents of directories a, b and c, the following requests will be send by the regular List function:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>trashed=false and 'a' in parents
trashed=false and 'b' in parents
trashed=false and 'c' in parents</pre></dl>
 

 These can now be combined into a single request:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>trashed=false and ('a' in parents or 'b' in parents or 'c' in parents)</pre></dl>
 

 The implementation of ListR will put up to 50 parents filters into one request. It will use the --checkers value to specify the number of requests to run in parallel. 

 In tests, these batch requests were up to 20x faster than the regular method. Running the following command against different sized folders gives:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsjson -vv -R --checkers=6 gdrive:folder</pre></dl>
 

 small folder (220 directories, 700 files):
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>without --fast-list: 38s
<dt>&bull;
<dd>with --fast-list: 10s</dl>
 

 large folder (10600 directories, 39000 files):
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>without --fast-list: 22:05 min
<dt>&bull;
<dd>with --fast-list: 58s</dl><h3>Modified time</h3>Google drive stores modification times accurate to 1 ms.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>Only Invalid UTF-8 bytes will be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings. 

 In contrast to other backends, / can also be used in names and . or .. are valid names.
<h3>Revisions</h3>Google drive stores revisions of files. When you upload a change to an existing file to google drive using rclone it will create a new revision of that file. 

 Revisions follow the standard google policy which at time of writing was
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>They are deleted after 30 days or 100 revisions (whatever comes first).
<dt>&bull;
<dd>They do not count towards a user storage quota.</dl><h3>Deleting files</h3>By default rclone will send all files to the trash when deleting files. If deleting them permanently is required then use the --drive-use-trash=false flag, or set the equivalent environment variable.
<h3>Shortcuts</h3>In March 2020 Google introduced a new feature in Google Drive called drive shortcuts (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://support.google.com/drive/answer/9700156)">https://support.google.com/drive/answer/9700156)</a> (API (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://developers.google.com/drive/api/v3/shortcuts)">https://developers.google.com/drive/api/v3/shortcuts)</a>). These will (by September 2020) replace the ability for files or folders to be in multiple folders at once (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/g-suite/simplifying-google-drives-folder-structure-and-sharing-models">https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/g-suite/simplifying-google-drives-folder-structure-and-sharing-models</a>). 

 Shortcuts are files that link to other files on Google Drive somewhat like a symlink in unix, except they point to the underlying file data (eg the inode in unix terms) so they don't break if the source is renamed or moved about. 

 Be default rclone treats these as follows. 

 For shortcuts pointing to files:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>When listing a file shortcut appears as the destination file.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When downloading the contents of the destination file is downloaded.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When updating shortcut file with a non shortcut file, the shortcut is removed then a new file is uploaded in place of the shortcut.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When server side moving (renaming) the shortcut is renamed, not the destination file.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When server side copying the shortcut is copied, not the contents of the shortcut.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When deleting the shortcut is deleted not the linked file.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When setting the modification time, the modification time of the linked file will be set.</dl>
 

 For shortcuts pointing to folders:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>When listing the shortcut appears as a folder and that folder will contain the contents of the linked folder appear (including any sub folders)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When downloading the contents of the linked folder and sub contents are downloaded
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When uploading to a shortcut folder the file will be placed in the linked folder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When server side moving (renaming) the shortcut is renamed, not the destination folder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When server side copying the contents of the linked folder is copied, not the shortcut.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>When deleting with rclone rmdir or rclone purge the shortcut is deleted not the linked folder.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>NB When deleting with rclone remove or rclone mount the contents of the linked folder will be deleted.</dl>
 

 The rclone backend (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_backend/)">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_backend/)</a> command can be used to create shortcuts. 

 Shortcuts can be completely ignored with the --drive-skip-shortcuts flag or the corresponding skip_shortcuts configuration setting.
<h3>Emptying trash</h3>If you wish to empty your trash you can use the rclone cleanup remote: command which will permanently delete all your trashed files. This command does not take any path arguments. 

 Note that Google Drive takes some time (minutes to days) to empty the trash even though the command returns within a few seconds. No output is echoed, so there will be no confirmation even using -v or -vv.
<h3>Quota information</h3>To view your current quota you can use the rclone about remote: command which will display your usage limit (quota), the usage in Google Drive, the size of all files in the Trash and the space used by other Google services such as Gmail. This command does not take any path arguments.
<h3>Import/Export of google documents</h3>Google documents can be exported from and uploaded to Google Drive. 

 When rclone downloads a Google doc it chooses a format to download depending upon the --drive-export-formats setting. By default the export formats are docx,xlsx,pptx,svg which are a sensible default for an editable document. 

 When choosing a format, rclone runs down the list provided in order and chooses the first file format the doc can be exported as from the list. If the file can't be exported to a format on the formats list, then rclone will choose a format from the default list. 

 If you prefer an archive copy then you might use --drive-export-formats pdf, or if you prefer openoffice/libreoffice formats you might use --drive-export-formats ods,odt,odp. 

 Note that rclone adds the extension to the google doc, so if it is called My Spreadsheet on google docs, it will be exported as My Spreadsheet.xlsx or My Spreadsheet.pdf etc. 

 When importing files into Google Drive, rclone will convert all files with an extension in --drive-import-formats to their associated document type. rclone will not convert any files by default, since the conversion is lossy process. 

 The conversion must result in a file with the same extension when the --drive-export-formats rules are applied to the uploaded document. 

 Here are some examples for allowed and prohibited conversions. 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> export-formats </td><td> import-formats </td><td> Upload Ext </td><td> Document Ext </td><td> Allowed 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=5><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> odt </td><td> odt </td><td> odt </td><td> odt </td><td> Yes 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> odt </td><td> docx,odt </td><td> odt </td><td> odt </td><td> Yes 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> </td><td> docx </td><td> docx </td><td> docx </td><td> Yes 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> </td><td> odt </td><td> odt </td><td> docx </td><td> No 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> odt,docx </td><td> docx,odt </td><td> docx </td><td> odt </td><td> No 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> docx,odt </td><td> docx,odt </td><td> docx </td><td> docx </td><td> Yes 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> docx,odt </td><td> docx,odt </td><td> odt </td><td> docx </td><td> No 
</td></tr> </table> 

 This limitation can be disabled by specifying --drive-allow-import-name-change. When using this flag, rclone can convert multiple files types resulting in the same document type at once, eg with --drive-import-formats docx,odt,txt, all files having these extension would result in a document represented as a docx file. This brings the additional risk of overwriting a document, if multiple files have the same stem. Many rclone operations will not handle this name change in any way. They assume an equal name when copying files and might copy the file again or delete them when the name changes. 

 Here are the possible export extensions with their corresponding mime types. Most of these can also be used for importing, but there more that are not listed here. Some of these additional ones might only be available when the operating system provides the correct MIME type entries. 

 This list can be changed by Google Drive at any time and might not represent the currently available conversions. 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Extension </td><td> Mime Type </td><td> Description 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> csv </td><td> text/csv </td><td> Standard CSV format for Spreadsheets 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> docx </td><td> application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document </td><td> Microsoft Office Document 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> epub </td><td> application/epub+zip </td><td> E-book format 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> html </td><td> text/html </td><td> An HTML Document 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> jpg </td><td> image/jpeg </td><td> A JPEG Image File 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> json </td><td> application/vnd.google-apps.script+json </td><td> JSON Text Format 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> odp </td><td> application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation </td><td> Openoffice Presentation 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> ods </td><td> application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet </td><td> Openoffice Spreadsheet 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> ods </td><td> application/x-vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet </td><td> Openoffice Spreadsheet 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> odt </td><td> application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text </td><td> Openoffice Document 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> pdf </td><td> application/pdf </td><td> Adobe PDF Format 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> png </td><td> image/png </td><td> PNG Image Format 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> pptx </td><td> application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation </td><td> Microsoft Office Powerpoint 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> rtf </td><td> application/rtf </td><td> Rich Text Format 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> svg </td><td> image/svg+xml </td><td> Scalable Vector Graphics Format 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> tsv </td><td> text/tab-separated-values </td><td> Standard TSV format for spreadsheets 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> txt </td><td> text/plain </td><td> Plain Text 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> xlsx </td><td> application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet </td><td> Microsoft Office Spreadsheet 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> zip </td><td> application/zip </td><td> A ZIP file of HTML, Images CSS 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Google documents can also be exported as link files. These files will open a browser window for the Google Docs website of that document when opened. The link file extension has to be specified as a --drive-export-formats parameter. They will match all available Google Documents. 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Extension </td><td> Description </td><td> OS Support 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> desktop </td><td> freedesktop.org specified desktop entry </td><td> Linux 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> link.html </td><td> An HTML Document with a redirect </td><td> All 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> url </td><td> INI style link file </td><td> macOS, Windows 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> webloc </td><td> macOS specific XML format </td><td> macOS 
</td></tr> </table><h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to drive (Google Drive).
<h3>-drive-client-id</h3>Google Application Client Id Setting your own is recommended. See <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/drive/#making-your-own-client-id">https://rclone.org/drive/#making-your-own-client-id</a> for how to create your own. If you leave this blank, it will use an internal key which is low performance.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DRIVE_CLIENT_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-drive-client-secret</h3>OAuth Client Secret Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_secret
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DRIVE_CLIENT_SECRET
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-drive-scope</h3>Scope that rclone should use when requesting access from drive.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: scope
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DRIVE_SCOPE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"drive"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Full access all files, excluding Application Data Folder.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"drive.readonly"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Read-only access to file metadata and file contents.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"drive.file"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Access to files created by rclone only.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>These are visible in the drive website.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>File authorization is revoked when the user deauthorizes the app.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"drive.appfolder"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Allows read and write access to the Application Data folder.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>This is not visible in the drive website.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"drive.metadata.readonly"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Allows read-only access to file metadata but
<dt>&bull;
<dd>does not allow any access to read or download file content.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-drive-root-folder-id</h3>ID of the root folder Leave blank normally. 

 Fill in to access "Computers" folders (see docs), or for rclone to use a non root folder as its starting point.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: root_folder_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DRIVE_ROOT_FOLDER_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-drive-service-account-file</h3>Service Account Credentials JSON file path Leave blank normally. Needed only if you want use SA instead of interactive login. 

 Leading ~ will be expanded in the file name as will environment variables such as ${RCLONE_CONFIG_DIR}.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: service_account_file
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DRIVE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-drive-alternate-export</h3>Deprecated: no longer needed
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: alternate_export
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DRIVE_ALTERNATE_EXPORT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to drive (Google Drive).
<h3>-drive-token</h3>OAuth Access Token as a JSON blob.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_DRIVE_TOKEN
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-drive-auth-url</h3>Auth server URL. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
