 Configuration of this backend does not require a local web browser. You can use the configured backend as shown below: 

 See top level directories
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:directory</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:directory</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote path, deleting any excess files in the path.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:directory</pre></dl><h3>Modified time</h3>Files support a modification time attribute with up to 1 second precision. Directories do not have a modification time, which is shown as "Jan 1 1970".
<h3>Hash checksums</h3>Hash sums use a custom Mail.ru algorithm based on SHA1. If file size is less than or equal to the SHA1 block size (20 bytes), its hash is simply its data right-padded with zero bytes. Hash sum of a larger file is computed as a SHA1 sum of the file data bytes concatenated with a decimal representation of the data length.
<h3>Emptying Trash</h3>Removing a file or directory actually moves it to the trash, which is not visible to rclone but can be seen in a web browser. The trashed file still occupies part of total quota. If you wish to empty your trash and free some quota, you can use the rclone cleanup remote: command, which will permanently delete all your trashed files. This command does not take any path arguments.
<h3>Quota information</h3>To view your current quota you can use the rclone about remote: command which will display your usage limit (quota) and the current usage.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>In addition to the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> the following characters are also replaced: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &quot; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x22 </td><td ALIGN=center> 02 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> * </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2A </td><td ALIGN=center> 0A 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> : </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3A </td><td ALIGN=center> 1A 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &lt; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3C </td><td ALIGN=center> 1C 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &gt; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3E </td><td ALIGN=center> 1E 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> ? </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3F </td><td ALIGN=center> 1F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> \ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x5C </td><td ALIGN=center> 3C 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> | </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x7C </td><td ALIGN=center> 5C 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Limitations</h3>File size limits depend on your account. A single file size is limited by 2G for a free account and unlimited for paid tariffs. Please refer to the Mail.ru site for the total uploaded size limits. 

 Note that Mailru is case insensitive so you can't have a file called "Hello.doc" and one called "hello.doc".
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to mailru (Mail.ru Cloud).
<h3>-mailru-user</h3>User name (usually email)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: user
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_USER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-mailru-pass</h3>Password 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: pass
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_PASS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-mailru-speedup-enable</h3>Skip full upload if there is another file with same data hash. This feature is called "speedup" or "put by hash". It is especially efficient in case of generally available files like popular books, video or audio clips, because files are searched by hash in all accounts of all mailru users. Please note that rclone may need local memory and disk space to calculate content hash in advance and decide whether full upload is required. Also, if rclone does not know file size in advance (e.g. in case of streaming or partial uploads), it will not even try this optimization.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: speedup_enable
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_SPEEDUP_ENABLE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: true
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"true"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Enable</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"false"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Disable</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to mailru (Mail.ru Cloud).
<h3>-mailru-speedup-file-patterns</h3>Comma separated list of file name patterns eligible for speedup (put by hash). Patterns are case insensitive and can contain '*' or `?' meta characters.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: speedup_file_patterns
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_SPEEDUP_FILE_PATTERNS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: ".mkv,.avi,.mp4,.mp3,.zip,.gz,.rar,.pdf"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>&quot;&quot;
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Empty list completely disables speedup (put by hash).</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>&quot;*&quot;
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>All files will be attempted for speedup.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>".mkv,.avi,.mp4,.mp3"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Only common audio/video files will be tried for put by hash.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>".zip,.gz,.rar,.pdf"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Only common archives or PDF books will be tried for speedup.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-mailru-speedup-max-disk</h3>This option allows you to disable speedup (put by hash) for large files (because preliminary hashing can exhaust you RAM or disk space)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: speedup_max_disk
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_SPEEDUP_MAX_DISK
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 3G
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"0"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Completely disable speedup (put by hash).</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"1G"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Files larger than 1Gb will be uploaded directly.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"3G"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Choose this option if you have less than 3Gb free on local disk.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-mailru-speedup-max-memory</h3>Files larger than the size given below will always be hashed on disk.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: speedup_max_memory
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_SPEEDUP_MAX_MEMORY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 32M
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"0"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Preliminary hashing will always be done in a temporary disk location.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"32M"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Do not dedicate more than 32Mb RAM for preliminary hashing.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"256M"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>You have at most 256Mb RAM free for hash calculations.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-mailru-check-hash</h3>What should copy do if file checksum is mismatched or invalid
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: check_hash
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_CHECK_HASH
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: true
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"true"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Fail with error.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"false"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Ignore and continue.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-mailru-user-agent</h3>HTTP user agent used internally by client. Defaults to "rclone/VERSION" or "-user-agent" provided on command line.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: user_agent
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_USER_AGENT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-mailru-quirks</h3>Comma separated list of internal maintenance flags. This option must not be used by an ordinary user. It is intended only to facilitate remote troubleshooting of backend issues. Strict meaning of flags is not documented and not guaranteed to persist between releases. Quirks will be removed when the backend grows stable. Supported quirks: atomicmkdir binlist gzip insecure retry400
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: quirks
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_QUIRKS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-mailru-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MAILRU_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,LtGt,DoubleQuote,Colon,Question,Asterisk,Pipe,BackSlash,Del,Ctl,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Mega</h3>Mega (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://mega.nz/)">https://mega.nz/)</a> is a cloud storage and file hosting service known for its security feature where all files are encrypted locally before they are uploaded. This prevents anyone (including employees of Mega) from accessing the files without knowledge of the key used for encryption. 

 This is an rclone backend for Mega which supports the file transfer features of Mega using the same client side encryption. 

 Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config
n/s/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / Mega
 \ &quot;mega&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; mega
User name
user&gt; you [at] example.com
Password.
y) Yes type in my own password
g) Generate random password
n) No leave this optional password blank
y/g/n&gt; y
Enter the password:
password:
Confirm the password:
password:
Remote config
--------------------
[remote]
type = mega
user = you [at] example.com
pass = *** ENCRYPTED ***
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 NOTE: The encryption keys need to have been already generated after a regular login via the browser, otherwise attempting to use the credentials in rclone will fail. 

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 List directories in top level of your Mega
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your Mega
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to an Mega directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Modified time and hashes</h3>Mega does not support modification times or hashes yet.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3><table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> NUL </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x00 </td><td ALIGN=center> 00 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Duplicated files</h3>Mega can have two files with exactly the same name and path (unlike a normal file system). 

 Duplicated files cause problems with the syncing and you will see messages in the log about duplicates. 

 Use rclone dedupe to fix duplicated files.
<h3>Failure to log-in</h3>Mega remotes seem to get blocked (reject logins) under "heavy use". We haven't worked out the exact blocking rules but it seems to be related to fast paced, successive rclone commands. 

 For example, executing this command 90 times in a row rclone link remote:file will cause the remote to become "blocked". This is not an abnormal situation, for example if you wish to get the public links of a directory with hundred of files... After more or less a week, the remote will remote accept rclone logins normally again. 

 You can mitigate this issue by mounting the remote it with rclone mount. This will log-in when mounting and a log-out when unmounting only. You can also run rclone rcd and then use rclone rc to run the commands over the API to avoid logging in each time. 

 Rclone does not currently close mega sessions (you can see them in the web interface), however closing the sessions does not solve the issue. 

 If you space rclone commands by 3 seconds it will avoid blocking the remote. We haven't identified the exact blocking rules, so perhaps one could execute the command 80 times without waiting and avoid blocking by waiting 3 seconds, then continuing... 

 Note that this has been observed by trial and error and might not be set in stone. 

 Other tools seem not to produce this blocking effect, as they use a different working approach (state-based, using sessionIDs instead of log-in) which isn't compatible with the current stateless rclone approach. 

 Note that once blocked, the use of other tools (such as megacmd) is not a sure workaround: following megacmd login times have been observed in succession for blocked remote: 7 minutes, 20 min, 30min, 30 min, 30min. Web access looks unaffected though. 

 Investigation is continuing in relation to workarounds based on timeouts, pacers, retrials and tpslimits - if you discover something relevant, please post on the forum. 

 So, if rclone was working nicely and suddenly you are unable to log-in and you are sure the user and the password are correct, likely you have got the remote blocked for a while.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to mega (Mega).
<h3>-mega-user</h3>User name
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: user
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MEGA_USER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-mega-pass</h3>Password. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: pass
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MEGA_PASS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to mega (Mega).
<h3>-mega-debug</h3>Output more debug from Mega. 

 If this flag is set (along with -vv) it will print further debugging information from the mega backend.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: debug
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MEGA_DEBUG
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-mega-hard-delete</h3>Delete files permanently rather than putting them into the trash. 

 Normally the mega backend will put all deletions into the trash rather than permanently deleting them. If you specify this then rclone will permanently delete objects instead.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: hard_delete
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MEGA_HARD_DELETE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-mega-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_MEGA_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>This backend uses the go-mega go library (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/t3rm1n4l/go-mega)">https://github.com/t3rm1n4l/go-mega)</a> which is an opensource go library implementing the Mega API. There doesn't appear to be any documentation for the mega protocol beyond the mega C++ SDK (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/meganz/sdk)">https://github.com/meganz/sdk)</a> source code so there are likely quite a few errors still remaining in this library. 

 Mega allows duplicate files which may confuse rclone.
<h3>Memory</h3>The memory backend is an in RAM backend. It does not persist its data - use the local backend for that. 

 The memory backend behaves like a bucket based remote (eg like s3). Because it has no parameters you can just use it with the :memory: remote name. 

 You can configure it as a remote like this with rclone config too if you want to:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config
n/s/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Enter a string value. Press Enter for the default (&quot;&quot;).
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / Memory
 \ &quot;memory&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; memory
** See help for memory backend at: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/memory/">https://rclone.org/memory/</a> **
Remote config
--------------------
[remote]
type = memory
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK (default)
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 Because the memory backend isn't persistent it is most useful for testing or with an rclone server or rclone mount, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mount :memory: /mnt/tmp
rclone serve webdav :memory:
rclone serve sftp :memory:</pre></dl><h3>Modified time and hashes</h3>The memory backend supports MD5 hashes and modification times accurate to 1 nS.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>The memory backend replaces the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters</a>).
<h3>Microsoft Azure Blob Storage</h3>Paths are specified as remote:container (or remote: for the lsd command.) You may put subdirectories in too, eg remote:container/path/to/dir. 

 Here is an example of making a Microsoft Azure Blob Storage configuration. For a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote

--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote

 See all containers
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new container
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:container</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a container
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:container</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote container, deleting any excess files in the container.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:container</pre></dl><h3>-fast-list</h3>This remote supports --fast-list which allows you to use fewer transactions in exchange for more memory. See the rclone docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)">https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)</a> for more details.
<h3>Modified time</h3>The modified time is stored as metadata on the object with the mtime key. It is stored using RFC3339 Format time with nanosecond precision. The metadata is supplied during directory listings so there is no overhead to using it.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>In addition to the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> the following characters are also replaced: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> \ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x5C </td><td ALIGN=center> 3C 
</td></tr> </table> 

 File names can also not end with the following characters. These only get replaced if they are the last character in the name: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> . </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2E </td><td ALIGN=center> 0E 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Hashes</h3>MD5 hashes are stored with blobs. However blobs that were uploaded in chunks only have an MD5 if the source remote was capable of MD5 hashes, eg the local disk.
<h3>Authenticating with Azure Blob Storage</h3>Rclone has 3 ways of authenticating with Azure Blob Storage:
<h3>Account and Key</h3>This is the most straight forward and least flexible way. Just fill in the account and key lines and leave the rest blank.
<h3>Sas Url</h3>This can be an account level SAS URL or container level SAS URL. 

 To use it leave account, key blank and fill in sas_url. 

 An account level SAS URL or container level SAS URL can be obtained from the Azure portal or the Azure Storage Explorer. To get a container level SAS URL right click on a container in the Azure Blob explorer in the Azure portal. 

 If you use a container level SAS URL, rclone operations are permitted only on a particular container, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls azureblob:container</pre></dl>
 

 You can also list the single container from the root. This will only show the container specified by the SAS URL.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>$ rclone lsd azureblob:
container/</pre></dl>
 

 Note that you can't see or access any other containers - this will fail
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls azureblob:othercontainer</pre></dl>
 

 Container level SAS URLs are useful for temporarily allowing third parties access to a single container or putting credentials into an untrusted environment such as a CI build server.
<h3>Multipart uploads</h3>Rclone supports multipart uploads with Azure Blob storage. Files bigger than 256MB will be uploaded using chunked upload by default. 

 The files will be uploaded in parallel in 4MB chunks (by default). Note that these chunks are buffered in memory and there may be up to --transfers of them being uploaded at once. 

 Files can't be split into more than 50,000 chunks so by default, so the largest file that can be uploaded with 4MB chunk size is 195GB. Above this rclone will double the chunk size until it creates less than 50,000 chunks. By default this will mean a maximum file size of 3.2TB can be uploaded. This can be raised to 5TB using --azureblob-chunk-size 100M. 

 Note that rclone doesn't commit the block list until the end of the upload which means that there is a limit of 9.5TB of multipart uploads in progress as Azure won't allow more than that amount of uncommitted blocks.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to azureblob (Microsoft Azure Blob Storage).
<h3>-azureblob-account</h3>Storage Account Name (leave blank to use SAS URL or Emulator)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: account
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_ACCOUNT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-azureblob-key</h3>Storage Account Key (leave blank to use SAS URL or Emulator)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: key
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_KEY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-azureblob-sas-url</h3>SAS URL for container level access only (leave blank if using account/key or Emulator)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: sas_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_SAS_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-azureblob-use-emulator</h3>Uses local storage emulator if provided as `true' (leave blank if using real azure storage endpoint)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: use_emulator
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_USE_EMULATOR
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to azureblob (Microsoft Azure Blob Storage).
<h3>-azureblob-endpoint</h3>Endpoint for the service Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: endpoint
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_ENDPOINT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-azureblob-upload-cutoff</h3>Cutoff for switching to chunked upload (&lt;= 256MB).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: upload_cutoff
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_UPLOAD_CUTOFF
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 256M</dl><h3>-azureblob-chunk-size</h3>Upload chunk size (&lt;= 100MB). 

 Note that this is stored in memory and there may be up to "-transfers" chunks stored at once in memory.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: chunk_size
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_CHUNK_SIZE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 4M</dl><h3>-azureblob-list-chunk</h3>Size of blob list. 

 This sets the number of blobs requested in each listing chunk. Default is the maximum, 5000. "List blobs" requests are permitted 2 minutes per megabyte to complete. If an operation is taking longer than 2 minutes per megabyte on average, it will time out ( source (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/setting-timeouts-for-blob-service-operations#exceptions-to-default-timeout-interval)">https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/setting-timeouts-for-blob-service-operations#exceptions-to-default-timeout-interval)</a> ). This can be used to limit the number of blobs items to return, to avoid the time out.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: list_chunk
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_LIST_CHUNK
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: int
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 5000</dl><h3>-azureblob-access-tier</h3>Access tier of blob: hot, cool or archive. 

 Archived blobs can be restored by setting access tier to hot or cool. Leave blank if you intend to use default access tier, which is set at account level 

 If there is no "access tier" specified, rclone doesn't apply any tier. rclone performs "Set Tier" operation on blobs while uploading, if objects are not modified, specifying "access tier" to new one will have no effect. If blobs are in "archive tier" at remote, trying to perform data transfer operations from remote will not be allowed. User should first restore by tiering blob to "Hot" or "Cool".
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: access_tier
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_ACCESS_TIER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-azureblob-disable-checksum</h3>Don't store MD5 checksum with object metadata. 

 Normally rclone will calculate the MD5 checksum of the input before uploading it so it can add it to metadata on the object. This is great for data integrity checking but can cause long delays for large files to start uploading.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: disable_checksum
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_DISABLE_CHECKSUM
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-azureblob-memory-pool-flush-time</h3>How often internal memory buffer pools will be flushed. Uploads which requires additional buffers (f.e multipart) will use memory pool for allocations. This option controls how often unused buffers will be removed from the pool.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: memory_pool_flush_time
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_MEMORY_POOL_FLUSH_TIME
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: Duration
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 1m0s</dl><h3>-azureblob-memory-pool-use-mmap</h3>Whether to use mmap buffers in internal memory pool.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: memory_pool_use_mmap
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_MEMORY_POOL_USE_MMAP
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-azureblob-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_AZUREBLOB_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,BackSlash,Del,Ctl,RightPeriod,InvalidUtf8</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>MD5 sums are only uploaded with chunked files if the source has an MD5 sum. This will always be the case for a local to azure copy.
<h3>Azure Storage Emulator Support</h3>You can test rclone with storage emulator locally, to do this make sure azure storage emulator installed locally and set up a new remote with rclone config follow instructions described in introduction, set use_emulator config as true, you do not need to provide default account name or key if using emulator.
<h3>Microsoft OneDrive</h3>Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 The initial setup for OneDrive involves getting a token from Microsoft which you need to do in your browser. rclone config walks you through it. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:

 See the remote setup docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)">https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)</a> for how to set it up on a machine with no Internet browser available. 

 Note that rclone runs a webserver on your local machine to collect the token as returned from Microsoft. This only runs from the moment it opens your browser to the moment you get back the verification code. This is on <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/">http://127.0.0.1:53682/</a> and this it may require you to unblock it temporarily if you are running a host firewall. 

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 List directories in top level of your OneDrive
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your OneDrive
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to an OneDrive directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Getting your own Client ID and Key</h3>You can use your own Client ID if the default (client_id left blank) one doesn't work for you or you see lots of throttling. The default Client ID and Key is shared by all rclone users when performing requests. 

 If you are having problems with them (E.g., seeing a lot of throttling), you can get your own Client ID and Key by following the steps below:
<dl COMPACT><dt>1.
<dd>Open <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade">https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade</a> and then click New registration.
<dt>2.
<dd>Enter a name for your app, choose account type Accounts in any organizational directory (Any Azure AD directory - Multitenant) and personal Microsoft accounts (e.g. Skype, Xbox), select Web in Redirect URI Enter <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:53682/">http://localhost:53682/</a> and click Register. Copy and keep the Application (client) ID under the app name for later use.
<dt>3.
<dd>Under manage select Certificates &amp; secrets, click New client secret. Copy and keep that secret for later use.
<dt>4.
<dd>Under manage select API permissions, click Add a permission and select Microsoft Graph then select delegated permissions.
<dt>5.
<dd>Search and select the following permissions: Files.Read, Files.ReadWrite, Files.Read.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, offline_access, User.Read. Once selected click Add permissions at the bottom.</dl>
 

 Now the application is complete. Run rclone config to create or edit a OneDrive remote. Supply the app ID and password as Client ID and Secret, respectively. rclone will walk you through the remaining steps.
<h3>Modification time and hashes</h3>OneDrive allows modification times to be set on objects accurate to 1 second. These will be used to detect whether objects need syncing or not. 

 OneDrive personal supports SHA1 type hashes. OneDrive for business and Sharepoint Server support QuickXorHash (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/developer/code-snippets/quickxorhash">https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/developer/code-snippets/quickxorhash</a>). 

 For all types of OneDrive you can use the --checksum flag.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>In addition to the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> the following characters are also replaced: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &quot; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x22 </td><td ALIGN=center> 02 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> * </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2A </td><td ALIGN=center> 0A 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> : </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3A </td><td ALIGN=center> 1A 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &lt; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3C </td><td ALIGN=center> 1C 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &gt; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3E </td><td ALIGN=center> 1E 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> ? </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3F </td><td ALIGN=center> 1F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> \ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x5C </td><td ALIGN=center> 3C 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> | </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x7C </td><td ALIGN=center> 5C 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> # </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x23 </td><td ALIGN=center> 03 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> % </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x25 </td><td ALIGN=center> 05 
</td></tr> </table> 

 File names can also not end with the following characters. These only get replaced if they are the last character in the name: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> SP </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x20 </td><td ALIGN=center> 20 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> . </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2E </td><td ALIGN=center> 0E 
</td></tr> </table> 

 File names can also not begin with the following characters. These only get replaced if they are the first character in the name: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> SP </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x20 </td><td ALIGN=center> 20 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> ~ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x7E </td><td ALIGN=center> 5E 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Deleting files</h3>Any files you delete with rclone will end up in the trash. Microsoft doesn't provide an API to permanently delete files, nor to empty the trash, so you will have to do that with one of Microsoft's apps or via the OneDrive website.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to onedrive (Microsoft OneDrive).
<h3>-onedrive-client-id</h3>OAuth Client Id Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_CLIENT_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-onedrive-client-secret</h3>OAuth Client Secret Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_secret
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_CLIENT_SECRET
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to onedrive (Microsoft OneDrive).
<h3>-onedrive-token</h3>OAuth Access Token as a JSON blob.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_TOKEN
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-onedrive-auth-url</h3>Auth server URL. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: auth_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_AUTH_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-onedrive-token-url</h3>Token server url. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_TOKEN_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-onedrive-chunk-size</h3>Chunk size to upload files with - must be multiple of 320k (327,680 bytes). 

 Above this size files will be chunked - must be multiple of 320k (327,680 bytes) and should not exceed 250M (262,144,000 bytes) else you may encounter &quot;Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.InvalidClientQueryException: The request message is too big.&quot; Note that the chunks will be buffered into memory.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: chunk_size
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_CHUNK_SIZE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 10M</dl><h3>-onedrive-drive-id</h3>The ID of the drive to use
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: drive_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_DRIVE_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-onedrive-drive-type</h3>The type of the drive ( personal | business | documentLibrary )
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: drive_type
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_DRIVE_TYPE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-onedrive-expose-onenote-files</h3>Set to make OneNote files show up in directory listings. 

 By default rclone will hide OneNote files in directory listings because operations like "Open" and "Update" won't work on them. But this behaviour may also prevent you from deleting them. If you want to delete OneNote files or otherwise want them to show up in directory listing, set this option.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: expose_onenote_files
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_EXPOSE_ONENOTE_FILES
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-onedrive-server-side-across-configs</h3>Allow server side operations (eg copy) to work across different onedrive configs. 

 This can be useful if you wish to do a server side copy between two different Onedrives. Note that this isn't enabled by default because it isn't easy to tell if it will work between any two configurations.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: server_side_across_configs
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_SERVER_SIDE_ACROSS_CONFIGS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-onedrive-no-versions</h3>Remove all versions on modifying operations 

 Onedrive for business creates versions when rclone uploads new files overwriting an existing one and when it sets the modification time. 

 These versions take up space out of the quota. 

 This flag checks for versions after file upload and setting modification time and removes all but the last version. 

 NB Onedrive personal can't currently delete versions so don't use this flag there.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: no_versions
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_NO_VERSIONS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-onedrive-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_ONEDRIVE_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,LtGt,DoubleQuote,Colon,Question,Asterisk,Pipe,Hash,Percent,BackSlash,Del,Ctl,LeftSpace,LeftTilde,RightSpace,RightPeriod,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>If you don't use rclone for 90 days the refresh token will expire. This will result in authorization problems. This is easy to fix by running the rclone config reconnect remote: command to get a new token and refresh token.
<h3>Naming</h3>Note that OneDrive is case insensitive so you can't have a file called "Hello.doc" and one called "hello.doc". 

 There are quite a few characters that can't be in OneDrive file names. These can't occur on Windows platforms, but on non-Windows platforms they are common. Rclone will map these names to and from an identical looking unicode equivalent. For example if a file has a ? in it will be mapped to 1F instead.
<h3>File sizes</h3>The largest allowed file size is 100GB for both OneDrive Personal and OneDrive for Business (Updated 17 June 2020) (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/invalid-file-names-and-file-types-in-onedrive-and-sharepoint-64883a5d-228e-48f5-b3d2-eb39e07630fa?ui=en-us">https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/invalid-file-names-and-file-types-in-onedrive-and-sharepoint-64883a5d-228e-48f5-b3d2-eb39e07630fa?ui=en-us</a>&amp;rs=en-us&amp;ad=us#individualfilesize).
<h3>Path length</h3>The entire path, including the file name, must contain fewer than 400 characters for OneDrive, OneDrive for Business and SharePoint Online. If you are encrypting file and folder names with rclone, you may want to pay attention to this limitation because the encrypted names are typically longer than the original ones.
<h3>Number of files</h3>OneDrive seems to be OK with at least 50,000 files in a folder, but at 100,000 rclone will get errors listing the directory like couldn't list files: UnknownError:. See #2707 (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/2707)">https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/2707)</a> for more info. 

 An official document about the limitations for different types of OneDrive can be found here (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://support.office.com/en-us/article/invalid-file-names-and-file-types-in-onedrive-onedrive-for-business-and-sharepoint-64883a5d-228e-48f5-b3d2-eb39e07630fa">https://support.office.com/en-us/article/invalid-file-names-and-file-types-in-onedrive-onedrive-for-business-and-sharepoint-64883a5d-228e-48f5-b3d2-eb39e07630fa</a>).
<h3>Versions</h3>Every change in a file OneDrive causes the service to create a new version of the the file. This counts against a users quota. For example changing the modification time of a file creates a second version, so the file apparently uses twice the space. 

 For example the copy command is affected by this as rclone copies the file and then afterwards sets the modification time to match the source file which uses another version. 

 You can use the rclone cleanup command (see below) to remove all old versions. 

 Or you can set the no_versions parameter to true and rclone will remove versions after operations which create new versions. This takes extra transactions so only enable it if you need it. 

 Note At the time of writing Onedrive Personal creates versions (but not for setting the modification time) but the API for removing them returns "API not found" so cleanup and no_versions should not be used on Onedrive Personal.
<h3>Disabling versioning</h3>Starting October 2018, users will no longer be able to disable versioning by default. This is because Microsoft has brought an update (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/Microsoft-OneDrive-Blog/New-Updates-to-OneDrive-and-SharePoint-Team-Site-Versioning/ba-p/204390)">https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/Microsoft-OneDrive-Blog/New-Updates-to-OneDrive-and-SharePoint-Team-Site-Versioning/ba-p/204390)</a> to the mechanism. To change this new default setting, a PowerShell command is required to be run by a SharePoint admin. If you are an admin, you can run these commands in PowerShell to change that setting:
<dl COMPACT><dt>1.
<dd>Install-Module -Name Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell (in case you haven't installed this already)
<dt>2.
<dd>Import-Module Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell -DisableNameChecking
<dt>3.
<dd>Connect-SPOService -Url <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://YOURSITE-admin.sharepoint.com">https://YOURSITE-admin.sharepoint.com</a> -Credential YOU [at] YOURSITE.COM (replacing YOURSITE, YOU, YOURSITE.COM with the actual values; this will prompt for your credentials)
<dt>4.
<dd>Set-SPOTenant -EnableMinimumVersionRequirement $False
<dt>5.
<dd>Disconnect-SPOService (to disconnect from the server)</dl>
 

 Below are the steps for normal users to disable versioning. If you don't see the "No Versioning" option, make sure the above requirements are met. 

 User Weropol (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/Weropol)">https://github.com/Weropol)</a> has found a method to disable versioning on OneDrive
<dl COMPACT><dt>1.
<dd>Open the settings menu by clicking on the gear symbol at the top of the OneDrive Business page.
<dt>2.
<dd>Click Site settings.
<dt>3.
<dd>Once on the Site settings page, navigate to Site Administration &gt; Site libraries and lists.
<dt>4.
<dd>Click Customize "Documents".
<dt>5.
<dd>Click General Settings &gt; Versioning Settings.
<dt>6.
<dd>Under Document Version History select the option No versioning. Note: This will disable the creation of new file versions, but will not remove any previous versions. Your documents are safe.
<dt>7.
<dd>Apply the changes by clicking OK.
<dt>8.
<dd>Use rclone to upload or modify files. (I also use the -no-update-modtime flag)
<dt>9.
<dd>Restore the versioning settings after using rclone. (Optional)</dl><h3>Cleanup</h3>OneDrive supports rclone cleanup which causes rclone to look through every file under the path supplied and delete all version but the current version. Because this involves traversing all the files, then querying each file for versions it can be quite slow. Rclone does --checkers tests in parallel. The command also supports -i which is a great way to see what it would do.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone cleanup -i remote:path/subdir # interactively remove all old version for path/subdir
rclone cleanup remote:path/subdir # unconditionally remove all old version for path/subdir</pre></dl>
 

 NB Onedrive personal can't currently delete versions
<h3>Troubleshooting</h3><h3>Unexpected file size/hash differences on Sharepoint</h3>It is a known (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/OneDrive/onedrive-api-docs/issues/935#issuecomment-441741631)">https://github.com/OneDrive/onedrive-api-docs/issues/935#issuecomment-441741631)</a> issue that Sharepoint (not OneDrive or OneDrive for Business) silently modifies uploaded files, mainly Office files (.docx, .xlsx, etc.), causing file size and hash checks to fail. There are also other situations that will cause OneDrive to report inconsistent file sizes. To use rclone with such affected files on Sharepoint, you may disable these checks with the following command line arguments:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>--ignore-checksum --ignore-size</pre></dl>
 

 Alternatively, if you have write access to the OneDrive files, it may be possible to fix this problem for certain files, by attempting the steps below. Open the web interface for OneDrive (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://onedrive.live.com)">https://onedrive.live.com)</a> and find the affected files (which will be in the error messages/log for rclone). Simply click on each of these files, causing OneDrive to open them on the web. This will cause each file to be converted in place to a format that is functionally equivalent but which will no longer trigger the size discrepancy. Once all problematic files are converted you will no longer need the ignore options above.
<h3>Replacing/deleting existing files on Sharepoint gets "item not found"</h3>It is a known (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/OneDrive/onedrive-api-docs/issues/1068)">https://github.com/OneDrive/onedrive-api-docs/issues/1068)</a> issue that Sharepoint (not OneDrive or OneDrive for Business) may return "item not found" errors when users try to replace or delete uploaded files; this seems to mainly affect Office files (.docx, .xlsx, etc.). As a workaround, you may use the --backup-dir &lt;BACKUP_DIR&gt; command line argument so rclone moves the files to be replaced/deleted into a given backup directory (instead of directly replacing/deleting them). For example, to instruct rclone to move the files into the directory rclone-backup-dir on backend mysharepoint, you may use:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>--backup-dir mysharepoint:rclone-backup-dir</pre></dl><h3>access_denied (AADSTS65005)</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Error: access_denied
Code: AADSTS65005
Description: Using application 'rclone' is currently not supported for your organization [YOUR_ORGANIZATION] because it is in an unmanaged state. An administrator needs to claim ownership of the company by DNS validation of [YOUR_ORGANIZATION] before the application rclone can be provisioned.</pre></dl>
 

 This means that rclone can't use the OneDrive for Business API with your account. You can't do much about it, maybe write an email to your admins. 

 However, there are other ways to interact with your OneDrive account. Have a look at the webdav backend: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/webdav/#sharepoint">https://rclone.org/webdav/#sharepoint</a>
<h3>invalid_grant (AADSTS50076)</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Error: invalid_grant
Code: AADSTS50076
Description: Due to a configuration change made by your administrator, or because you moved to a new location, you must use multi-factor authentication to access '...'.</pre></dl>
 

 If you see the error above after enabling multi-factor authentication for your account, you can fix it by refreshing your OAuth refresh token. To do that, run rclone config, and choose to edit your OneDrive backend. Then, you don't need to actually make any changes until you reach this question: Already have a token - refresh?. For this question, answer y and go through the process to refresh your token, just like the first time the backend is configured. After this, rclone should work again for this backend.
<h3>OpenDrive</h3>Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>n) New remote
d) Delete remote
q) Quit config
e/n/d/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / OpenDrive
 \ &quot;opendrive&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; opendrive
Username
username&gt;
Password
y) Yes type in my own password
g) Generate random password
y/g&gt; y
Enter the password:
password:
Confirm the password:
password:
--------------------
[remote]
username =
password = *** ENCRYPTED ***
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 List directories in top level of your OpenDrive
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your OpenDrive
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to an OpenDrive directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Modified time and MD5SUMs</h3>OpenDrive allows modification times to be set on objects accurate to 1 second. These will be used to detect whether objects need syncing or not.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3><table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement

</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &quot; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x22 </td><td ALIGN=center> 02

</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> ? </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x3F </td><td ALIGN=center> 1F

 File names can also not begin or end with the following characters. These only get replaced if they are the first or last character in the name:

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to opendrive (OpenDrive).
<h3>-opendrive-username</h3>Username
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: username
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_OPENDRIVE_USERNAME
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-opendrive-password</h3>Password. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: password
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_OPENDRIVE_PASSWORD
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to opendrive (OpenDrive).
<h3>-opendrive-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_OPENDRIVE_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,LtGt,DoubleQuote,Colon,Question,Asterisk,Pipe,BackSlash,LeftSpace,LeftCrLfHtVt,RightSpace,RightCrLfHtVt,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>-opendrive-chunk-size</h3>Files will be uploaded in chunks this size. 

 Note that these chunks are buffered in memory so increasing them will increase memory use.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: chunk_size
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_OPENDRIVE_CHUNK_SIZE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 10M</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>Note that OpenDrive is case insensitive so you can't have a file called "Hello.doc" and one called "hello.doc". 

 There are quite a few characters that can't be in OpenDrive file names. These can't occur on Windows platforms, but on non-Windows platforms they are common. Rclone will map these names to and from an identical looking unicode equivalent. For example if a file has a ? in it will be mapped to 1F instead.
<h3>QingStor</h3>Paths are specified as remote:bucket (or remote: for the lsd command.) You may put subdirectories in too, eg remote:bucket/path/to/dir. 

 Here is an example of making an QingStor configuration. First run
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process.

 This remote is called remote and can now be used like this 

 See all buckets
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new bucket
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:bucket</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a bucket
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:bucket</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote bucket, deleting any excess files in the bucket.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:bucket</pre></dl><h3>-fast-list</h3>This remote supports --fast-list which allows you to use fewer transactions in exchange for more memory. See the rclone docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)">https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)</a> for more details.
<h3>Multipart uploads</h3>rclone supports multipart uploads with QingStor which means that it can upload files bigger than 5GB. Note that files uploaded with multipart upload don't have an MD5SUM. 

 Note that incomplete multipart uploads older than 24 hours can be removed with rclone cleanup remote:bucket just for one bucket rclone cleanup remote: for all buckets. QingStor does not ever remove incomplete multipart uploads so it may be necessary to run this from time to time.
<h3>Buckets and Zone</h3>With QingStor you can list buckets (rclone lsd) using any zone, but you can only access the content of a bucket from the zone it was created in. If you attempt to access a bucket from the wrong zone, you will get an error, incorrect zone, the bucket is not in 'XXX' zone.
<h3>Authentication</h3>There are two ways to supply rclone with a set of QingStor credentials. In order of precedence:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Directly in the rclone configuration file (as configured by rclone config)
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>set access_key_id and secret_access_key</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>Runtime configuration:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>set env_auth to true in the config file
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Exporting the following environment variables before running rclone
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Access Key ID: QS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or QS_ACCESS_KEY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Secret Access Key: QS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or QS_SECRET_KEY</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>The control characters 0x00-0x1F and / are replaced as in the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters</a>). Note that 0x7F is not replaced. 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to qingstor (QingCloud Object Storage).
<h3>-qingstor-env-auth</h3>Get QingStor credentials from runtime. Only applies if access_key_id and secret_access_key is blank.

<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"false"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Enter QingStor credentials in the next step</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"true"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Get QingStor credentials from the environment (env vars or IAM)</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-qingstor-access-key-id</h3>QingStor Access Key ID Leave blank for anonymous access or runtime credentials.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: access_key_id

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-qingstor-secret-access-key</h3>QingStor Secret Access Key (password) Leave blank for anonymous access or runtime credentials.

<dt>&bull;

<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-qingstor-endpoint</h3>Enter an endpoint URL to connection QingStor API. Leave blank will use the default value "<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://qingstor.com:443">https://qingstor.com:443</a>"
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-qingstor-zone</h3>Zone to connect to. Default is "pek3a".

<dd>"sh1a"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>The Shanghai (China) First Zone
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Needs location constraint sh1a.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;

</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to qingstor (QingCloud Object Storage).
<h3>-qingstor-connection-retries</h3>Number of connection retries.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: connection_retries
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_QINGSTOR_CONNECTION_RETRIES
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: int
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 3</dl><h3>-qingstor-upload-cutoff</h3>Cutoff for switching to chunked upload 

 Any files larger than this will be uploaded in chunks of chunk_size. The minimum is 0 and the maximum is 5GB.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: upload_cutoff
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_QINGSTOR_UPLOAD_CUTOFF
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 200M</dl><h3>-qingstor-chunk-size</h3>Chunk size to use for uploading. 

 When uploading files larger than upload_cutoff they will be uploaded as multipart uploads using this chunk size. 

 Note that "-qingstor-upload-concurrency" chunks of this size are buffered in memory per transfer. 

 If you are transferring large files over high speed links and you have enough memory, then increasing this will speed up the transfers.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: chunk_size
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_QINGSTOR_CHUNK_SIZE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 4M</dl><h3>-qingstor-upload-concurrency</h3>Concurrency for multipart uploads. 

 This is the number of chunks of the same file that are uploaded concurrently. 

 NB if you set this to &gt; 1 then the checksums of multpart uploads become corrupted (the uploads themselves are not corrupted though). 

 If you are uploading small numbers of large file over high speed link and these uploads do not fully utilize your bandwidth, then increasing this may help to speed up the transfers.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: upload_concurrency
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_QINGSTOR_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: int
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 1</dl><h3>-qingstor-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_QINGSTOR_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,Ctl,InvalidUtf8</dl><h3>Swift</h3>Swift refers to OpenStack Object Storage (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://docs.openstack.org/swift/latest/">https://docs.openstack.org/swift/latest/</a>). Commercial implementations of that being:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;

 Paths are specified as remote:container (or remote: for the lsd command.) You may put subdirectories in too, eg remote:container/path/to/dir.

 This remote is called remote and can now be used like this 

 See all containers
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new container
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:container</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a container
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:container</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote container, deleting any excess files in the container.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:container</pre></dl><h3>Configuration from an OpenStack credentials file</h3>An OpenStack credentials file typically looks something something like this (without the comments)
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>export OS_AUTH_URL=<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://a.provider.net/v2.0">https://a.provider.net/v2.0</a>
export OS_TENANT_ID=ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff
export OS_TENANT_NAME=&quot;1234567890123456&quot;
export OS_USERNAME=&quot;123abc567xy&quot;
echo &quot;Please enter your OpenStack Password: &quot;
read -sr OS_PASSWORD_INPUT
export OS_PASSWORD=$OS_PASSWORD_INPUT
export OS_REGION_NAME=&quot;SBG1&quot;
if [ -z &quot;$OS_REGION_NAME&quot; ]; then unset OS_REGION_NAME; fi</pre></dl>
 

 The config file needs to look something like this where $OS_USERNAME represents the value of the OS_USERNAME variable - 123abc567xy in the example above.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>[remote]
type = swift
user = $OS_USERNAME
key = $OS_PASSWORD
auth = $OS_AUTH_URL
tenant = $OS_TENANT_NAME</pre></dl>
 

 Note that you may (or may not) need to set region too - try without first.
<h3>Configuration from the environment</h3>If you prefer you can configure rclone to use swift using a standard set of OpenStack environment variables. 

 When you run through the config, make sure you choose true for env_auth and leave everything else blank. 

 rclone will then set any empty config parameters from the environment using standard OpenStack environment variables. There is a list of the variables (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://godoc.org/github.com/ncw/swift#Connection.ApplyEnvironment)">https://godoc.org/github.com/ncw/swift#Connection.ApplyEnvironment)</a> in the docs for the swift library.
<h3>Using an alternate authentication method</h3>If your OpenStack installation uses a non-standard authentication method that might not be yet supported by rclone or the underlying swift library, you can authenticate externally (e.g. calling manually the openstack commands to get a token). Then, you just need to pass the two configuration variables auth_token and storage_url. If they are both provided, the other variables are ignored. rclone will not try to authenticate but instead assume it is already authenticated and use these two variables to access the OpenStack installation.
<h3>Using rclone without a config file</h3>You can use rclone with swift without a config file, if desired, like this:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>source openstack-credentials-file
export RCLONE_CONFIG_MYREMOTE_TYPE=swift
export RCLONE_CONFIG_MYREMOTE_ENV_AUTH=true
rclone lsd myremote:</pre></dl><h3>-fast-list</h3>This remote supports --fast-list which allows you to use fewer transactions in exchange for more memory. See the rclone docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)">https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)</a> for more details.
<h3>-update and -use-server-modtime</h3>As noted below, the modified time is stored on metadata on the object. It is used by default for all operations that require checking the time a file was last updated. It allows rclone to treat the remote more like a true filesystem, but it is inefficient because it requires an extra API call to retrieve the metadata. 

 For many operations, the time the object was last uploaded to the remote is sufficient to determine if it is "dirty". By using --update along with --use-server-modtime, you can avoid the extra API call and simply upload files whose local modtime is newer than the time it was last uploaded.

</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to swift (OpenStack Swift (Rackspace Cloud Files, Memset Memstore, OVH)).
<h3>-swift-chunk-size</h3>Above this size files will be chunked into a _segments container. 

 Above this size files will be chunked into a _segments container. The default for this is 5GB which is its maximum value.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: chunk_size
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SWIFT_CHUNK_SIZE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: SizeSuffix
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 5G</dl><h3>-swift-no-chunk</h3>Don't chunk files during streaming upload. 

 When doing streaming uploads (eg using rcat or mount) setting this flag will cause the swift backend to not upload chunked files. 

 This will limit the maximum upload size to 5GB. However non chunked files are easier to deal with and have an MD5SUM. 

 Rclone will still chunk files bigger than chunk_size when doing normal copy operations.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: no_chunk
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SWIFT_NO_CHUNK
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-swift-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SWIFT_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,InvalidUtf8</dl><h3>Modified time</h3>The modified time is stored as metadata on the object as X-Object-Meta-Mtime as floating point since the epoch accurate to 1 ns. 

 This is a de facto standard (used in the official python-swiftclient amongst others) for storing the modification time for an object.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3><table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> NUL </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x00 </td><td ALIGN=center> 00 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Limitations</h3>The Swift API doesn't return a correct MD5SUM for segmented files (Dynamic or Static Large Objects) so rclone won't check or use the MD5SUM for these.
<h3>Troubleshooting</h3><h3>Rclone gives Failed to create file system for "remote:": Bad Request</h3>Due to an oddity of the underlying swift library, it gives a "Bad Request" error rather than a more sensible error when the authentication fails for Swift. 

 So this most likely means your username / password is wrong. You can investigate further with the --dump-bodies flag. 

 This may also be caused by specifying the region when you shouldn't have (eg OVH).
<h3>Rclone gives Failed to create file system: Response didn't have storage url and auth token</h3>This is most likely caused by forgetting to specify your tenant when setting up a swift remote.
<h3>pCloud</h3>Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 The initial setup for pCloud involves getting a token from pCloud which you need to do in your browser. rclone config walks you through it. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config
n/s/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / Pcloud
 \ &quot;pcloud&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; pcloud
Pcloud App Client Id - leave blank normally.
client_id&gt; 
Pcloud App Client Secret - leave blank normally.
client_secret&gt; 
Remote config
Use auto config?
 * Say Y if not sure
 * Say N if you are working on a remote or headless machine
y) Yes
n) No
y/n&gt; y
If your browser doesn't open automatically go to the following link: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth">http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth</a>
Log in and authorize rclone for access
Waiting for code...
Got code
--------------------
[remote]
client_id = 
client_secret = 
token = {&quot;access_token&quot;:&quot;XXX&quot;,&quot;token_type&quot;:&quot;bearer&quot;,&quot;expiry&quot;:&quot;0001-01-01T00:00:00Z&quot;}
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 See the remote setup docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)">https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)</a> for how to set it up on a machine with no Internet browser available. 

 Note that rclone runs a webserver on your local machine to collect the token as returned from pCloud. This only runs from the moment it opens your browser to the moment you get back the verification code. This is on <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/">http://127.0.0.1:53682/</a> and this it may require you to unblock it temporarily if you are running a host firewall. 

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 List directories in top level of your pCloud
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your pCloud
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to an pCloud directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Modified time and hashes</h3>pCloud allows modification times to be set on objects accurate to 1 second. These will be used to detect whether objects need syncing or not. In order to set a Modification time pCloud requires the object be re-uploaded. 

 pCloud supports MD5 and SHA1 type hashes, so you can use the --checksum flag.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>In addition to the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> the following characters are also replaced: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> \ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x5C </td><td ALIGN=center> 3C 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Deleting files</h3>Deleted files will be moved to the trash. Your subscription level will determine how long items stay in the trash. rclone cleanup can be used to empty the trash.
<h3>Root folder ID</h3>You can set the root_folder_id for rclone. This is the directory (identified by its Folder ID) that rclone considers to be the root of your pCloud drive. 

 Normally you will leave this blank and rclone will determine the correct root to use itself. 

 However you can set this to restrict rclone to a specific folder hierarchy. 

 In order to do this you will have to find the Folder ID of the directory you wish rclone to display. This will be the folder field of the URL when you open the relevant folder in the pCloud web interface. 

 So if the folder you want rclone to use has a URL which looks like <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://my.pcloud.com/#page=filemanager">https://my.pcloud.com/#page=filemanager</a>&amp;folder=5xxxxxxxx8&amp;tpl=foldergrid in the browser, then you use 5xxxxxxxx8 as the root_folder_id in the config.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to pcloud (Pcloud).
<h3>-pcloud-client-id</h3>OAuth Client Id Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PCLOUD_CLIENT_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-pcloud-client-secret</h3>OAuth Client Secret Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_secret
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PCLOUD_CLIENT_SECRET
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to pcloud (Pcloud).
<h3>-pcloud-token</h3>OAuth Access Token as a JSON blob.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PCLOUD_TOKEN
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-pcloud-auth-url</h3>Auth server URL. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: auth_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PCLOUD_AUTH_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-pcloud-token-url</h3>Token server url. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PCLOUD_TOKEN_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-pcloud-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PCLOUD_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,BackSlash,Del,Ctl,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>-pcloud-root-folder-id</h3>Fill in for rclone to use a non root folder as its starting point.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: root_folder_id

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "d0"</dl><h3>-pcloud-hostname</h3>Hostname to connect to. 

 This is normally set when rclone initially does the oauth connection, however you will need to set it by hand if you are using remote config with rclone authorize.
