</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>premiumize.me</h3>Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 The initial setup for premiumize.me (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://premiumize.me/)">https://premiumize.me/)</a> involves getting a token from premiumize.me which you need to do in your browser. rclone config walks you through it. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config
n/s/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Enter a string value. Press Enter for the default (&quot;&quot;).
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / premiumize.me
 \ &quot;premiumizeme&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; premiumizeme
** See help for premiumizeme backend at: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/premiumizeme/">https://rclone.org/premiumizeme/</a> **
Remote config
Use auto config?
 * Say Y if not sure
 * Say N if you are working on a remote or headless machine
y) Yes
n) No
y/n&gt; y
If your browser doesn't open automatically go to the following link: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth">http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth</a>
Log in and authorize rclone for access
Waiting for code...
Got code
--------------------
[remote]
type = premiumizeme
token = {&quot;access_token&quot;:&quot;XXX&quot;,&quot;token_type&quot;:&quot;Bearer&quot;,&quot;refresh_token&quot;:&quot;XXX&quot;,&quot;expiry&quot;:&quot;2029-08-07T18:44:15.548915378+01:00&quot;}
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; </pre></dl>
 

 See the remote setup docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)">https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)</a> for how to set it up on a machine with no Internet browser available. 

 Note that rclone runs a webserver on your local machine to collect the token as returned from premiumize.me. This only runs from the moment it opens your browser to the moment you get back the verification code. This is on <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/">http://127.0.0.1:53682/</a> and this it may require you to unblock it temporarily if you are running a host firewall. 

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 List directories in top level of your premiumize.me
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your premiumize.me
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to an premiumize.me directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Modified time and hashes</h3>premiumize.me does not support modification times or hashes, therefore syncing will default to --size-only checking. Note that using --update will work.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>In addition to the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> the following characters are also replaced: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> \ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x5C </td><td ALIGN=center> 3C 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &quot; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x22 </td><td ALIGN=center> 02 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to premiumizeme (premiumize.me).
<h3>-premiumizeme-api-key</h3>API Key. 

 This is not normally used - use oauth instead.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: api_key
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PREMIUMIZEME_API_KEY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to premiumizeme (premiumize.me).
<h3>-premiumizeme-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PREMIUMIZEME_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,DoubleQuote,BackSlash,Del,Ctl,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>Note that premiumize.me is case insensitive so you can't have a file called "Hello.doc" and one called "hello.doc". 

 premiumize.me file names can't have the \ or &quot; characters in. rclone maps these to and from an identical looking unicode equivalents 3C and 02 

 premiumize.me only supports filenames up to 255 characters in length.

 Note that rclone runs a webserver on your local machine to collect the token as returned from Google if you use auto config mode. This only runs from the moment it opens your browser to the moment you get back the verification code. This is on <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/">http://127.0.0.1:53682/</a> and this it may require you to unblock it temporarily if you are running a host firewall, or use manual mode.

 To copy a local directory to a put.io directory called backup

</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to putio (Put.io).
<h3>-putio-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding

<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_PUTIO_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,BackSlash,Del,Ctl,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Seafile</h3>This is a backend for the Seafile (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.seafile.com/)">https://www.seafile.com/)</a> storage service: - It works with both the free community edition or the professional edition. - Seafile versions 6.x and 7.x are all supported. - Encrypted libraries are also supported. - It supports 2FA enabled users
<h3>Root mode vs Library mode</h3>There are two distinct modes you can setup your remote: - you point your remote to the root of the server, meaning you don't specify a library during the configuration: Paths are specified as remote:library. You may put subdirectories in too, eg remote:library/path/to/dir. - you point your remote to a specific library during the configuration: Paths are specified as remote:path/to/dir. This is the recommended mode when using encrypted libraries. (This mode is possibly slightly faster than the root mode)
<h3>Configuration in root mode</h3>Here is an example of making a seafile configuration for a user with no two-factor authentication. First run
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config</pre></dl>

 This remote is called seafile. It's pointing to the root of your seafile server and can now be used like this: 

 See all libraries

<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls seafile:library</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote library, deleting any excess files in the library.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory seafile:library</pre></dl><h3>Configuration in library mode</h3>Here's an example of a configuration in library mode with a user that has the two-factor authentication enabled.  You'll notice your password is blank in the configuration. It's because we only need the password to authenticate you once. 

 You specified My Library during the configuration. The root of the remote is pointing at the root of the library My Library: 

 See all files in the library:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd seafile:</pre></dl>
 

 Create a new directory inside the library
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir seafile:directory</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls seafile:directory</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote library, deleting any excess files in the library.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory seafile:</pre></dl><h3>-fast-list</h3>Seafile version 7+ supports --fast-list which allows you to use fewer transactions in exchange for more memory. See the rclone docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)">https://rclone.org/docs/#fast-list)</a> for more details. Please note this is not supported on seafile server version 6.x
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>In addition to the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> the following characters are also replaced: 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> &quot; </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x22 </td><td ALIGN=center> 02 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> \ </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x5C </td><td ALIGN=center> 3C 
</td></tr> </table> 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Seafile and rclone link</h3>Rclone supports generating share links for non-encrypted libraries only. They can either be for a file or a directory:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone link seafile:seafile-tutorial.doc
<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://my.seafile.server/f/fdcd8a2f93f84b8b90f4/">http://my.seafile.server/f/fdcd8a2f93f84b8b90f4/</a></pre></dl>
 

 or if run on a directory you will get:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone link seafile:dir
<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://my.seafile.server/d/9ea2455f6f55478bbb0d/">http://my.seafile.server/d/9ea2455f6f55478bbb0d/</a></pre></dl>
 

 Please note a share link is unique for each file or directory. If you run a link command on a file/dir that has already been shared, you will get the exact same link.
<h3>Compatibility</h3>It has been actively tested using the seafile docker image (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/haiwen/seafile-docker)">https://github.com/haiwen/seafile-docker)</a> of these versions: - 6.3.4 community edition - 7.0.5 community edition - 7.1.3 community edition 

 Versions below 6.0 are not supported. Versions between 6.0 and 6.3 haven't been tested and might not work properly.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to seafile (seafile).

<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://cloud.seafile.com/">https://cloud.seafile.com/</a>"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Connect to cloud.seafile.com</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-seafile-user</h3>User name (usually email address)

<dd>Config: user
<dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: pass
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SEAFILE_PASS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-seafile-2fa</h3>Two-factor authentication (`true' if the account has 2FA enabled)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: 2fa
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SEAFILE_2FA
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-seafile-library</h3>Name of the library. Leave blank to access all non-encrypted libraries.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: library
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SEAFILE_LIBRARY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-seafile-library-key</h3>Library password (for encrypted libraries only). Leave blank if you pass it through the command line. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: library_key
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SEAFILE_LIBRARY_KEY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-seafile-auth-token</h3>Authentication token
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: auth_token
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SEAFILE_AUTH_TOKEN
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to seafile (seafile).
<h3>-seafile-create-library</h3>Should rclone create a library if it doesn't exist
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: create_library
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SEAFILE_CREATE_LIBRARY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-seafile-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SEAFILE_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,DoubleQuote,BackSlash,Ctl,InvalidUtf8</dl><h3>Sftp</h3>SFTP is the Secure (or SSH) File Transfer Protocol (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSH_File_Transfer_Protocol">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSH_File_Transfer_Protocol</a>). 

 The SFTP backend can be used with a number of different providers:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>C14
<dt>&bull;
<dd>rsync.net</dl>
 

 SFTP runs over SSH v2 and is installed as standard with most modern SSH installations. 

 Paths are specified as remote:path. If the path does not begin with a / it is relative to the home directory of the user. An empty path remote: refers to the user's home directory. 

 &quot;Note that some SFTP servers will need the leading / - Synology is a good example of this. rsync.net, on the other hand, requires users to OMIT the leading /. 

 Here is an example of making an SFTP configuration. First run
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config
n/s/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / SSH/SFTP Connection
 \ &quot;sftp&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; sftp
SSH host to connect to
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
 1 / Connect to example.com
 \ &quot;example.com&quot;
host&gt; example.com
SSH username, leave blank for current username, ncw
user&gt; sftpuser
SSH port, leave blank to use default (22)
port&gt;
SSH password, leave blank to use ssh-agent.
y) Yes type in my own password
g) Generate random password
n) No leave this optional password blank
y/g/n&gt; n
Path to unencrypted PEM-encoded private key file, leave blank to use ssh-agent.
key_file&gt;
Remote config
--------------------
[remote]
host = example.com
user = sftpuser
port =
pass =
key_file =
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 This remote is called remote and can now be used like this: 

 See all directories in the home directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:path/to/directory</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:path/to/directory</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote directory, deleting any excess files in the directory.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:directory</pre></dl><h3>SSH Authentication</h3>The SFTP remote supports three authentication methods:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Password
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Key file
<dt>&bull;
<dd>ssh-agent</dl>
 

 Key files should be PEM-encoded private key files. For instance /home/$USER/.ssh/id_rsa. Only unencrypted OpenSSH or PEM encrypted files are supported. 

 The key file can be specified in either an external file (key_file) or contained within the rclone config file (key_pem). If using key_pem in the config file, the entry should be on a single line with new line (`' or `') separating lines. i.e.&nbsp; 

 key_pem = ----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----0gAMbMbaSsd----END RSA PRIVATE KEY---- 

 This will generate it correctly for key_pem for use in the config:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>awk '{printf &quot;%s\\n&quot;, $0}' &lt; ~/.ssh/id_rsa</pre></dl>
 

 If you don't specify pass, key_file, or key_pem then rclone will attempt to contact an ssh-agent. 

 You can also specify key_use_agent to force the usage of an ssh-agent. In this case key_file or key_pem can also be specified to force the usage of a specific key in the ssh-agent. 

 Using an ssh-agent is the only way to load encrypted OpenSSH keys at the moment. 

 If you set the --sftp-ask-password option, rclone will prompt for a password when needed and no password has been configured.
<h3>ssh-agent on macOS</h3>Note that there seem to be various problems with using an ssh-agent on macOS due to recent changes in the OS. The most effective work-around seems to be to start an ssh-agent in each session, eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>eval `ssh-agent -s` &amp;&amp; ssh-add -A</pre></dl>
 

 And then at the end of the session
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>eval `ssh-agent -k`</pre></dl>
 

 These commands can be used in scripts of course.
<h3>Modified time</h3>Modified times are stored on the server to 1 second precision. 

 Modified times are used in syncing and are fully supported. 

 Some SFTP servers disable setting/modifying the file modification time after upload (for example, certain configurations of ProFTPd with mod_sftp). If you are using one of these servers, you can set the option set_modtime = false in your RClone backend configuration to disable this behaviour.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to sftp (SSH/SFTP Connection).
<h3>-sftp-host</h3>SSH host to connect to
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: host
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_HOST
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"example.com"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Connect to example.com</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-sftp-user</h3>SSH username, leave blank for current username, ncw
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: user
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_USER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-port</h3>SSH port, leave blank to use default (22)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: port
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_PORT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-pass</h3>SSH password, leave blank to use ssh-agent. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: pass
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_PASS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-key-pem</h3>Raw PEM-encoded private key, If specified, will override key_file parameter.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: key_pem
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_KEY_PEM
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-key-file</h3>Path to PEM-encoded private key file, leave blank or set key-use-agent to use ssh-agent. 

 Leading ~ will be expanded in the file name as will environment variables such as ${RCLONE_CONFIG_DIR}.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: key_file
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_KEY_FILE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-key-file-pass</h3>The passphrase to decrypt the PEM-encoded private key file. 

 Only PEM encrypted key files (old OpenSSH format) are supported. Encrypted keys in the new OpenSSH format can't be used. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: key_file_pass
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_KEY_FILE_PASS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-key-use-agent</h3>When set forces the usage of the ssh-agent. 

 When key-file is also set, the ".pub" file of the specified key-file is read and only the associated key is requested from the ssh-agent. This allows to avoid Too many authentication failures for *username* errors when the ssh-agent contains many keys.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: key_use_agent
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_KEY_USE_AGENT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-sftp-use-insecure-cipher</h3>Enable the use of insecure ciphers and key exchange methods. 

 This enables the use of the following insecure ciphers and key exchange methods:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>aes128-cbc
<dt>&bull;
<dd>aes192-cbc
<dt>&bull;
<dd>aes256-cbc
<dt>&bull;
<dd>3des-cbc
<dt>&bull;
<dd>diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256
<dt>&bull;
<dd>diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1</dl>
 

 Those algorithms are insecure and may allow plaintext data to be recovered by an attacker.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: use_insecure_cipher
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_USE_INSECURE_CIPHER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"false"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use default Cipher list.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"true"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Enables the use of the aes128-cbc cipher and diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256, diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1 key exchange.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-sftp-disable-hashcheck</h3>Disable the execution of SSH commands to determine if remote file hashing is available. Leave blank or set to false to enable hashing (recommended), set to true to disable hashing.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: disable_hashcheck
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_DISABLE_HASHCHECK
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to sftp (SSH/SFTP Connection).
<h3>-sftp-ask-password</h3>Allow asking for SFTP password when needed. 

 If this is set and no password is supplied then rclone will: - ask for a password - not contact the ssh agent
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: ask_password
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_ASK_PASSWORD
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-sftp-path-override</h3>Override path used by SSH connection. 

 This allows checksum calculation when SFTP and SSH paths are different. This issue affects among others Synology NAS boxes. 

 Shared folders can be found in directories representing volumes
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync /home/local/directory remote:/directory --ssh-path-override /volume2/directory</pre></dl>
 

 Home directory can be found in a shared folder called "home"
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync /home/local/directory remote:/home/directory --ssh-path-override /volume1/homes/USER/directory</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: path_override
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_PATH_OVERRIDE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-set-modtime</h3>Set the modified time on the remote if set.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: set_modtime
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_SET_MODTIME
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: true</dl><h3>-sftp-md5sum-command</h3>The command used to read md5 hashes. Leave blank for autodetect.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: md5sum_command
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_MD5SUM_COMMAND
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-sha1sum-command</h3>The command used to read sha1 hashes. Leave blank for autodetect.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: sha1sum_command
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_SHA1SUM_COMMAND
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sftp-skip-links</h3>Set to skip any symlinks and any other non regular files.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: skip_links
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_SKIP_LINKS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>-sftp-subsystem</h3>Specifies the SSH2 subsystem on the remote host.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: subsystem
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_SUBSYSTEM
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "sftp"</dl><h3>-sftp-server-command</h3>Specifies the path or command to run a sftp server on the remote host. 

 The subsystem option is ignored when server_command is defined.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: server_command
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SFTP_SERVER_COMMAND
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Limitations</h3>SFTP supports checksums if the same login has shell access and md5sum or sha1sum as well as echo are in the remote's PATH. This remote checksumming (file hashing) is recommended and enabled by default. Disabling the checksumming may be required if you are connecting to SFTP servers which are not under your control, and to which the execution of remote commands is prohibited. Set the configuration option disable_hashcheck to true to disable checksumming. 

 SFTP also supports about if the same login has shell access and df are in the remote's PATH. about will return the total space, free space, and used space on the remote for the disk of the specified path on the remote or, if not set, the disk of the root on the remote. about will fail if it does not have shell access or if df is not in the remote's PATH. 

 Note that some SFTP servers (eg Synology) the paths are different for SSH and SFTP so the hashes can't be calculated properly. For them using disable_hashcheck is a good idea. 

 The only ssh agent supported under Windows is Putty's pageant. 

 The Go SSH library disables the use of the aes128-cbc cipher by default, due to security concerns. This can be re-enabled on a per-connection basis by setting the use_insecure_cipher setting in the configuration file to true. Further details on the insecurity of this cipher can be found [in this paper] (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.isg.rhul.ac.uk/~kp/SandPfinal.pdf">http://www.isg.rhul.ac.uk/~kp/SandPfinal.pdf</a>). 

 SFTP isn't supported under plan9 until this issue (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/pkg/sftp/issues/156)">https://github.com/pkg/sftp/issues/156)</a> is fixed. 

 Note that since SFTP isn't HTTP based the following flags don't work with it: --dump-headers, --dump-bodies, --dump-auth 

 Note that --timeout isn't supported (but --contimeout is).
<h3>C14</h3>C14 is supported through the SFTP backend. 

 See C14's documentation (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.online.net/en/storage/c14-cold-storage)">https://www.online.net/en/storage/c14-cold-storage)</a>
<h3>rsync.net</h3>rsync.net is supported through the SFTP backend. 

 See rsync.net's documentation of rclone examples (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.rsync.net/products/rclone.html">https://www.rsync.net/products/rclone.html</a>).
<h3>SugarSync</h3>SugarSync (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://sugarsync.com)">https://sugarsync.com)</a> is a cloud service that enables active synchronization of files across computers and other devices for file backup, access, syncing, and sharing. 

 The initial setup for SugarSync involves getting a token from SugarSync which you can do with rclone. rclone config walks you through it. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config
n/s/q&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Enter a string value. Press Enter for the default (&quot;&quot;).
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / Sugarsync
 \ &quot;sugarsync&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; sugarsync
** See help for sugarsync backend at: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/sugarsync/">https://rclone.org/sugarsync/</a> **
Sugarsync App ID.
Leave blank to use rclone's.
Enter a string value. Press Enter for the default (&quot;&quot;).
app_id&gt; 
Sugarsync Access Key ID.
Leave blank to use rclone's.
Enter a string value. Press Enter for the default (&quot;&quot;).
access_key_id&gt; 
Sugarsync Private Access Key
Leave blank to use rclone's.
Enter a string value. Press Enter for the default (&quot;&quot;).
private_access_key&gt; 
Permanently delete files if true
otherwise put them in the deleted files.
Enter a boolean value (true or false). Press Enter for the default (&quot;false&quot;).
hard_delete&gt; 
Edit advanced config? (y/n)
y) Yes
n) No (default)
y/n&gt; n
Remote config
Username (email address)&gt; nick [at] craig-wood.com
Your Sugarsync password is only required during setup and will not be stored.
password:
--------------------
[remote]
type = sugarsync
refresh_token = <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://api.sugarsync.com/app-authorization/XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX">https://api.sugarsync.com/app-authorization/XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX</a>
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK (default)
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 Note that the config asks for your email and password but doesn't store them, it only uses them to get the initial token. 

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 List directories (sync folders) in top level of your SugarSync
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in your SugarSync folder "Test"
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:Test</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to an SugarSync folder called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl>
 

 Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 NB you can't create files in the top level folder you have to create a folder, which rclone will create as a "Sync Folder" with SugarSync.
<h3>Modified time and hashes</h3>SugarSync does not support modification times or hashes, therefore syncing will default to --size-only checking. Note that using --update will work as rclone can read the time files were uploaded.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>SugarSync replaces the default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> except for DEL. 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in XML strings.
<h3>Deleting files</h3>Deleted files will be moved to the "Deleted items" folder by default. 

 However you can supply the flag --sugarsync-hard-delete or set the config parameter hard_delete = true if you would like files to be deleted straight away.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to sugarsync (Sugarsync).

 Leave blank to use rclone's.

<dt>&bull;

 Leave blank to use rclone's.

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_ACCESS_KEY_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-private-access-key</h3>Sugarsync Private Access Key 

 Leave blank to use rclone's.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: private_access_key
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_PRIVATE_ACCESS_KEY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-hard-delete</h3>Permanently delete files if true otherwise put them in the deleted files.

<dd>Config: hard_delete

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: bool
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: false</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to sugarsync (Sugarsync).
<h3>-sugarsync-refresh-token</h3>Sugarsync refresh token 

 Leave blank normally, will be auto configured by rclone.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: refresh_token
<dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-authorization</h3>Sugarsync authorization 

 Leave blank normally, will be auto configured by rclone.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: authorization
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_AUTHORIZATION
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-authorization-expiry</h3>Sugarsync authorization expiry 

 Leave blank normally, will be auto configured by rclone.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: authorization_expiry
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-user</h3>Sugarsync user 

 Leave blank normally, will be auto configured by rclone.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: user
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_USER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-root-id</h3>Sugarsync root id 

 Leave blank normally, will be auto configured by rclone.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: root_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_ROOT_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-deleted-id</h3>Sugarsync deleted folder id 

 Leave blank normally, will be auto configured by rclone.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: deleted_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_DELETED_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-sugarsync-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_SUGARSYNC_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,Ctl,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Tardigrade</h3>Tardigrade (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://tardigrade.io)">https://tardigrade.io)</a> is an encrypted, secure, and cost-effective object storage service that enables you to store, back up, and archive large amounts of data in a decentralized manner.
<h3>Setup</h3>To make a new Tardigrade configuration you need one of the following: * Access Grant that someone else shared with you. * API Key (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://documentation.tardigrade.io/getting-started/uploading-your-first-object/create-an-api-key)">https://documentation.tardigrade.io/getting-started/uploading-your-first-object/create-an-api-key)</a> of a Tardigrade project you are a member of. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<h3>Setup with access grant</h3><dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one

s) Set configuration password
q) Quit config

[snip]

y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl><h3>Usage</h3>Paths are specified as remote:bucket (or remote: for the lsf command.) You may put subdirectories in too, eg remote:bucket/path/to/dir. 

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this.
<h3>Create a new bucket</h3>Use the mkdir command to create new bucket, e.g. bucket.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:bucket</pre></dl><h3>List all buckets</h3>Use the lsf command to list all buckets.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsf remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Note the colon (:) character at the end of the command line.
<h3>Delete a bucket</h3>Use the rmdir command to delete an empty bucket.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone rmdir remote:bucket</pre></dl>
 

 Use the purge command to delete a non-empty bucket with all its content.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone purge remote:bucket</pre></dl><h3>Upload objects</h3>Use the copy command to upload an object.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy --progress /home/local/directory/file.ext remote:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl>
 

 The --progress flag is for displaying progress information. Remove it if you don't need this information. 

 Use a folder in the local path to upload all its objects.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy --progress /home/local/directory/ remote:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl>
 

 Only modified files will be copied.
<h3>List objects</h3>Use the ls command to list recursively all objects in a bucket.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:bucket</pre></dl>
 

 Add the folder to the remote path to list recursively all objects in this folder.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl>
 

 Use the lsf command to list non-recursively all objects in a bucket or a folder.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsf remote:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl><h3>Download objects</h3>Use the copy command to download an object.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy --progress remote:bucket/path/to/dir/file.ext /home/local/directory/</pre></dl>
 

 The --progress flag is for displaying progress information. Remove it if you don't need this information. 

 Use a folder in the remote path to download all its objects.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy --progress remote:bucket/path/to/dir/ /home/local/directory/</pre></dl><h3>Delete objects</h3>Use the deletefile command to delete a single object.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone deletefile remote:bucket/path/to/dir/file.ext</pre></dl>
 

 Use the delete command to delete all object in a folder.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone delete remote:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl><h3>Print the total size of objects</h3>Use the size command to print the total size of objects in a bucket or a folder.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone size remote:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl><h3>Sync two Locations</h3>Use the sync command to sync the source to the destination, changing the destination only, deleting any excess files.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i --progress /home/local/directory/ remote:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl>
 

 The --progress flag is for displaying progress information. Remove it if you don't need this information. 

 Since this can cause data loss, test first with the --dry-run flag to see exactly what would be copied and deleted. 

 The sync can be done also from Tardigrade to the local file system.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i --progress remote:bucket/path/to/dir/ /home/local/directory/</pre></dl>
 

 Or between two Tardigrade buckets.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i --progress remote-us:bucket/path/to/dir/ remote-europe:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl>
 

 Or even between another cloud storage and Tardigrade.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i --progress s3:bucket/path/to/dir/ tardigrade:bucket/path/to/dir/</pre></dl><h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to tardigrade (Tardigrade Decentralized Cloud Storage).
<h3>-tardigrade-provider</h3>Choose an authentication method.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: provider
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_TARDIGRADE_PROVIDER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "existing"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"existing"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use an existing access grant.</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"new"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Create a new access grant from satellite address, API key, and passphrase.</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-tardigrade-access-grant</h3>Access Grant.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: access_grant
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_TARDIGRADE_ACCESS_GRANT
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-tardigrade-satellite-address</h3>Satellite Address. Custom satellite address should match the format: &lt;nodeid&gt;@&lt;address&gt;:&lt;port&gt;.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: satellite_address
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_TARDIGRADE_SATELLITE_ADDRESS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "us-central-1.tardigrade.io"
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"us-central-1.tardigrade.io"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>US Central 1</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"europe-west-1.tardigrade.io"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Europe West 1</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"asia-east-1.tardigrade.io"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Asia East 1</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-tardigrade-api-key</h3>API Key.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: api_key
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_TARDIGRADE_API_KEY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-tardigrade-passphrase</h3>Encryption Passphrase. To access existing objects enter passphrase used for uploading.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: passphrase
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_TARDIGRADE_PASSPHRASE
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Union</h3>The union remote provides a unification similar to UnionFS using other remotes. 

 Paths may be as deep as required or a local path, eg remote:directory/subdirectory or /directory/subdirectory. 

 During the initial setup with rclone config you will specify the upstream remotes as a space separated list. The upstream remotes can either be a local paths or other remotes. 

 Attribute :ro and :nc can be attach to the end of path to tag the remote as read only or no create, eg remote:directory/subdirectory:ro or remote:directory/subdirectory:nc. 

 Subfolders can be used in upstream remotes. Assume a union remote named backup with the remotes mydrive:private/backup. Invoking rclone mkdir backup:desktop is exactly the same as invoking rclone mkdir mydrive2:/backup/desktop. 

 There will be no special handling of paths containing .. segments. Invoking rclone mkdir backup:../desktop is exactly the same as invoking rclone mkdir mydrive2:/backup/../desktop.
<h3>Behavior / Policies</h3>The behavior of union backend is inspired by trapexit/mergerfs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/trapexit/mergerfs">https://github.com/trapexit/mergerfs</a>). All functions are grouped into 3 categories: action, create and search. These functions and categories can be assigned a policy which dictates what file or directory is chosen when performing that behavior. Any policy can be assigned to a function or category though some may not be very useful in practice. For instance: rand (random) may be useful for file creation (create) but could lead to very odd behavior if used for delete if there were more than one copy of the file.
<h3>Function / Category classifications</h3><table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Category </td><td> Description </td><td> Functions 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> action </td><td> Writing Existing file </td><td> move, rmdir, rmdirs, delete, purge and copy, sync (as destination when file exist) 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> create </td><td> Create non-existing file </td><td> copy, sync (as destination when file not exist) 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> search </td><td> Reading and listing file </td><td> ls, lsd, lsl, cat, md5sum, sha1sum and copy, sync (as source) 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> N/A </td><td> </td><td> size, about 
</td></tr> </table><h3>Path Preservation</h3>Policies, as described below, are of two basic types. path preserving and non-path preserving. 

 All policies which start with ep (epff, eplfs, eplus, epmfs, eprand) are path preserving. ep stands for existing path. 

 A path preserving policy will only consider upstreams where the relative path being accessed already exists. 

 When using non-path preserving policies paths will be created in target upstreams as necessary.
<h3>Quota Relevant Policies</h3>Some policies rely on quota information. These policies should be used only if your upstreams support the respective quota fields. 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Policy </td><td> Required Field 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=2><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> lfs, eplfs </td><td> Free 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> mfs, epmfs </td><td> Free 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> lus, eplus </td><td> Used 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> lno, eplno </td><td> Objects 
</td></tr> </table> 

 To check if your upstream supports the field, run rclone about remote: [flags] and see if the required field exists.
<h3>Filters</h3>Policies basically search upstream remotes and create a list of files / paths for functions to work on. The policy is responsible for filtering and sorting. The policy type defines the sorting but filtering is mostly uniform as described below.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>No search policies filter.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>All action policies will filter out remotes which are tagged as read-only.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>All create policies will filter out remotes which are tagged read-only or no-create.</dl>
 

 If all remotes are filtered an error will be returned.
<h3>Policy descriptions</h3>The policies definition are inspired by trapexit/mergerfs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/trapexit/mergerfs)">https://github.com/trapexit/mergerfs)</a> but not exactly the same. Some policy definition could be different due to the much larger latency of remote file systems. 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Policy </td><td> Description 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=2><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> all </td><td> Search category: same as epall. Action category: same as epall. Create category: act on all upstreams. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> epall (existing path, all) </td><td> Search category: Given this order configured, act on the first one found where the relative path exists. Action category: apply to all found. Create category: act on all upstreams where the relative path exists. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> epff (existing path, first found) </td><td> Act on the first one found, by the time upstreams reply, where the relative path exists. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> eplfs (existing path, least free space) </td><td> Of all the upstreams on which the relative path exists choose the one with the least free space. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> eplus (existing path, least used space) </td><td> Of all the upstreams on which the relative path exists choose the one with the least used space. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> eplno (existing path, least number of objects) </td><td> Of all the upstreams on which the relative path exists choose the one with the least number of objects. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> epmfs (existing path, most free space) </td><td> Of all the upstreams on which the relative path exists choose the one with the most free space. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> eprand (existing path, random) </td><td> Calls epall and then randomizes. Returns only one upstream. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> ff (first found) </td><td> Search category: same as epff. Action category: same as epff. Create category: Act on the first one found by the time upstreams reply. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> lfs (least free space) </td><td> Search category: same as eplfs. Action category: same as eplfs. Create category: Pick the upstream with the least available free space. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> lus (least used space) </td><td> Search category: same as eplus. Action category: same as eplus. Create category: Pick the upstream with the least used space. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> lno (least number of objects) </td><td> Search category: same as eplno. Action category: same as eplno. Create category: Pick the upstream with the least number of objects. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> mfs (most free space) </td><td> Search category: same as epmfs. Action category: same as epmfs. Create category: Pick the upstream with the most available free space. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> newest </td><td> Pick the file / directory with the largest mtime. 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> rand (random) </td><td> Calls all and then randomizes. Returns only one upstream. 
</td></tr> </table><h3>Setup</h3>Here is an example of how to make a union called remote for local folders. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one

q) Quit config

List of space separated upstreams.
Can be 'upstreama:test/dir upstreamb:', '\&quot;upstreama:test/space:ro dir\&quot; upstreamb:', etc.

Current remotes:
Name Type

remote union
e) Edit existing remote

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 List directories in top level in C:\dir1, C:\dir2 and C:\dir3
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 List all the files in C:\dir1, C:\dir2 and C:\dir3
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Copy another local directory to the union directory called source, which will be placed into C:\dir3
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy C:\source remote:source</pre></dl><h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to union (Union merges the contents of several upstream fs).
<h3>-union-upstreams</h3>List of space separated upstreams. Can be `upstreama:test/dir upstreamb:', `"upstreama:test/space:ro dir" upstreamb:', etc.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: upstreams
<dt>&bull;

<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-union-action-policy</h3>Policy to choose upstream on ACTION category.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: action_policy
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_UNION_ACTION_POLICY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "epall"</dl><h3>-union-create-policy</h3>Policy to choose upstream on CREATE category.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: create_policy
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_UNION_CREATE_POLICY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "epmfs"</dl><h3>-union-search-policy</h3>Policy to choose upstream on SEARCH category.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: search_policy
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_UNION_SEARCH_POLICY
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: "ff"</dl><h3>-union-cache-time</h3>Cache time of usage and free space (in seconds). This option is only useful when a path preserving policy is used.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: cache_time
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_UNION_CACHE_TIME
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: int
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: 120</dl><h3>WebDAV</h3>Paths are specified as remote:path 

 Paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory. 

 To configure the WebDAV remote you will need to have a URL for it, and a username and password. If you know what kind of system you are connecting to then rclone can enable extra features. 

 Here is an example of how to make a remote called remote. First run:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre> rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 List directories in top level of your WebDAV

<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:</pre></dl>
 

 To copy a local directory to an WebDAV directory called backup
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone copy /home/source remote:backup</pre></dl><h3>Modified time and hashes</h3>Plain WebDAV does not support modified times. However when used with Owncloud or Nextcloud rclone will support modified times. 

 Likewise plain WebDAV does not support hashes, however when used with Owncloud or Nextcloud rclone will support SHA1 and MD5 hashes. Depending on the exact version of Owncloud or Nextcloud hashes may appear on all objects, or only on objects which had a hash uploaded with them.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to webdav (Webdav).
<h3>-webdav-url</h3>URL of http host to connect to
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_WEBDAV_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://example.com">https://example.com</a>"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Connect to example.com</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-webdav-vendor</h3>Name of the Webdav site/service/software you are using
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: vendor
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_WEBDAV_VENDOR
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>"nextcloud"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Nextcloud</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"owncloud"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Owncloud</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"sharepoint"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Sharepoint</dl></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>"other"
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Other site/service or software</dl></dl>
</dl></dl>
</dl><h3>-webdav-user</h3>User name
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: user
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_WEBDAV_USER
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-webdav-pass</h3>Password. 

 NB Input to this must be obscured - see rclone obscure (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/">https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/</a>).
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: pass
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_WEBDAV_PASS
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-webdav-bearer-token</h3>Bearer token instead of user/pass (eg a Macaroon)
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: bearer_token
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_WEBDAV_BEARER_TOKEN
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to webdav (Webdav).
<h3>-webdav-bearer-token-command</h3>Command to run to get a bearer token
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: bearer_token_command
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_WEBDAV_BEARER_TOKEN_COMMAND
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Provider notes</h3>See below for notes on specific providers.
<h3>Owncloud</h3>Click on the settings cog in the bottom right of the page and this will show the WebDAV URL that rclone needs in the config step. It will look something like <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://example.com/remote.php/webdav/.">https://example.com/remote.php/webdav/.</a> 

 Owncloud supports modified times using the X-OC-Mtime header.
<h3>Nextcloud</h3>This is configured in an identical way to Owncloud. Note that Nextcloud does not support streaming of files (rcat) whereas Owncloud does. This may be fixed (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/nextcloud/nextcloud-snap/issues/365)">https://github.com/nextcloud/nextcloud-snap/issues/365)</a> in the future.
<h3>Sharepoint</h3>Rclone can be used with Sharepoint provided by OneDrive for Business or Office365 Education Accounts. This feature is only needed for a few of these Accounts, mostly Office365 Education ones. These accounts are sometimes not verified by the domain owner github#1975 (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/1975)">https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/1975)</a> 

 This means that these accounts can't be added using the official API (other Accounts should work with the "onedrive" option). However, it is possible to access them using webdav. 

 To use a sharepoint remote with rclone, add it like this: First, you need to get your remote's URL:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Go here (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://onedrive.live.com/about/en-us/signin/)">https://onedrive.live.com/about/en-us/signin/)</a> to open your OneDrive or to sign in
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Now take a look at your address bar, the URL should look like this: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://[YOUR-DOMAIN]-my.sharepoint.com/personal/[YOUR-EMAIL]/_layouts/15/onedrive.aspx">https://[YOUR-DOMAIN]-my.sharepoint.com/personal/[YOUR-EMAIL]/_layouts/15/onedrive.aspx</a></dl>
 

 You'll only need this URL up to the email address. After that, you'll most likely want to add "/Documents". That subdirectory contains the actual data stored on your OneDrive. 

 Add the remote to rclone like this: Configure the url as <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://[YOUR-DOMAIN]-my.sharepoint.com/personal/[YOUR-EMAIL]/Documents">https://[YOUR-DOMAIN]-my.sharepoint.com/personal/[YOUR-EMAIL]/Documents</a> and use your normal account email and password for user and pass. If you have 2FA enabled, you have to generate an app password. Set the vendor to sharepoint. 

 Your config file should look like this:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>[sharepoint]
type = webdav
url = <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://[YOUR-DOMAIN]-my.sharepoint.com/personal/[YOUR-EMAIL]/Documents">https://[YOUR-DOMAIN]-my.sharepoint.com/personal/[YOUR-EMAIL]/Documents</a>
vendor = other
user = YourEmailAddress
pass = encryptedpassword</pre></dl><h3>Required Flags for SharePoint</h3>As SharePoint does some special things with uploaded documents, you won't be able to use the documents size or the documents hash to compare if a file has been changed since the upload / which file is newer. 

 For Rclone calls copying files (especially Office files such as .docx, .xlsx, etc.) from/to SharePoint (like copy, sync, etc.), you should append these flags to ensure Rclone uses the "Last Modified" datetime property to compare your documents:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>--ignore-size --ignore-checksum --update</pre></dl><h3>dCache</h3>dCache is a storage system that supports many protocols and authentication/authorisation schemes. For WebDAV clients, it allows users to authenticate with username and password (BASIC), X.509, Kerberos, and various bearer tokens, including Macaroons (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.dcache.org/manuals/workshop-2017-05-29-Umea/000-Final/anupam_macaroons_v02.pdf)">https://www.dcache.org/manuals/workshop-2017-05-29-Umea/000-Final/anupam_macaroons_v02.pdf)</a> and OpenID-Connect (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenID_Connect)">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenID_Connect)</a> access tokens. 

 Configure as normal using the other type. Don't enter a username or password, instead enter your Macaroon as the bearer_token. 

 The config will end up looking something like this.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>[dcache]
type = webdav
url = <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://dcache...">https://dcache...</a>
vendor = other
user =
pass =
bearer_token = your-macaroon</pre></dl>
 

 There is a script (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/sara-nl/GridScripts/blob/master/get-macaroon)">https://github.com/sara-nl/GridScripts/blob/master/get-macaroon)</a> that obtains a Macaroon from a dCache WebDAV endpoint, and creates an rclone config file. 

 Macaroons may also be obtained from the dCacheView web-browser/JavaScript client that comes with dCache.
<h3>OpenID-Connect</h3>dCache also supports authenticating with OpenID-Connect access tokens. OpenID-Connect is a protocol (based on OAuth 2.0) that allows services to identify users who have authenticated with some central service. 

 Support for OpenID-Connect in rclone is currently achieved using another software package called oidc-agent (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/indigo-dc/oidc-agent">https://github.com/indigo-dc/oidc-agent</a>). This is a command-line tool that facilitates obtaining an access token. Once installed and configured, an access token is obtained by running the oidc-token command. The following example shows a (shortened) access token obtained from the XDC OIDC Provider.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>paul [at] celebrimbor:~$ oidc-token XDC
eyJraWQ[...]QFXDt0
paul [at] celebrimbor:~$</pre></dl>
 

 Note Before the oidc-token command will work, the refresh token must be loaded into the oidc agent. This is done with the oidc-add command (e.g., oidc-add XDC). This is typically done once per login session. Full details on this and how to register oidc-agent with your OIDC Provider are provided in the oidc-agent documentation (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://indigo-dc.gitbooks.io/oidc-agent/">https://indigo-dc.gitbooks.io/oidc-agent/</a>). 

 The rclone bearer_token_command configuration option is used to fetch the access token from oidc-agent. 

 Configure as a normal WebDAV endpoint, using the `other' vendor, leaving the username and password empty. When prompted, choose to edit the advanced config and enter the command to get a bearer token (e.g., oidc-agent XDC). 

 The following example config shows a WebDAV endpoint that uses oidc-agent to supply an access token from the XDC OIDC Provider.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>[dcache]
type = webdav
url = <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://dcache.example.org/">https://dcache.example.org/</a>
vendor = other
bearer_token_command = oidc-token XDC</pre></dl><h3>Yandex Disk</h3>Yandex Disk (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://disk.yandex.com)">https://disk.yandex.com)</a> is a cloud storage solution created by Yandex (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://yandex.com">https://yandex.com</a>). 

 Here is an example of making a yandex configuration. First run
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone config</pre></dl>
 

 This will guide you through an interactive setup process:
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>No remotes found - make a new one
n) New remote
s) Set configuration password
n/s&gt; n
name&gt; remote
Type of storage to configure.
Choose a number from below, or type in your own value
[snip]
XX / Yandex Disk
 \ &quot;yandex&quot;
[snip]
Storage&gt; yandex
Yandex Client Id - leave blank normally.
client_id&gt;
Yandex Client Secret - leave blank normally.
client_secret&gt;
Remote config
Use auto config?
 * Say Y if not sure
 * Say N if you are working on a remote or headless machine
y) Yes
n) No
y/n&gt; y
If your browser doesn't open automatically go to the following link: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth">http://127.0.0.1:53682/auth</a>
Log in and authorize rclone for access
Waiting for code...
Got code
--------------------
[remote]
client_id =
client_secret =
token = {&quot;access_token&quot;:&quot;xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx&quot;,&quot;token_type&quot;:&quot;bearer&quot;,&quot;expiry&quot;:&quot;2016-12-29T12:27:11.362788025Z&quot;}
--------------------
y) Yes this is OK
e) Edit this remote
d) Delete this remote
y/e/d&gt; y</pre></dl>
 

 See the remote setup docs (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)">https://rclone.org/remote_setup/)</a> for how to set it up on a machine with no Internet browser available. 

 Note that rclone runs a webserver on your local machine to collect the token as returned from Yandex Disk. This only runs from the moment it opens your browser to the moment you get back the verification code. This is on <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://127.0.0.1:53682/">http://127.0.0.1:53682/</a> and this it may require you to unblock it temporarily if you are running a host firewall. 

 Once configured you can then use rclone like this, 

 See top level directories
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone lsd remote:</pre></dl>
 

 Make a new directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone mkdir remote:directory</pre></dl>
 

 List the contents of a directory
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone ls remote:directory</pre></dl>
 

 Sync /home/local/directory to the remote path, deleting any excess files in the path.
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/local/directory remote:directory</pre></dl>
 

 Yandex paths may be as deep as required, eg remote:directory/subdirectory.
<h3>Modified time</h3>Modified times are supported and are stored accurate to 1 ns in custom metadata called rclone_modified in RFC3339 with nanoseconds format.
<h3>MD5 checksums</h3>MD5 checksums are natively supported by Yandex Disk.
<h3>Emptying Trash</h3>If you wish to empty your trash you can use the rclone cleanup remote: command which will permanently delete all your trashed files. This command does not take any path arguments.
<h3>Quota information</h3>To view your current quota you can use the rclone about remote: command which will display your usage limit (quota) and the current usage.
<h3>Restricted filename characters</h3>The default restricted characters set (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)">https://rclone.org/overview/#restricted-characters)</a> are replaced. 

 Invalid UTF-8 bytes will also be replaced (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8">https://rclone.org/overview/#invalid-utf8</a>), as they can't be used in JSON strings.
<h3>Limitations</h3>When uploading very large files (bigger than about 5GB) you will need to increase the --timeout parameter. This is because Yandex pauses (perhaps to calculate the MD5SUM for the entire file) before returning confirmation that the file has been uploaded. The default handling of timeouts in rclone is to assume a 5 minute pause is an error and close the connection - you'll see net/http: timeout awaiting response headers errors in the logs if this is happening. Setting the timeout to twice the max size of file in GB should be enough, so if you want to upload a 30GB file set a timeout of 2 * 30 = 60m, that is --timeout 60m.
<h3>Standard Options</h3>Here are the standard options specific to yandex (Yandex Disk).
<h3>-yandex-client-id</h3>OAuth Client Id Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_id
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_YANDEX_CLIENT_ID
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-yandex-client-secret</h3>OAuth Client Secret Leave blank normally.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: client_secret
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_YANDEX_CLIENT_SECRET
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>Advanced Options</h3>Here are the advanced options specific to yandex (Yandex Disk).
<h3>-yandex-token</h3>OAuth Access Token as a JSON blob.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_YANDEX_TOKEN
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-yandex-auth-url</h3>Auth server URL. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: auth_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_YANDEX_AUTH_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-yandex-token-url</h3>Token server url. Leave blank to use the provider defaults.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: token_url
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_YANDEX_TOKEN_URL
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: string
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: &quot;&quot;</dl><h3>-yandex-encoding</h3>This sets the encoding for the backend. 

 See: the encoding section in the overview (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)">https://rclone.org/overview/#encoding)</a> for more info.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Config: encoding
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Env Var: RCLONE_YANDEX_ENCODING
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Type: MultiEncoder
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Default: Slash,Del,Ctl,InvalidUtf8,Dot</dl><h3>Local Filesystem</h3>Local paths are specified as normal filesystem paths, eg /path/to/wherever, so
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>rclone sync -i /home/source /tmp/destination</pre></dl>
 

 Will sync /home/source to /tmp/destination 

 These can be configured into the config file for consistencies sake, but it is probably easier not to.
<h3>Modified time</h3>Rclone reads and writes the modified time using an accuracy determined by the OS. Typically this is 1ns on Linux, 10 ns on Windows and 1 Second on OS X.
<h3>Filenames</h3>Filenames should be encoded in UTF-8 on disk. This is the normal case for Windows and OS X. 

 There is a bit more uncertainty in the Linux world, but new distributions will have UTF-8 encoded files names. If you are using an old Linux filesystem with non UTF-8 file names (eg latin1) then you can use the convmv tool to convert the filesystem to UTF-8. This tool is available in most distributions' package managers. 

 If an invalid (non-UTF8) filename is read, the invalid characters will be replaced with a quoted representation of the invalid bytes. The name gro\xdf will be transferred as gro1BDF. rclone will emit a debug message in this case (use -v to see), eg
<dl COMPACT><dd><pre>Local file system at .: Replacing invalid UTF-8 characters in &quot;gro\xdf&quot;</pre></dl><h3>Restricted characters</h3>On non Windows platforms the following characters are replaced when handling file names. 

 <table> <tr VALIGN=top><td> Character </td><td ALIGN=center> Value </td><td ALIGN=center> Replacement 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td COLSPAN=3><hr></td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> NUL </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x00 </td><td ALIGN=center> 00 
</td></tr><tr VALIGN=top><td> / </td><td ALIGN=center> 0x2F </td><td ALIGN=center> 0F 
</td></tr> </table> 

 When running on Windows the following characters are replaced. This list is based on the Windows file naming conventions (<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://docs.microsoft.com/de-de/windows/desktop/FileIO/naming-a-file#naming-conventions">https://docs.microsoft.com/de-de/windows/desktop/FileIO/naming-a-file#naming-conventions</a>).
